title: Paradise Lost
author: milton
attributionNote: Recorded in the Christian Classics Ethereal Library under John Milton (1608-1674). The site catalogues the work at https://ccel.org/ccel/milton/paradiselost, whose own card names the print edition transcribed here; where the site carries a title by a publisher's permission rather than in public domain, this library does not take it.
description: Paradise Lost — the English text the Christian Classics Ethereal Library publishes for this work. The record was created by the CCEL import from the site's own catalogue and plain text; an editor's note for the work itself is still to be written.
historicalContext: Read in the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's catalogue, whose shelves follow the site's own division of Christian literature.
availabilityNote: Complete in the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's plain-text edition: 11 chapter(s), 10553 paragraph(s), 79,864 words. The divisions are the headings of the site's own text, which the library stores rather than asking the site for again when the work is read. The text is public domain and is displayed with the library's credit.

texts.1.4: Of Mans First Disobedience, and the Fruit
texts.1.5: Of that Forbidden Tree, whose mortal tast
texts.1.6: Brought Death into the World, and all our woe,
texts.1.7: With loss of EDEN, till one greater Man
texts.1.8: Restore us, and regain the blissful Seat,
texts.1.9: Sing Heav'nly Muse, that on the secret top
texts.1.10: Of OREB, or of SINAI, didst inspire
texts.1.11: That Shepherd, who first taught the chosen Seed,
texts.1.12: In the Beginning how the Heav'ns and Earth
texts.1.13: Rose out of CHAOS: Or if SION Hill
texts.1.14: Delight thee more, and SILOA'S Brook that flow'd
texts.1.15: Fast by the Oracle of God; I thence
texts.1.16: Invoke thy aid to my adventrous Song,
texts.1.17: That with no middle flight intends to soar
texts.1.18: Above th' AONIAN Mount, while it pursues
texts.1.19: Things unattempted yet in Prose or Rhime.
texts.1.20: And chiefly Thou O Spirit, that dost prefer
texts.1.21: Before all Temples th' upright heart and pure,
texts.1.22: Instruct me, for Thou know'st; Thou from the first
texts.1.23: Wast present, and with mighty wings outspread
texts.1.24: Dove-like satst brooding on the vast Abyss
texts.1.25: And mad'st it pregnant: What in me is dark
texts.1.26: Illumine, what is low raise and support;
texts.1.27: That to the highth of this great Argument
texts.1.28: I may assert th' Eternal Providence,
texts.1.29: And justifie the wayes of God to men.
texts.1.30: Say first, for Heav'n hides nothing from thy view
texts.1.31: Nor the deep Tract of Hell, say first what cause
texts.1.32: Mov'd our Grand Parents in that happy State,
texts.1.33: Favour'd of Heav'n so highly, to fall off
texts.1.34: From their Creator, and transgress his Will
texts.1.35: For one restraint, Lords of the World besides?
texts.1.36: Who first seduc'd them to that fowl revolt?
texts.1.37: Th' infernal Serpent; he it was, whose guile
texts.1.38: Stird up with Envy and Revenge, deceiv'd
texts.1.39: The Mother of Mankinde, what time his Pride
texts.1.40: Had cast him out from Heav'n, with all his Host
texts.1.41: Of Rebel Angels, by whose aid aspiring
texts.1.42: To set himself in Glory above his Peers,
texts.1.43: He trusted to have equal'd the most High,
texts.1.44: If he oppos'd; and with ambitious aim
texts.1.45: Against the Throne and Monarchy of God
texts.1.46: Rais'd impious War in Heav'n and Battel proud
texts.1.47: With vain attempt. Him the Almighty Power
texts.1.48: Hurld headlong flaming from th' Ethereal Skie
texts.1.49: With hideous ruine and combustion down
texts.1.50: To bottomless perdition, there to dwell
texts.1.51: In Adamantine Chains and penal Fire,
texts.1.52: Who durst defie th' Omnipotent to Arms.
texts.1.53: Nine times the Space that measures Day and Night
texts.1.54: To mortal men, he with his horrid crew
texts.1.55: Lay vanquisht, rowling in the fiery Gulfe
texts.1.56: Confounded though immortal: But his doom
texts.1.57: Reserv'd him to more wrath; for now the thought
texts.1.58: Both of lost happiness and lasting pain
texts.1.59: Torments him; round he throws his baleful eyes
texts.1.60: That witness'd huge affliction and dismay
texts.1.61: Mixt with obdurate pride and stedfast hate:
texts.1.62: At once as far as Angels kenn he views
texts.1.63: The dismal Situation waste and wilde,
texts.1.64: A Dungeon horrible, on all sides round
texts.1.65: As one great Furnace flam'd, yet from those flames
texts.1.66: No light, but rather darkness visible
texts.1.67: Serv'd only to discover sights of woe,
texts.1.68: Regions of sorrow, doleful shades, where peace
texts.1.69: And rest can never dwell, hope never comes
texts.1.70: That comes to all; but torture without end
texts.1.71: Still urges, and a fiery Deluge, fed
texts.1.73: Such place Eternal Justice had prepar'd
texts.1.74: For those rebellious, here their Prison ordain'd
texts.1.75: In utter darkness, and their portion set
texts.1.76: As far remov'd from God and light of Heav'n
texts.1.77: As from the Center thrice to th' utmost Pole.
texts.1.78: O how unlike the place from whence they fell!
texts.1.79: There the companions of his fall, o'rewhelm'd
texts.1.80: With Floods and Whirlwinds of tempestuous fire,
texts.1.81: He soon discerns, and weltring by his side
texts.1.82: One next himself in power, and next in crime,
texts.1.83: Long after known in PALESTINE, and nam'd
texts.1.85: And thence in Heav'n call'd Satan, with bold words
texts.1.86: Breaking the horrid silence thus began.
texts.1.87: If thou beest he; But O how fall'n! how chang'd
texts.1.88: From him, who in the happy Realms of Light
texts.1.89: Cloth'd with transcendent brightnes didst outshine
texts.1.90: Myriads though bright: If he whom mutual league,
texts.1.91: United thoughts and counsels, equal hope,
texts.1.92: And hazard in the Glorious Enterprize,
texts.1.93: Joynd with me once, now misery hath joynd
texts.1.94: In equal ruin: into what Pit thou seest
texts.1.95: From what highth fal'n, so much the stronger provd
texts.1.96: He with his Thunder: and till then who knew
texts.1.97: The force of those dire Arms? yet not for those
texts.1.98: Nor what the Potent Victor in his rage
texts.1.99: Can else inflict do I repent or change,
texts.1.100: Though chang'd in outward lustre; that fixt mind
texts.1.101: And high disdain, from sence of injur'd merit,
texts.1.102: That with the mightiest rais'd me to contend,
texts.1.103: And to the fierce contention brought along
texts.1.105: That durst dislike his reign, and me preferring,
texts.1.106: His utmost power with adverse power oppos'd
texts.1.107: In dubious Battel on the Plains of Heav'n,
texts.1.108: And shook his throne. What though the field be lost?
texts.1.109: All is not lost; the unconquerable Will,
texts.1.110: And study of revenge, immortal hate,
texts.1.111: And courage never to submit or yield:
texts.1.112: And what is else not to be overcome?
texts.1.113: That Glory never shall his wrath or might
texts.1.114: Extort from me. To bow and sue for grace
texts.1.115: With suppliant knee, and deifie his power
texts.1.116: Who from the terrour of this Arm so late
texts.1.117: Doubted his Empire, that were low indeed,
texts.1.118: That were an ignominy and shame beneath
texts.1.119: This downfall; since by Fate the strength of Gods
texts.1.120: And this Empyreal substance cannot fail,
texts.1.121: Since through experience of this great event
texts.1.122: In Arms not worse, in foresight much advanc't,
texts.1.123: We may with more successful hope resolve
texts.1.124: To wage by force or guile eternal Warr
texts.1.126: Who now triumphs, and in th' excess of joy
texts.1.127: Sole reigning holds the Tyranny of Heav'n.
texts.1.128: So spake th' Apostate Angel, though in pain,
texts.1.129: Vaunting aloud, but rackt with deep despare:
texts.1.130: And him thus answer'd soon his bold Compeer.
texts.1.131: O Prince, O Chief of many Throned Powers,
texts.1.132: That led th' imbattelld Seraphim to Warr
texts.1.133: Under thy conduct, and in dreadful deeds
texts.1.135: And put to proof his high Supremacy,
texts.1.136: Whether upheld by strength, or Chance, or Fate,
texts.1.137: Too well I see and rue the dire event,
texts.1.138: That with sad overthrow and foul defeat
texts.1.139: Hath lost us Heav'n, and all this mighty Host
texts.1.140: In horrible destruction laid thus low,
texts.1.141: As far as Gods and Heav'nly Essences
texts.1.142: Can Perish: for the mind and spirit remains
texts.1.144: Though all our Glory extinct, and happy state
texts.1.145: Here swallow'd up in endless misery.
texts.1.146: But what if he our Conquerour, (whom I now
texts.1.147: Of force believe Almighty, since no less
texts.1.148: Then such could hav orepow'rd such force as ours)
texts.1.149: Have left us this our spirit and strength intire
texts.1.150: Strongly to suffer and support our pains,
texts.1.151: That we may so suffice his vengeful ire,
texts.1.152: Or do him mightier service as his thralls
texts.1.153: By right of Warr, what e're his business be
texts.1.154: Here in the heart of Hell to work in Fire,
texts.1.155: Or do his Errands in the gloomy Deep;
texts.1.156: What can it then avail though yet we feel
texts.1.159: Whereto with speedy words th' Arch-fiend reply'd.
texts.1.160: Fall'n Cherube, to be weak is miserable
texts.1.161: Doing or Suffering: but of this be sure,
texts.1.162: To do ought good never will be our task,
texts.1.163: But ever to do ill our sole delight,
texts.1.164: As being the contrary to his high will
texts.1.165: Whom we resist. If then his Providence
texts.1.166: Out of our evil seek to bring forth good,
texts.1.167: Our labour must be to pervert that end,
texts.1.168: And out of good still to find means of evil;
texts.1.169: Which oft times may succeed, so as perhaps
texts.1.170: Shall grieve him, if I fail not, and disturb
texts.1.171: His inmost counsels from their destind aim.
texts.1.172: But see the angry Victor hath recall'd
texts.1.173: His Ministers of vengeance and pursuit
texts.1.174: Back to the Gates of Heav'n: The Sulphurous Hail
texts.1.175: Shot after us in storm, oreblown hath laid
texts.1.176: The fiery Surge, that from the Precipice
texts.1.177: Of Heav'n receiv'd us falling, and the Thunder,
texts.1.178: Wing'd with red Lightning and impetuous rage,
texts.1.179: Perhaps hath spent his shafts, and ceases now
texts.1.180: To bellow through the vast and boundless Deep.
texts.1.181: Let us not slip th' occasion, whether scorn,
texts.1.182: Or satiate fury yield it from our Foe.
texts.1.183: Seest thou yon dreary Plain, forlorn and wilde,
texts.1.184: The seat of desolation, voyd of light,
texts.1.185: Save what the glimmering of these livid flames
texts.1.186: Casts pale and dreadful? Thither let us tend
texts.1.187: From off the tossing of these fiery waves,
texts.1.188: There rest, if any rest can harbour there,
texts.1.190: Consult how we may henceforth most offend
texts.1.191: Our Enemy, our own loss how repair,
texts.1.193: What reinforcement we may gain from Hope,
texts.1.194: If not what resolution from despare.
texts.1.195: Thus Satan talking to his neerest Mate
texts.1.196: With Head up-lift above the wave, and Eyes
texts.1.197: That sparkling blaz'd, his other Parts besides
texts.1.198: Prone on the Flood, extended long and large
texts.1.199: Lay floating many a rood, in bulk as huge
texts.1.200: As whom the Fables name of monstrous size,
texts.1.201: TITANIAN, or EARTH-BORN, that warr'd on JOVE,
texts.1.202: BRIARIOS or TYPHON, whom the Den
texts.1.203: By ancient TARSUS held, or that Sea-beast
texts.1.204: LEVIATHAN, which God of all his works
texts.1.205: Created hugest that swim th' Ocean stream:
texts.1.206: Him haply slumbring on the NORWAY foam
texts.1.207: The Pilot of some small night-founder'd Skiff,
texts.1.208: Deeming some Island, oft, as Sea-men tell,
texts.1.209: With fixed Anchor in his skaly rind
texts.1.210: Moors by his side under the Lee, while Night
texts.1.211: Invests the Sea, and wished Morn delayes:
texts.1.212: So stretcht out huge in length the Arch-fiend lay
texts.1.213: Chain'd on the burning Lake, nor ever thence
texts.1.214: Had ris'n or heav'd his head, but that the will
texts.1.215: And high permission of all-ruling Heaven
texts.1.216: Left him at large to his own dark designs,
texts.1.217: That with reiterated crimes he might
texts.1.218: Heap on himself damnation, while he sought
texts.1.219: Evil to others, and enrag'd might see
texts.1.220: How all his malice serv'd but to bring forth
texts.1.221: Infinite goodness, grace and mercy shewn
texts.1.222: On Man by him seduc't, but on himself
texts.1.223: Treble confusion, wrath and vengeance pour'd.
texts.1.224: Forthwith upright he rears from off the Pool
texts.1.225: His mighty Stature; on each hand the flames
texts.1.226: Drivn backward slope their pointing spires, rowld
texts.1.227: In billows, leave i'th' midst a horrid Vale.
texts.1.228: Then with expanded wings he stears his flight
texts.1.229: Aloft, incumbent on the dusky Air
texts.1.230: That felt unusual weight, till on dry Land
texts.1.231: He lights, if it were Land that ever burn'd
texts.1.232: With solid, as the Lake with liquid fire;
texts.1.233: And such appear'd in hue, as when the force
texts.1.234: Of subterranean wind transports a Hill
texts.1.235: Torn from PELORUS, or the shatter'd side
texts.1.237: And fewel'd entrals thence conceiving Fire,
texts.1.238: Sublim'd with Mineral fury, aid the Winds,
texts.1.239: And leave a singed bottom all involv'd
texts.1.240: With stench and smoak: Such resting found the sole
texts.1.241: Of unblest feet. Him followed his next Mate,
texts.1.242: Both glorying to have scap't the STYGIAN flood
texts.1.243: As Gods, and by their own recover'd strength,
texts.1.244: Not by the sufferance of supernal Power.
texts.1.245: Is this the Region, this the Soil, the Clime,
texts.1.246: Said then the lost Arch Angel, this the seat
texts.1.247: That we must change for Heav'n, this mournful gloom
texts.1.248: For that celestial light? Be it so, since hee
texts.1.249: Who now is Sovran can dispose and bid
texts.1.250: What shall be right: fardest from him is best
texts.1.251: Whom reason hath equald, force hath made supream
texts.1.252: Above his equals. Farewel happy Fields
texts.1.253: Where Joy for ever dwells: Hail horrours, hail
texts.1.254: Infernal world, and thou profoundest Hell
texts.1.255: Receive thy new Possessor: One who brings
texts.1.256: A mind not to be chang'd by Place or Time.
texts.1.257: The mind is its own place, and in it self
texts.1.258: Can make a Heav'n of Hell, a Hell of Heav'n.
texts.1.259: What matter where, if I be still the same,
texts.1.260: And what I should be, all but less then hee
texts.1.261: Whom Thunder hath made greater? Here at least
texts.1.262: We shall be free; th' Almighty hath not built
texts.1.263: Here for his envy, will not drive us hence:
texts.1.264: Here we may reign secure, and in my choyce
texts.1.265: To reign is worth ambition though in Hell:
texts.1.266: Better to reign in Hell, then serve in Heav'n.
texts.1.267: But wherefore let we then our faithful friends,
texts.1.268: Th' associates and copartners of our loss
texts.1.269: Lye thus astonisht on th' oblivious Pool,
texts.1.270: And call them not to share with us their part
texts.1.271: In this unhappy Mansion, or once more
texts.1.272: With rallied Arms to try what may be yet
texts.1.273: Regaind in Heav'n, or what more lost in Hell?
texts.1.274: So SATAN spake, and him BEELZEBUB
texts.1.275: Thus answer'd. Leader of those Armies bright,
texts.1.276: Which but th' Omnipotent none could have foyld,
texts.1.277: If once they hear that voyce, their liveliest pledge
texts.1.278: Of hope in fears and dangers, heard so oft
texts.1.279: In worst extreams, and on the perilous edge
texts.1.280: Of battel when it rag'd, in all assaults
texts.1.281: Their surest signal, they will soon resume
texts.1.282: New courage and revive, though now they lye
texts.1.283: Groveling and prostrate on yon Lake of Fire,
texts.1.284: As we erewhile, astounded and amaz'd,
texts.1.285: No wonder, fall'n such a pernicious highth.
texts.1.286: He scarce had ceas't when the superiour Fiend
texts.1.287: Was moving toward the shore; his ponderous shield
texts.1.288: Ethereal temper, massy, large and round,
texts.1.289: Behind him cast; the broad circumference
texts.1.290: Hung on his shoulders like the Moon, whose Orb
texts.1.291: Through Optic Glass the TUSCAN Artist views
texts.1.292: At Ev'ning from the top of FESOLE,
texts.1.293: Or in VALDARNO, to descry new Lands,
texts.1.294: Rivers or Mountains in her spotty Globe.
texts.1.295: His Spear, to equal which the tallest Pine
texts.1.296: Hewn on NORWEGIAN hills, to be the Mast
texts.1.297: Of some great Ammiral, were but a wand,
texts.1.298: He walkt with to support uneasie steps
texts.1.299: Over the burning Marle, not like those steps
texts.1.300: On Heavens Azure, and the torrid Clime
texts.1.301: Smote on him sore besides, vaulted with Fire;
texts.1.302: Nathless he so endur'd, till on the Beach
texts.1.303: Of that inflamed Sea, he stood and call'd
texts.1.304: His Legions, Angel Forms, who lay intrans't
texts.1.305: Thick as Autumnal Leaves that strow the Brooks
texts.1.306: In VALLOMBROSA, where th' ETRURIAN shades
texts.1.307: High overarch't imbowr; or scatterd sedge
texts.1.308: Afloat, when with fierce Winds ORION arm'd
texts.1.309: Hath vext the Red-Sea Coast, whose waves orethrew
texts.1.311: VVhile with perfidious hatred they pursu'd
texts.1.312: The Sojourners of GOSHEN, who beheld
texts.1.313: From the safe shore their floating Carkases
texts.1.314: And broken Chariot Wheels, so thick bestrown
texts.1.315: Abject and lost lay these, covering the Flood,
texts.1.316: Under amazement of their hideous change.
texts.1.317: He call'd so loud, that all the hollow Deep
texts.1.319: Warriers, the Flowr of Heav'n, once yours, now lost,
texts.1.320: If such astonishment as this can sieze
texts.1.321: Eternal spirits; or have ye chos'n this place
texts.1.322: After the toyl of Battel to repose
texts.1.323: Your wearied vertue, for the ease you find
texts.1.324: To slumber here, as in the Vales of Heav'n?
texts.1.325: Or in this abject posture have ye sworn
texts.1.326: To adore the Conquerour? who now beholds
texts.1.327: Cherube and Seraph rowling in the Flood
texts.1.328: With scatter'd Arms and Ensigns, till anon
texts.1.329: His swift pursuers from Heav'n Gates discern
texts.1.330: Th' advantage, and descending tread us down
texts.1.331: Thus drooping, or with linked Thunderbolts
texts.1.332: Transfix us to the bottom of this Gulfe.
texts.1.333: Awake, arise, or be for ever fall'n.
texts.1.334: They heard, and were abasht, and up they sprung
texts.1.335: Upon the wing, as when men wont to watch
texts.1.336: On duty, sleeping found by whom they dread,
texts.1.337: Rouse and bestir themselves ere well awake.
texts.1.338: Nor did they not perceave the evil plight
texts.1.339: In which they were, or the fierce pains not feel;
texts.1.340: Yet to their Generals Voyce they soon obeyd
texts.1.341: Innumerable. As when the potent Rod
texts.1.342: Of AMRAMS Son in EGYPTS evill day
texts.1.343: Wav'd round the Coast, up call'd a pitchy cloud
texts.1.344: Of LOCUSTS, warping on the Eastern Wind,
texts.1.345: That ore the Realm of impious PHAROAH hung
texts.1.346: Like Night, and darken'd all the Land of NILE:
texts.1.347: So numberless were those bad Angels seen
texts.1.348: Hovering on wing under the Cope of Hell
texts.1.350: Till, as a signal giv'n, th' uplifted Spear
texts.1.351: Of their great Sultan waving to direct
texts.1.352: Thir course, in even ballance down they light
texts.1.353: On the firm brimstone, and fill all the Plain;
texts.1.354: A multitude, like which the populous North
texts.1.355: Pour'd never from her frozen loyns, to pass
texts.1.356: RHENE or the DANAW, when her barbarous Sons
texts.1.357: Came like a Deluge on the South, and spread
texts.1.358: Beneath GIBRALTAR to the LYBIAN sands.
texts.1.359: Forthwith from every Squadron and each Band
texts.1.360: The Heads and Leaders thither hast where stood
texts.1.361: Their great Commander; Godlike shapes and forms
texts.1.363: And Powers that earst in Heaven sat on Thrones;
texts.1.364: Though of their Names in heav'nly Records now
texts.1.365: Be no memorial, blotted out and ras'd
texts.1.366: By thir Rebellion, from the Books of Life.
texts.1.367: Nor had they yet among the Sons of EVE
texts.1.368: Got them new Names, till wandring ore the Earth,
texts.1.369: Through Gods high sufferance for the tryal of man,
texts.1.370: By falsities and lyes the greatest part
texts.1.371: Of Mankind they corrupted to forsake
texts.1.372: God their Creator, and th' invisible
texts.1.373: Glory of him, that made them, to transform
texts.1.374: Oft to the Image of a Brute, adorn'd
texts.1.375: With gay Religions full of Pomp and Gold,
texts.1.376: And Devils to adore for Deities:
texts.1.377: Then were they known to men by various Names,
texts.1.378: And various Idols through the Heathen World.
texts.1.379: Say, Muse, their Names then known, who first, who last,
texts.1.380: Rous'd from the slumber, on that fiery Couch,
texts.1.381: At thir great Emperors call, as next in worth
texts.1.382: Came singly where he stood on the bare strand,
texts.1.383: While the promiscuous croud stood yet aloof?
texts.1.384: The chief were those who from the Pit of Hell
texts.1.385: Roaming to seek their prey on earth, durst fix
texts.1.386: Their Seats long after next the Seat of God,
texts.1.387: Their Altars by his Altar, Gods ador'd
texts.1.388: Among the Nations round, and durst abide
texts.1.389: JEHOVAH thundring out of SION, thron'd
texts.1.390: Between the Cherubim; yea, often plac'd
texts.1.391: Within his Sanctuary it self their Shrines,
texts.1.393: His holy Rites, and solemn Feasts profan'd,
texts.1.394: And with their darkness durst affront his light.
texts.1.395: First MOLOCH, horrid King besmear'd with blood
texts.1.396: Of human sacrifice, and parents tears,
texts.1.397: Though for the noyse of Drums and Timbrels loud
texts.1.398: Their childrens cries unheard, that past through fire
texts.1.399: To his grim Idol. Him the AMMONITE
texts.1.400: Worshipt in RABBA and her watry Plain,
texts.1.401: In ARGOB and in BASAN, to the stream
texts.1.402: Of utmost ARNON. Nor content with such
texts.1.404: Of SOLOMON he led by fraud to build
texts.1.405: His Temple right against the Temple of God
texts.1.406: On that opprobrious Hill, and made his Grove
texts.1.407: The pleasant Vally of HINNOM, TOPHET thence
texts.1.408: And black GEHENNA call'd, the Type of Hell.
texts.1.409: Next CHEMOS, th' obscene dread of MOABS Sons,
texts.1.410: From AROER to NEBO, and the wild
texts.1.413: The flowry Dale of SIBMA clad with Vines,
texts.1.414: And ELEALE to th' ASPHALTICK Pool.
texts.1.415: PEOR his other Name, when he entic'd
texts.1.416: ISRAEL in SITTIM on their march from NILE
texts.1.417: To do him wanton rites, which cost them woe.
texts.1.418: Yet thence his lustful Orgies he enlarg'd
texts.1.419: Even to that Hill of scandal, by the Grove
texts.1.420: Of MOLOCH homicide, lust hard by hate;
texts.1.421: Till good JOSIAH drove them thence to Hell.
texts.1.422: With these came they, who from the bordring flood
texts.1.423: Of old EUPHRATES to the Brook that parts
texts.1.424: EGYPT from SYRIAN ground, had general Names
texts.1.425: Of BAALIM and ASHTAROTH, those male,
texts.1.426: These Feminine. For Spirits when they please
texts.1.427: Can either Sex assume, or both; so soft
texts.1.428: And uncompounded is their Essence pure,
texts.1.429: Not ti'd or manacl'd with joynt or limb,
texts.1.430: Nor founded on the brittle strength of bones,
texts.1.431: Like cumbrous flesh; but in what shape they choose
texts.1.432: Dilated or condens't, bright or obscure,
texts.1.434: And works of love or enmity fulfill.
texts.1.435: For those the Race of ISRAEL oft forsook
texts.1.436: Their living strength, and unfrequented left
texts.1.437: His righteous Altar, bowing lowly down
texts.1.438: To bestial Gods; for which their heads as low
texts.1.439: Bow'd down in Battel, sunk before the Spear
texts.1.440: Of despicable foes. With these in troop
texts.1.441: Came ASTORETH, whom the PHOENICIANS call'd
texts.1.442: ASTARTE, Queen of Heav'n, with crescent Horns;
texts.1.443: To whose bright Image nightly by the Moon
texts.1.444: SIDONIAN Virgins paid their Vows and Songs,
texts.1.445: In SION also not unsung, where stood
texts.1.446: Her Temple on th' offensive Mountain, built
texts.1.447: By that uxorious King, whose heart though large,
texts.1.449: To Idols foul. THAMMUZ came next behind,
texts.1.450: Whose annual wound in LEBANON allur'd
texts.1.451: The SYRIAN Damsels to lament his fate
texts.1.452: In amorous dittyes all a Summers day,
texts.1.453: While smooth ADONIS from his native Rock
texts.1.454: Ran purple to the Sea, suppos'd with blood
texts.1.455: Of THAMMUZ yearly wounded: the Love-tale
texts.1.456: Infected SIONS daughters with like heat,
texts.1.457: Whose wanton passions in the sacred Porch
texts.1.458: EZEKIEL saw, when by the Vision led
texts.1.459: His eye survay'd the dark Idolatries
texts.1.460: Of alienated JUDAH. Next came one
texts.1.461: Who mourn'd in earnest, when the Captive Ark
texts.1.462: Maim'd his brute Image, head and hands lopt off
texts.1.463: In his own Temple, on the grunsel edge,
texts.1.464: Where he fell flat, and sham'd his Worshipers:
texts.1.465: DAGON his Name, Sea Monster, upward Man
texts.1.466: And downward Fish: yet had his Temple high
texts.1.467: Rear'd in AZOTUS, dreaded through the Coast
texts.1.468: Of PALESTINE, in GATH and ASCALON,
texts.1.469: And ACCARON and GAZA's frontier bounds.
texts.1.470: Him follow'd RIMMON, whose delightful Seat
texts.1.471: Was fair DAMASCUS, on the fertil Banks
texts.1.472: Of ABBANA and PHARPHAR, lucid streams.
texts.1.473: He also against the house of God was bold:
texts.1.474: A Leper once he lost and gain'd a King,
texts.1.475: AHAZ his sottish Conquerour, whom he drew
texts.1.476: Gods Altar to disparage and displace
texts.1.477: For one of SYRIAN mode, whereon to burn
texts.1.478: His odious offrings, and adore the Gods
texts.1.479: Whom he had vanquisht. After these appear'd
texts.1.480: A crew who under Names of old Renown,
texts.1.481: OSIRIS, ISIS, ORUS and their Train
texts.1.482: With monstrous shapes and sorceries abus'd
texts.1.483: Fanatic EGYPT and her Priests, to seek
texts.1.484: Thir wandring Gods disguis'd in brutish forms
texts.1.485: Rather then human. Nor did ISRAEL scape
texts.1.486: Th' infection when their borrow'd Gold compos'd
texts.1.487: The Calf in OREB: and the Rebel King
texts.1.488: Doubl'd that sin in BETHEL and in DAN,
texts.1.489: Lik'ning his Maker to the Grazed Ox,
texts.1.490: JEHOVAH, who in one Night when he pass'd
texts.1.491: From EGYPT marching, equal'd with one stroke
texts.1.492: Both her first born and all her bleating Gods.
texts.1.493: BELIAL came last, then whom a Spirit more lewd
texts.1.494: Fell not from Heaven, or more gross to love
texts.1.495: Vice for it self: To him no Temple stood
texts.1.496: Or Altar smoak'd; yet who more oft then hee
texts.1.497: In Temples and at Altars, when the Priest
texts.1.498: Turns Atheist, as did ELY'S Sons, who fill'd
texts.1.499: With lust and violence the house of God.
texts.1.500: In Courts and Palaces he also Reigns
texts.1.501: And in luxurious Cities, where the noyse
texts.1.502: Of riot ascends above thir loftiest Towrs,
texts.1.503: And injury and outrage: And when Night
texts.1.504: Darkens the Streets, then wander forth the Sons
texts.1.505: Of BELIAL, flown with insolence and wine.
texts.1.506: Witness the Streets of SODOM, and that night
texts.1.508: Yielded thir Matrons to prevent worse rape.
texts.1.509: These were the prime in order and in might;
texts.1.510: The rest were long to tell, though far renown'd,
texts.1.511: Th' IONIAN Gods, of JAVANS Issue held
texts.1.512: Gods, yet confest later then Heav'n and Earth
texts.1.513: Thir boasted Parents; TITAN Heav'ns first born
texts.1.514: With his enormous brood, and birthright seis'd
texts.1.515: By younger SATURN, he from mightier JOVE
texts.1.516: His own and RHEA'S Son like measure found;
texts.1.517: So JOVE usurping reign'd: these first in CREET
texts.1.518: And IDA known, thence on the Snowy top
texts.1.519: Of cold OLYMPUS rul'd the middle Air
texts.1.520: Thir highest Heav'n; or on the DELPHIAN Cliff,
texts.1.521: Or in DODONA, and through all the bounds
texts.1.522: Of DORIC Land; or who with SATURN old
texts.1.523: Fled over ADRIA to th' HESPERIAN Fields,
texts.1.524: And ore the CELTIC roam'd the utmost Isles.
texts.1.525: All these and more came flocking; but with looks
texts.1.526: Down cast and damp, yet such wherein appear'd
texts.1.527: Obscure som glimps of joy, to have found thir chief
texts.1.528: Not in despair, to have found themselves not lost
texts.1.529: In loss it self; which on his count'nance cast
texts.1.530: Like doubtful hue: but he his wonted pride
texts.1.531: Soon recollecting, with high words, that bore
texts.1.532: Semblance of worth not substance, gently rais'd
texts.1.533: Their fainted courage, and dispel'd their fears.
texts.1.534: Then strait commands that at the warlike sound
texts.1.535: Of Trumpets loud and Clarions be upreard
texts.1.536: His mighty Standard; that proud honour claim'd
texts.1.537: AZAZEL as his right, a Cherube tall:
texts.1.538: Who forthwith from the glittering Staff unfurld
texts.1.539: Th' Imperial Ensign, which full high advanc't
texts.1.540: Shon like a Meteor streaming to the Wind
texts.1.541: With Gemms and Golden lustre rich imblaz'd,
texts.1.542: Seraphic arms and Trophies: all the while
texts.1.544: At which the universal Host upsent
texts.1.545: A shout that tore Hells Concave, and beyond
texts.1.546: Frighted the Reign of CHAOS and old Night.
texts.1.547: All in a moment through the gloom were seen
texts.1.548: Ten thousand Banners rise into the Air
texts.1.549: With Orient Colours waving: with them rose
texts.1.550: A Forrest huge of Spears: and thronging Helms
texts.1.551: Appear'd, and serried Shields in thick array
texts.1.552: Of depth immeasurable: Anon they move
texts.1.553: In perfect PHALANX to the Dorian mood
texts.1.554: Of Flutes and soft Recorders; such as rais'd
texts.1.555: To highth of noblest temper Hero's old
texts.1.556: Arming to Battel, and in stead of rage
texts.1.557: Deliberate valour breath'd, firm and unmov'd
texts.1.558: With dread of death to flight or foul retreat,
texts.1.559: Nor wanting power to mitigate and swage
texts.1.560: With solemn touches, troubl'd thoughts, and chase
texts.1.561: Anguish and doubt and fear and sorrow and pain
texts.1.562: From mortal or immortal minds. Thus they
texts.1.563: Breathing united force with fixed thought
texts.1.564: Mov'd on in silence to soft Pipes that charm'd
texts.1.565: Thir painful steps o're the burnt soyle; and now
texts.1.566: Advanc't in view they stand, a horrid Front
texts.1.567: Of dreadful length and dazling Arms, in guise
texts.1.568: Of Warriers old with order'd Spear and Shield,
texts.1.569: Awaiting what command thir mighty Chief
texts.1.570: Had to impose: He through the armed Files
texts.1.571: Darts his experienc't eye, and soon traverse
texts.1.572: The whole Battalion views, thir order due,
texts.1.573: Thir visages and stature as of Gods,
texts.1.574: Thir number last he summs. And now his heart
texts.1.575: Distends with pride, and hardning in his strength
texts.1.576: Glories: For never since created man,
texts.1.577: Met such imbodied force, as nam'd with these
texts.1.578: Could merit more then that small infantry
texts.1.579: Warr'd on by Cranes: though all the Giant brood
texts.1.580: Of PHLEGRA with th' Heroic Race were joyn'd
texts.1.581: That fought at THEB'S and ILIUM, on each side
texts.1.582: Mixt with auxiliar Gods; and what resounds
texts.1.583: In Fable or ROMANCE of UTHERS Son
texts.1.584: Begirt with BRITISH and ARMORIC Knights;
texts.1.585: And all who since, Baptiz'd or Infidel
texts.1.588: Or whom BISERTA sent from AFRIC shore
texts.1.589: When CHARLEMAIN with all his Peerage fell
texts.1.590: By FONTARABBIA. Thus far these beyond
texts.1.591: Compare of mortal prowess, yet observ'd
texts.1.592: Thir dread Commander: he above the rest
texts.1.593: In shape and gesture proudly eminent
texts.1.594: Stood like a Towr; his form had yet not lost
texts.1.595: All her Original brightness, nor appear'd
texts.1.596: Less then Arch Angel ruind, and th' excess
texts.1.597: Of Glory obscur'd: As when the Sun new ris'n
texts.1.598: Looks through the Horizontal misty Air
texts.1.599: Shorn of his Beams, or from behind the Moon
texts.1.600: In dim Eclips disastrous twilight sheds
texts.1.601: On half the Nations, and with fear of change
texts.1.602: Perplexes Monarchs. Dark'n'd so, yet shon
texts.1.603: Above them all th' Arch Angel: but his face
texts.1.604: Deep scars of Thunder had intrencht, and care
texts.1.605: Sat on his faded cheek, but under Browes
texts.1.606: Of dauntless courage, and considerate Pride
texts.1.607: Waiting revenge: cruel his eye, but cast
texts.1.608: Signs of remorse and passion to behold
texts.1.609: The fellows of his crime, the followers rather
texts.1.610: (Far other once beheld in bliss) condemn'd
texts.1.611: For ever now to have their lot in pain,
texts.1.612: Millions of Spirits for his fault amerc't
texts.1.613: Of Heav'n, and from Eternal Splendors flung
texts.1.614: For his revolt, yet faithfull how they stood,
texts.1.615: Thir Glory witherd. As when Heavens Fire
texts.1.616: Hath scath'd the Forrest Oaks, or Mountain Pines,
texts.1.617: With singed top their stately growth though bare

texts.1.625: O Myriads of immortal Spirits, O Powers
texts.1.626: Matchless, but with th' Almighty, and that strife
texts.1.627: Was not inglorious, though th' event was dire,
texts.1.628: As this place testifies, and this dire change
texts.1.629: Hateful to utter: but what power of mind
texts.1.630: Foreseeing or presaging, from the Depth
texts.1.631: Of knowledge past or present, could have fear'd,
texts.1.632: How such united force of Gods, how such
texts.1.633: As stood like these, could ever know repulse?
texts.1.634: For who can yet beleeve, though after loss,
texts.1.635: That all these puissant Legions, whose exile
texts.1.636: Hath emptied Heav'n, shall faile to re-ascend
texts.1.637: Self-rais'd, and repossess their native seat.
texts.1.638: For me, be witness all the Host of Heav'n,
texts.1.639: If counsels different, or danger shun'd
texts.1.640: By me, have lost our hopes. But he who reigns
texts.1.641: Monarch in Heav'n, till then as one secure
texts.1.642: Sat on his Throne, upheld by old repute,
texts.1.643: Consent or custome, and his Regal State
texts.1.644: Put forth at full, but still his strength conceal'd,
texts.1.645: Which tempted our attempt, and wrought our fall.
texts.1.646: Henceforth his might we know, and know our own
texts.1.647: So as not either to provoke, or dread
texts.1.648: New warr, provok't; our better part remains

texts.1.650: What force effected not: that he no less
texts.1.651: At length from us may find, who overcomes

texts.1.653: Space may produce new Worlds; whereof so rife

texts.1.666: He spake: and to confirm his words, out-flew

texts.1.670: Against the Highest, and fierce with grasped arm's

texts.1.673: There stood a Hill not far whose griesly top
texts.1.674: Belch'd fire and rowling smoak; the rest entire

texts.1.677: The work of Sulphur. Thither wing'd with speed
texts.1.678: A numerous Brigad hasten'd. As when bands
texts.1.679: Of Pioners with Spade and Pickaxe arm'd
texts.1.680: Forerun the Royal Camp, to trench a Field,
texts.1.681: Or cast a Rampart. MAMMON led them on,
texts.1.682: MAMMON, the least erected Spirit that fell
texts.1.683: From heav'n, for ev'n in heav'n his looks thoughts
texts.1.684: Were always downward bent, admiring more
texts.1.685: The riches of Heav'ns pavement, trod'n Gold,
texts.1.686: Then aught divine or holy else enjoy'd
texts.1.687: In vision beatific: by him first
texts.1.688: Men also, and by his suggestion taught,
texts.1.689: Ransack'd the Center, and with impious hands
texts.1.690: Rifl'd the bowels of thir mother Earth
texts.1.691: For Treasures better hid. Soon had his crew
texts.1.692: Op'nd into the Hill a spacious wound
texts.1.693: And dig'd out ribs of Gold. Let none admire
texts.1.694: That riches grow in Hell; that soyle may best
texts.1.695: Deserve the pretious bane. And here let those
texts.1.696: Who boast in mortal things, and wondring tell
texts.1.697: Of BABEL, and the works of MEMPHIAN Kings,
texts.1.698: Learn how thir greatest Monuments of Fame,
texts.1.699: And Strength and Art are easily outdone
texts.1.700: By Spirits reprobate, and in an hour
texts.1.701: What in an age they with incessant toyle
texts.1.703: Nigh on the Plain in many cells prepar'd,
texts.1.704: That underneath had veins of liquid fire
texts.1.705: Sluc'd from the Lake, a second multitude
texts.1.706: With wondrous Art founded the massie Ore,
texts.1.707: Severing each kinde, and scum'd the Bullion dross:
texts.1.708: A third as soon had form'd within the ground
texts.1.709: A various mould, and from the boyling cells
texts.1.710: By strange conveyance fill'd each hollow nook,
texts.1.711: As in an Organ from one blast of wind

texts.1.713: Anon out of the earth a Fabrick huge
texts.1.714: Rose like an Exhalation, with the sound
texts.1.715: Of Dulcet Symphonies and voices sweet,
texts.1.716: Built like a Temple, where PILASTERS round
texts.1.717: Were set, and Doric pillars overlaid
texts.1.718: With Golden Architrave; nor did there want
texts.1.719: Cornice or Freeze, with bossy Sculptures grav'n,
texts.1.720: The Roof was fretted Gold. Not BABILON,
texts.1.722: Equal'd in all thir glories, to inshrine
texts.1.723: BELUS or SERAPIS thir Gods, or seat
texts.1.724: Thir Kings, when AEGYPT with ASSYRIA strove
texts.1.725: In wealth and luxurie. Th' ascending pile
texts.1.726: Stood fixt her stately highth, and strait the dores
texts.1.727: Op'ning thir brazen foulds discover wide
texts.1.728: Within, her ample spaces, o're the smooth
texts.1.729: And level pavement: from the arched roof
texts.1.730: Pendant by suttle Magic many a row
texts.1.731: Of Starry Lamps and blazing Cressets fed
texts.1.732: With Naphtha and ASPHALTUS yeilded light
texts.1.733: As from a sky. The hasty multitude
texts.1.734: Admiring enter'd, and the work some praise
texts.1.735: And some the Architect: his hand was known
texts.1.736: In Heav'n by many a Towred structure high,
texts.1.737: Where Scepter'd Angels held thir residence,
texts.1.738: And sat as Princes, whom the supreme King
texts.1.739: Exalted to such power, and gave to rule,
texts.1.740: Each in his Herarchie, the Orders bright.
texts.1.741: Nor was his name unheard or unador'd
texts.1.742: In ancient Greece; and in AUSONIAN land
texts.1.743: Men call'd him MULCIBER; and how he fell
texts.1.744: From Heav'n, they fabl'd, thrown by angry JOVE
texts.1.745: Sheer o're the Chrystal Battlements: from Morn
texts.1.746: To Noon he fell, from Noon to dewy Eve,
texts.1.747: A Summers day; and with the setting Sun
texts.1.748: Dropt from the Zenith like a falling Star,
texts.1.749: On LEMNOS th' AEGAEAN Ile: thus they relate,
texts.1.750: Erring; for he with this rebellious rout
texts.1.751: Fell long before; nor aught avail'd him now
texts.1.752: To have built in Heav'n high Towrs; nor did he scape
texts.1.753: By all his Engins, but was headlong sent
texts.1.754: With his industrious crew to build in hell.
texts.1.755: Mean while the winged Haralds by command
texts.1.756: Of Sovran power, with awful Ceremony
texts.1.757: And Trumpets sound throughout the Host proclaim
texts.1.758: A solemn Councel forthwith to be held
texts.1.760: Of Satan and his Peers: thir summons call'd
texts.1.761: From every and Band squared Regiment
texts.1.762: By place or choice the worthiest; they anon
texts.1.763: With hundreds and with thousands trooping came
texts.1.764: Attended: all access was throng'd, the Gates
texts.1.765: And Porches wide, but chief the spacious Hall
texts.1.766: (Though like a cover'd field, where Champions bold
texts.1.767: Wont ride in arm'd, and at the Soldans chair
texts.1.768: Defi'd the best of Panim chivalry
texts.1.769: To mortal combat or carreer with Lance)
texts.1.770: Thick swarm'd, both on the ground and in the air,
texts.1.771: Brusht with the hiss of russling wings. As Bees
texts.1.772: In spring time, when the Sun with Taurus rides,
texts.1.773: Poure forth thir populous youth about the Hive
texts.1.774: In clusters; they among fresh dews and flowers
texts.1.775: Flie to and fro, or on the smoothed Plank,
texts.1.776: The suburb of thir Straw-built Cittadel,
texts.1.777: New rub'd with Baume, expatiate and confer
texts.1.778: Thir State affairs. So thick the aerie crowd
texts.1.779: Swarm'd and were straitn'd; till the Signal giv'n,
texts.1.780: Behold a wonder! they but now who seemd
texts.1.781: In bigness to surpass Earths Giant Sons
texts.1.782: Now less then smallest Dwarfs, in narrow room
texts.1.783: Throng numberless, like that Pigmean Race
texts.1.784: Beyond the INDIAN Mount, or Faerie Elves,
texts.1.785: Whose midnight Revels, by a Forrest side
texts.1.786: Or Fountain fome belated Peasant sees,
texts.1.787: Or dreams he sees, while over head the Moon
texts.1.788: Sits Arbitress, and neerer to the Earth
texts.1.789: Wheels her pale course, they on thir mirth dance
texts.1.790: Intent, with jocond Music charm his ear;
texts.1.791: At once with joy and fear his heart rebounds.
texts.1.792: Thus incorporeal Spirits to smallest forms
texts.1.793: Reduc'd thir shapes immense, and were at large,

texts.1.795: Of that infernal Court. But far within

texts.1.797: The great Seraphic Lords and Cherubim
texts.1.798: In close recess and secret conclave sat
texts.1.799: A thousand Demy-Gods on golden seat's,
texts.1.800: Frequent and full. After short silence then
texts.1.801: And summons read, the great consult began.
