texts.2.236: Within Heav'ns bound, unless Heav'ns Lord supream
texts.2.237: We overpower? Suppose he should relent
texts.2.238: And publish Grace to all, on promise made
texts.2.239: Of new Subjection; with what eyes could we
texts.2.240: Stand in his presence humble, and receive
texts.2.241: Strict Laws impos'd, to celebrate his Throne
texts.2.242: With warbl'd Hymns, and to his Godhead sing
texts.2.243: Forc't Halleluiah's; while he Lordly sits
texts.2.244: Our envied Sovran, and his Altar breathes
texts.2.246: Our servile offerings. This must be our task
texts.2.247: In Heav'n, this our delight; how wearisom
texts.2.248: Eternity so spent in worship paid
texts.2.249: To whom we hate. Let us not then pursue
texts.2.250: By force impossible, by leave obtain'd
texts.2.251: Unacceptable, though in Heav'n, our state
texts.2.252: Of splendid vassalage, but rather seek
texts.2.253: Our own good from our selves, and from our own
texts.2.254: Live to our selves, though in this vast recess,
texts.2.255: Free, and to none accountable, preferring
texts.2.256: Hard liberty before the easie yoke
texts.2.257: Of servile Pomp. Our greatness will appear
texts.2.258: Then most conspicuous, when great things of small,
texts.2.259: Useful of hurtful, prosperous of adverse
texts.2.260: We can create, and in what place so e're
texts.2.261: Thrive under evil, and work ease out of pain
texts.2.262: Through labour and endurance. This deep world
texts.2.263: Of darkness do we dread? How oft amidst
texts.2.264: Thick clouds and dark doth Heav'ns all-ruling Sire
texts.2.265: Choose to reside, his Glory unobscur'd,
texts.2.266: And with the Majesty of darkness round
texts.2.267: Covers his Throne; from whence deep thunders roar
texts.2.268: Must'ring thir rage, and Heav'n resembles Hell?
texts.2.269: As he our Darkness, cannot we his Light
texts.2.270: Imitate when we please? This Desart soile
texts.2.271: Wants not her hidden lustre, Gemms and Gold;
texts.2.272: Nor want we skill or art, from whence to raise
texts.2.273: Magnificence; and what can Heav'n shew more?
texts.2.274: Our torments also may in length of time
texts.2.275: Become our Elements, these piercing Fires
texts.2.276: As soft as now severe, our temper chang'd
texts.2.277: Into their temper; which must needs remove
texts.2.278: The sensible of pain. All things invite
texts.2.279: To peaceful Counsels, and the settl'd State
texts.2.280: Of order, how in safety best we may
texts.2.281: Compose our present evils, with regard
texts.2.282: Of what we are and where, dismissing quite
texts.2.283: All thoughts of Warr: ye have what I advise.
texts.2.284: He scarce had finisht, when such murmur filld
texts.2.285: Th' Assembly, as when hollow Rocks retain
texts.2.286: The sound of blustring winds, which all night long
texts.2.287: Had rous'd the Sea, now with hoarse cadence lull
texts.2.288: Sea-faring men orewatcht, whose Bark by chance
texts.2.289: Or Pinnace anchors in a craggy Bay
texts.2.290: After the Tempest: Such applause was heard
texts.2.291: As MAMMON ended, and his Sentence pleas'd,
texts.2.292: Advising peace: for such another Field
texts.2.293: They dreaded worse then Hell: so much the fear
texts.2.294: Of Thunder and the Sword of MICHAEL
texts.2.295: Wrought still within them; and no less desire
texts.2.296: To found this nether Empire, which might rise
texts.2.297: By pollicy, and long process of time,
texts.2.299: Which when BEELZEBUB perceiv'd, then whom,
texts.2.300: SATAN except, none higher sat, with grave
texts.2.301: Aspect he rose, and in his rising seem'd
texts.2.302: A Pillar of State; deep on his Front engraven
texts.2.304: And Princely counsel in his face yet shon,
texts.2.305: Majestick though in ruin: sage he stood
texts.2.306: With ATLANTEAN shoulders fit to bear
texts.2.307: The weight of mightiest Monarchies; his look
texts.2.308: Drew audience and attention still as Night
texts.2.309: Or Summers Noon-tide air, while thus he spake.
texts.2.310: Thrones and imperial Powers, off-spring of heav'n,
texts.2.311: Ethereal Vertues; or these Titles now
texts.2.312: Must we renounce, and changing stile be call'd
texts.2.313: Princes of Hell? for so the popular vote
texts.2.314: Inclines, here to continue, and build up here
texts.2.315: A growing Empire; doubtless; while we dream,
texts.2.316: And know not that the King of Heav'n hath doom'd
texts.2.317: This place our dungeon, not our safe retreat
texts.2.318: Beyond his Potent arm, to live exempt
texts.2.319: From Heav'ns high jurisdiction, in new League
texts.2.320: Banded against his Throne, but to remaine
texts.2.321: In strictest bondage, though thus far remov'd,
texts.2.323: His captive multitude: For he, be sure,
texts.2.324: In highth or depth, still first and last will Reign
texts.2.325: Sole King, and of his Kingdom loose no part
texts.2.326: By our revolt, but over Hell extend
texts.2.327: His Empire, and with Iron Scepter rule
texts.2.328: Us here, as with his Golden those in Heav'n.
texts.2.329: What sit we then projecting Peace and Warr?
texts.2.330: Warr hath determin'd us, and foild with loss
texts.2.331: Irreparable; tearms of peace yet none
texts.2.332: Voutsaf't or sought; for what peace will be giv'n
texts.2.333: To us enslav'd, but custody severe,
texts.2.335: Inflicted? and what peace can we return,
texts.2.336: But to our power hostility and hate,
texts.2.337: Untam'd reluctance, and revenge though slow,
texts.2.338: Yet ever plotting how the Conquerour least
texts.2.339: May reap his conquest, and may least rejoyce
texts.2.340: In doing what we most in suffering feel?
texts.2.341: Nor will occasion want, nor shall we need
texts.2.343: Heav'n, whose high walls fear no assault or Siege,
texts.2.344: Or ambush from the Deep. What if we find
texts.2.345: Some easier enterprize? There is a place
texts.2.346: (If ancient and prophetic fame in Heav'n
texts.2.347: Err not) another World, the happy seat
texts.2.348: Of som new Race call'd MAN, about this time
texts.2.349: To be created like to us, though less
texts.2.350: In power and excellence, but favour'd more
texts.2.351: Of him who rules above; so was his will
texts.2.352: Pronounc'd among the Gods, and by an Oath,
texts.2.353: That shook Heav'ns whol circumference, confirm'd.
texts.2.354: Thither let us bend all our thoughts, to learn
texts.2.355: What creatures there inhabit, of what mould,
texts.2.356: Or substance, how endu'd, and what thir Power,
texts.2.357: And where thir weakness, how attempted best,
texts.2.358: By force or suttlety: Though Heav'n be shut,
texts.2.359: And Heav'ns high Arbitrator sit secure
texts.2.360: In his own strength, this place may lye expos'd
texts.2.361: The utmost border of his Kingdom, left
texts.2.362: To their defence who hold it: here perhaps
texts.2.363: Som advantagious act may be achiev'd
texts.2.364: By sudden onset, either with Hell fire
texts.2.365: To waste his whole Creation, or possess
texts.2.366: All as our own, and drive as we were driven,
texts.2.367: The punie habitants, or if not drive,
texts.2.368: Seduce them to our Party, that thir God
texts.2.369: May prove thir foe, and with repenting hand
texts.2.370: Abolish his own works. This would surpass
texts.2.371: Common revenge, and interrupt his joy
texts.2.372: In our Confusion, and our Joy upraise
texts.2.373: In his disturbance; when his darling Sons
texts.2.374: Hurl'd headlong to partake with us, shall curse
texts.2.375: Thir frail Originals, and faded bliss,
texts.2.376: Faded so soon. Advise if this be worth
texts.2.377: Attempting, or to sit in darkness here
texts.2.379: Pleaded his devilish Counsel, first devis'd
texts.2.380: By SATAN, and in part propos'd: for whence,
texts.2.381: But from the Author of all ill could Spring
texts.2.382: So deep a malice, to confound the race
texts.2.383: Of mankind in one root, and Earth with Hell
texts.2.384: To mingle and involve, done all to spite
texts.2.385: The great Creatour? But thir spite still serves
texts.2.386: His glory to augment. The bold design
texts.2.387: Pleas'd highly those infernal States, and joy
texts.2.388: Sparkl'd in all thir eyes; with full assent
texts.2.389: They vote: whereat his speech he thus renews.
texts.2.390: Well have ye judg'd, well ended long debate,
texts.2.391: Synod of Gods, and like to what ye are,
texts.2.392: Great things resolv'd; which from the lowest deep
texts.2.393: Will once more lift us up, in spight of Fate,
texts.2.394: Neerer our ancient Seat; perhaps in view
texts.2.395: Of those bright confines, whence with neighbouring Arms
texts.2.396: And opportune excursion we may chance
texts.2.397: Re-enter Heav'n; or else in some milde Zone
texts.2.398: Dwell not unvisited of Heav'ns fair Light
texts.2.399: Secure, and at the brightning Orient beam
texts.2.400: Purge off this gloom; the soft delicious Air,
texts.2.401: To heal the scarr of these corrosive Fires
texts.2.402: Shall breath her balme. But first whom shall we send
texts.2.403: In search of this new world, whom shall we find
texts.2.404: Sufficient? who shall tempt with wandring feet
texts.2.406: And through the palpable obscure find out
texts.2.407: His uncouth way, or spread his aerie flight
texts.2.409: Over the vast abrupt, ere he arrive
texts.2.410: The happy Ile; what strength, what art can then
texts.2.411: Suffice, or what evasion bear him safe
texts.2.412: Through the strict Senteries and Stations thick
texts.2.413: Of Angels watching round? Here he had need
texts.2.414: All circumspection, and we now no less
texts.2.415: Choice in our suffrage; for on whom we send,
texts.2.416: The weight of all and our last hope relies.
texts.2.417: This said, he sat; and expectation held
texts.2.418: His look suspence, awaiting who appeer'd
texts.2.419: To second, or oppose, or undertake
texts.2.420: The perilous attempt: but all sat mute,
texts.2.421: Pondering the danger with deep thoughts; each
texts.2.422: In others count'nance red his own dismay
texts.2.423: Astonisht: none among the choice and prime
texts.2.424: Of those Heav'n-warring Champions could be found
texts.2.425: So hardie as to proffer or accept
texts.2.426: Alone the dreadful voyage; till at last
texts.2.427: SATAN, whom now transcendent glory rais'd
texts.2.428: Above his fellows, with Monarchal pride
texts.2.429: Conscious of highest worth, unmov'd thus spake.
texts.2.430: O Progeny of Heav'n, Empyreal Thrones,
texts.2.431: With reason hath deep silence and demurr
texts.2.432: Seis'd us, though undismaid: long is the way
texts.2.433: And hard, that out of Hell leads up to Light;
texts.2.434: Our prison strong, this huge convex of Fire,
texts.2.435: Outrageous to devour, immures us round
texts.2.436: Ninefold, and gates of burning Adamant
texts.2.437: Barr'd over us prohibit all egress.
texts.2.438: These past, if any pass, the void profound
texts.2.439: Of unessential Night receives him next
texts.2.440: Wide gaping, and with utter loss of being
texts.2.441: Threatens him, plung'd in that abortive gulf.
texts.2.442: If thence he scape into what ever world,
texts.2.443: Or unknown Region, what remains him less
texts.2.444: Then unknown dangers and as hard escape.
texts.2.445: But I should ill become this Throne, O Peers,
texts.2.447: With splendor, arm'd with power, if aught propos'd
texts.2.448: And judg'd of public moment, in the shape
texts.2.449: Of difficulty or danger could deterre
texts.2.450: Me from attempting. Wherefore do I assume
texts.2.451: These Royalties, and not refuse to Reign,
texts.2.452: Refusing to accept as great a share
texts.2.453: Of hazard as of honour, due alike
texts.2.454: To him who Reigns, and so much to him due
texts.2.455: Of hazard more, as he above the rest
texts.2.456: High honourd sits? Go therfore mighty powers,
texts.2.457: Terror of Heav'n, though fall'n; intend at home,
texts.2.458: While here shall be our home, what best may ease
texts.2.459: The present misery, and render Hell
texts.2.460: More tollerable; if there be cure or charm
texts.2.461: To respite or deceive, or slack the pain
texts.2.462: Of this ill Mansion: intermit no watch
texts.2.463: Against a wakeful Foe, while I abroad
texts.2.464: Through all the coasts of dark destruction seek
texts.2.465: Deliverance for us all: this enterprize
texts.2.466: None shall partake with me. Thus saying rose
texts.2.467: The Monarch, and prevented all reply,
texts.2.468: Prudent, least from his resolution rais'd
texts.2.469: Others among the chief might offer now
texts.2.470: (Certain to be refus'd) what erst they feard;
texts.2.471: And so refus'd might in opinion stand
texts.2.472: His rivals, winning cheap the high repute
texts.2.473: Which he through hazard huge must earn. But they
texts.2.474: Dreaded not more th' adventure then his voice
texts.2.475: Forbidding; and at once with him they rose;
texts.2.476: Thir rising all at once was as the sound
texts.2.477: Of Thunder heard remote. Towards him they bend
texts.2.478: With awful reverence prone; and as a God
texts.2.479: Extoll him equal to the highest in Heav'n:
texts.2.480: Nor fail'd they to express how much they prais'd,
texts.2.481: That for the general safety he despis'd
texts.2.482: His own: for neither do the Spirits damn'd
texts.2.483: Loose all thir vertue; least bad men should boast
texts.2.484: Thir specious deeds on earth, which glory excites,
texts.2.485: Or close ambition varnisht o're with zeal.
texts.2.486: Thus they thir doubtful consultations dark
texts.2.487: Ended rejoycing in thir matchless Chief:
texts.2.488: As when from mountain tops the dusky clouds
texts.2.489: Ascending, while the North wind sleeps, o'respread
texts.2.490: Heav'ns chearful face, the lowring Element
texts.2.491: Scowls ore the dark'nd lantskip Snow, or showre;
texts.2.492: If chance the radiant Sun with farewell sweet
texts.2.493: Extend his ev'ning beam, the fields revive,
texts.2.494: The birds thir notes renew, and bleating herds
texts.2.495: Attest thir joy, that hill and valley rings.
texts.2.496: O shame to men! Devil with Devil damn'd
texts.2.497: Firm concord holds, men onely disagree
texts.2.498: Of Creatures rational, though under hope
texts.2.499: Of heavenly Grace: and God proclaiming peace,
texts.2.500: Yet live in hatred, enmitie, and strife
texts.2.501: Among themselves, and levie cruel warres,
texts.2.502: Wasting the Earth, each other to destroy:
texts.2.503: As if (which might induce us to accord)
texts.2.504: Man had not hellish foes anow besides,
texts.2.505: That day and night for his destruction waite.
texts.2.506: The STYGIAN Councel thus dissolv'd; and forth
texts.2.507: In order came the grand infernal Peers,
texts.2.508: Midst came thir mighty Paramount, and seemd
texts.2.509: Alone th' Antagonist of Heav'n, nor less
texts.2.510: Then Hells dread Emperour with pomp Supream,
texts.2.511: And God-like imitated State; him round
texts.2.512: A Globe of fierie Seraphim inclos'd
texts.2.513: With bright imblazonrie, and horrent Arms.
texts.2.514: Then of thir Session ended they bid cry
texts.2.515: With Trumpets regal sound the great result:
texts.2.516: Toward the four winds four speedy Cherubim
texts.2.517: Put to thir mouths the sounding Alchymie
texts.2.518: By Haralds voice explain'd: the hollow Abyss
texts.2.519: Heard farr and wide, and all the host of Hell
texts.2.520: With deafning shout, return'd them loud acclaim.
texts.2.521: Thence more at ease thir minds and somwhat rais'd
texts.2.522: By false presumptuous hope, the ranged powers
texts.2.523: Disband, and wandring, each his several way
texts.2.524: Pursues, as inclination or sad choice
texts.2.525: Leads him perplext, where he may likeliest find
texts.2.526: Truce to his restless thoughts, and entertain
texts.2.527: The irksome hours, till his great Chief return.
texts.2.528: Part on the Plain, or in the Air sublime
texts.2.529: Upon the wing, or in swift race contend,
texts.2.530: As at th' Olympian Games or PYTHIAN fields;
texts.2.531: Part curb thir fierie Steeds, or shun the Goal
texts.2.532: With rapid wheels, or fronted Brigads form.
texts.2.533: As when to warn proud Cities warr appears
texts.2.534: Wag'd in the troubl'd Skie, and Armies rush
texts.2.535: To Battel in the Clouds, before each Van
texts.2.536: Pric forth the Aerie Knights, and couch thir spears
texts.2.537: Till thickest Legions close; with feats of Arms
texts.2.538: From either end of Heav'n the welkin burns.
texts.2.539: Others with vast TYPHOEAN rage more fell
texts.2.540: Rend up both Rocks and Hills, and ride the Air
texts.2.541: In whirlwind; Hell scarce holds the wilde uproar.
texts.2.542: As when ALCIDES from OEALIA Crown'd
texts.2.543: With conquest, felt th' envenom'd robe, and tore
texts.2.544: Through pain up by the roots THESSALIAN Pines,
texts.2.545: And LICHAS from the top of OETA threw
texts.2.546: Into th' EUBOIC Sea. Others more milde,
texts.2.547: Retreated in a silent valley, sing
texts.2.548: With notes Angelical to many a Harp
texts.2.549: Thir own Heroic deeds and hapless fall
texts.2.550: By doom of Battel; and complain that Fate
texts.2.551: Free Vertue should enthrall to Force or Chance.
texts.2.552: Thir song was partial, but the harmony
texts.2.553: (What could it less when Spirits immortal sing?)
texts.2.554: Suspended Hell, and took with ravishment
texts.2.555: The thronging audience. In discourse more sweet
texts.2.556: (For Eloquence the Soul, Song charms the Sense,)
texts.2.557: Others apart sat on a Hill retir'd,
texts.2.558: In thoughts more elevate, and reason'd high
texts.2.559: Of Providence, Foreknowledge, Will, and Fate,
texts.2.560: Fixt Fate, free will, foreknowledge absolute,
texts.2.561: And found no end, in wandring mazes lost.
texts.2.562: Of good and evil much they argu'd then,
texts.2.564: Passion and Apathie, and glory and shame,
texts.2.565: Vain wisdom all, and false Philosophie:
texts.2.566: Yet with a pleasing sorcerie could charm
texts.2.567: Pain for a while or anguish, and excite
texts.2.568: Fallacious hope, or arm th' obdured brest
texts.2.569: With stubborn patience as with triple steel.
texts.2.570: Another part in Squadrons and gross Bands,
texts.2.571: On bold adventure to discover wide
texts.2.572: That dismal world, if any Clime perhaps
texts.2.573: Might yeild them easier habitation, bend
texts.2.574: Four ways thir flying March, along the Banks
texts.2.575: Of four infernal Rivers that disgorge
texts.2.576: Into the burning Lake thir baleful streams;
texts.2.577: Abhorred STYX the flood of deadly hate,
texts.2.578: Sad ACHERON of sorrow, black and deep;
texts.2.580: Heard on the ruful stream; fierce PHLEGETON
texts.2.581: Whose waves of torrent fire inflame with rage.
texts.2.582: Farr off from these a slow and silent stream,
texts.2.583: LETHE the River of Oblivion roules
texts.2.584: Her watrie Labyrinth, whereof who drinks,
texts.2.585: Forthwith his former state and being forgets,
texts.2.586: Forgets both joy and grief, pleasure and pain.
texts.2.587: Beyond this flood a frozen Continent
texts.2.588: Lies dark and wilde, beat with perpetual storms
texts.2.589: Of Whirlwind and dire Hail, which on firm land
texts.2.590: Thaws not, but gathers heap, and ruin seems
texts.2.591: Of ancient pile; all else deep snow and ice,
texts.2.592: A gulf profound as that SERBONIAN Bog
texts.2.593: Betwixt DAMIATA and mount CASIUS old,
texts.2.594: Where Armies whole have sunk: the parching Air
texts.2.595: Burns frore, and cold performs th' effect of Fire.
texts.2.597: At certain revolutions all the damn'd
texts.2.598: Are brought: and feel by turns the bitter change
texts.2.599: Of fierce extreams, extreams by change more fierce,
texts.2.600: From Beds of raging Fire to starve in Ice
texts.2.601: Thir soft Ethereal warmth, and there to pine
texts.2.603: Periods of time, thence hurried back to fire.
texts.2.604: They ferry over this LETHEAN Sound
texts.2.605: Both to and fro, thir sorrow to augment,
texts.2.606: And wish and struggle, as they pass, to reach
texts.2.607: The tempting stream, with one small drop to loose
texts.2.608: In sweet forgetfulness all pain and woe,
texts.2.609: All in one moment, and so neer the brink;
texts.2.610: But fate withstands, and to oppose th' attempt
texts.2.612: The Ford, and of it self the water flies
texts.2.613: All taste of living wight, as once it fled
texts.2.614: The lip of TANTALUS. Thus roving on
texts.2.615: In confus'd march forlorn, th' adventrous Bands
texts.2.616: With shuddring horror pale, and eyes agast
texts.2.617: View'd first thir lamentable lot, and found
texts.2.618: No rest: through many a dark and drearie Vaile
texts.2.619: They pass'd, and many a Region dolorous,
texts.2.620: O're many a Frozen, many a Fierie Alpe,
texts.2.621: Rocks, Caves, Lakes, Fens, Bogs, Dens, and shades of death,
texts.2.622: A Universe of death, which God by curse
texts.2.623: Created evil, for evil only good,
texts.2.624: Where all life dies, death lives, and nature breeds,
texts.2.625: Perverse, all monstrous, all prodigious things,
texts.2.627: Then Fables yet have feign'd, or fear conceiv'd,
texts.2.628: GORGONS and HYDRA'S, and CHIMERA'S dire.
texts.2.629: Mean while the Adversary of God and Man,
texts.2.630: SATAN with thoughts inflam'd of highest design,
texts.2.631: Puts on swift wings, and toward the Gates of Hell
texts.2.632: Explores his solitary flight; som times
texts.2.633: He scours the right hand coast, som times the left,
texts.2.634: Now shaves with level wing the Deep, then soares
texts.2.635: Up to the fiery concave touring high.
texts.2.636: As when farr off at Sea a Fleet descri'd
texts.2.637: Hangs in the Clouds, by AEQUINOCTIAL Winds
texts.2.638: Close sailing from BENGALA, or the Iles
texts.2.639: Of TERNATE and TIDORE, whence Merchants bring
texts.2.640: Thir spicie Drugs: they on the trading Flood
texts.2.641: Through the wide ETHIOPIAN to the Cape
texts.2.642: Ply stemming nightly toward the Pole. So seem'd
texts.2.643: Farr off the flying Fiend: at last appeer
texts.2.644: Hell bounds high reaching to the horrid Roof,
texts.2.645: And thrice threefold the Gates; three folds were Brass
texts.2.646: Three Iron, three of Adamantine Rock,
texts.2.648: Yet unconsum'd. Before the Gates there sat
texts.2.649: On either side a formidable shape;
texts.2.650: The one seem'd Woman to the waste, and fair,
texts.2.651: But ended foul in many a scaly fould
texts.2.652: Voluminous and vast, a Serpent arm'd
texts.2.653: With mortal sting: about her middle round
texts.2.654: A cry of Hell Hounds never ceasing bark'd
texts.2.655: With wide CERBEREAN mouths full loud, and rung
texts.2.656: A hideous Peal: yet, when they list, would creep,
texts.2.657: If aught disturb'd thir noyse, into her woomb,
texts.2.658: And kennel there, yet there still bark'd and howl'd
texts.2.659: Within unseen. Farr less abhorrd then these
texts.2.660: Vex'd SCYLLA bathing in the Sea that parts
texts.2.661: CALABRIA from the hoarce TRINACRIAN shore:
texts.2.662: Nor uglier follow the Night-Hag, when call'd
texts.2.663: In secret, riding through the Air she comes
texts.2.664: Lur'd with the smell of infant blood, to dance
texts.2.665: With LAPLAND Witches, while the labouring Moon
texts.2.666: Eclipses at thir charms. The other shape,
texts.2.667: If shape it might be call'd that shape had none
texts.2.668: Distinguishable in member, joynt, or limb,
texts.2.669: Or substance might be call'd that shadow seem'd,
texts.2.670: For each seem'd either; black it stood as Night,
texts.2.671: Fierce as ten Furies, terrible as Hell,
texts.2.672: And shook a dreadful Dart; what seem'd his head
texts.2.673: The likeness of a Kingly Crown had on.
texts.2.674: SATAN was now at hand, and from his seat
texts.2.675: The Monster moving onward came as fast,
texts.2.676: With horrid strides, Hell trembled as he strode.
texts.2.677: Th' undaunted Fiend what this might be admir'd,
texts.2.678: Admir'd, not fear'd; God and his Son except,
texts.2.679: Created thing naught vallu'd he nor shun'd;
texts.2.680: And with disdainful look thus first began.
texts.2.681: Whence and what art thou, execrable shape,
texts.2.682: That dar'st, though grim and terrible, advance
texts.2.683: Thy miscreated Front athwart my way
texts.2.684: To yonder Gates? through them I mean to pass,
texts.2.685: That be assur'd, without leave askt of thee:
texts.2.686: Retire, or taste thy folly, and learn by proof,
texts.2.687: Hell-born, not to contend with Spirits of Heav'n.
texts.2.688: To whom the Goblin full of wrauth reply'd,
texts.2.689: Art thou that Traitor Angel, art thou hee,
texts.2.690: Who first broke peace in Heav'n and Faith, till then
texts.2.691: Unbrok'n, and in proud rebellious Arms
texts.2.692: Drew after him the third part of Heav'ns Sons
texts.2.693: Conjur'd against the highest, for which both Thou
texts.2.694: And they outcast from God, are here condemn'd
texts.2.695: To waste Eternal daies in woe and pain?
texts.2.696: And reck'n'st thou thy self with Spirits of Heav'n,
texts.2.697: Hell-doomd, and breath'st defiance here and scorn,
texts.2.698: Where I reign King, and to enrage thee more,
texts.2.699: Thy King and Lord? Back to thy punishment,
texts.2.700: False fugitive, and to thy speed add wings,
texts.2.701: Least with a whip of Scorpions I pursue
texts.2.702: Thy lingring, or with one stroke of this Dart
texts.2.703: Strange horror seise thee, and pangs unfelt before.
texts.2.704: So spake the grieslie terrour, and in shape,
texts.2.705: So speaking and so threatning, grew ten fold
texts.2.706: More dreadful and deform: on th' other side
texts.2.708: Unterrifi'd, and like a Comet burn'd,
texts.2.709: That fires the length of OPHIUCUS huge
texts.2.710: In th' Artick Sky, and from his horrid hair
texts.2.711: Shakes Pestilence and Warr. Each at the Head
texts.2.712: Level'd his deadly aime; thir fatall hands
texts.2.713: No second stroke intend, and such a frown
texts.2.714: Each cast at th' other, as when two black Clouds
texts.2.715: With Heav'ns Artillery fraught, come rattling on
texts.2.716: Over the CASPIAN, then stand front to front
texts.2.717: Hov'ring a space, till Winds the signal blow
texts.2.718: To joyn thir dark Encounter in mid air:
texts.2.719: So frownd the mighty Combatants, that Hell
texts.2.720: Grew darker at thir frown, so matcht they stood;
texts.2.721: For never but once more was either like
texts.2.722: To meet so great a foe: and now great deeds
texts.2.723: Had been achiev'd, whereof all Hell had rung,
texts.2.724: Had not the Snakie Sorceress that sat
texts.2.725: Fast by Hell Gate, and kept the fatal Key,
texts.2.726: Ris'n, and with hideous outcry rush'd between.
texts.2.727: O Father, what intends thy hand, she cry'd,
texts.2.728: Against thy only Son? What fury O Son,
texts.2.729: Possesses thee to bend that mortal Dart
texts.2.730: Against thy Fathers head? and know'st for whom;
texts.2.731: For him who sits above and laughs the while
texts.2.732: At thee ordain'd his drudge, to execute
texts.2.733: What e're his wrath, which he calls Justice, bids,
texts.2.734: His wrath which one day will destroy ye both.
texts.2.735: She spake, and at her words the hellish Pest
texts.2.736: Forbore, then these to her SATAN return'd:
texts.2.737: So strange thy outcry, and thy words so strange
texts.2.738: Thou interposest, that my sudden hand
texts.2.739: Prevented spares to tell thee yet by deeds
texts.2.740: What it intends; till first I know of thee,
texts.2.741: What thing thou art, thus double-form'd, and why
texts.2.742: In this infernal Vaile first met thou call'st
texts.2.743: Me Father, and that Fantasm call'st my Son?
texts.2.744: I know thee not, nor ever saw till now
texts.2.745: Sight more detestable then him and thee.
texts.2.746: T' whom thus the Portress of Hell Gate reply'd;
texts.2.747: Hast thou forgot me then, and do I seem
texts.2.748: Now in thine eye so foul, once deemd so fair
texts.2.749: In Heav'n, when at th' Assembly, and in sight
texts.2.750: Of all the Seraphim with thee combin'd
texts.2.751: In bold conspiracy against Heav'ns King,
texts.2.752: All on a sudden miserable pain
texts.2.753: Surpris'd thee, dim thine eyes, and dizzie swumm
texts.2.754: In darkness, while thy head flames thick and fast
texts.2.755: Threw forth, till on the left side op'ning wide,
texts.2.756: Likest to thee in shape and count'nance bright,
texts.2.757: Then shining heav'nly fair, a Goddess arm'd
texts.2.758: Out of thy head I sprung: amazement seis'd
texts.2.759: All th' Host of Heav'n; back they recoild affraid
texts.2.760: At first, and call'd me SIN, and for a Sign
texts.2.761: Portentous held me; but familiar grown,
texts.2.762: I pleas'd, and with attractive graces won
texts.2.763: The most averse, thee chiefly, who full oft
texts.2.764: Thy self in me thy perfect image viewing
texts.2.765: Becam'st enamour'd, and such joy thou took'st
texts.2.766: With me in secret, that my womb conceiv'd
texts.2.767: A growing burden. Mean while Warr arose,
texts.2.768: And fields were fought in Heav'n; wherein remaind
texts.2.769: (For what could else) to our Almighty Foe
texts.2.770: Cleer Victory, to our part loss and rout
texts.2.771: Through all the Empyrean: down they fell
texts.2.772: Driv'n headlong from the Pitch of Heaven, down
texts.2.773: Into this Deep, and in the general fall
texts.2.774: I also; at which time this powerful Key
texts.2.775: Into my hand was giv'n, with charge to keep
texts.2.776: These Gates for ever shut, which none can pass
texts.2.777: Without my op'ning. Pensive here I sat
texts.2.778: Alone, but long I sat not, till my womb
texts.2.779: Pregnant by thee, and now excessive grown
texts.2.780: Prodigious motion felt and rueful throes.
texts.2.781: At last this odious offspring whom thou seest
texts.2.782: Thine own begotten, breaking violent way
texts.2.783: Tore through my entrails, that with fear and pain
texts.2.784: Distorted, all my nether shape thus grew
texts.2.785: Transform'd: but he my inbred enemie
texts.2.786: Forth issu'd, brandishing his fatal Dart
texts.2.787: Made to destroy: I fled, and cry'd out DEATH;
texts.2.788: Hell trembl'd at the hideous Name, and sigh'd
texts.2.789: From all her Caves, and back resounded DEATH.
texts.2.790: I fled, but he pursu'd (though more, it seems,
texts.2.791: Inflam'd with lust then rage) and swifter far,
texts.2.792: Me overtook his mother all dismaid,
texts.2.793: And in embraces forcible and foule
texts.2.794: Ingendring with me, of that rape begot
texts.2.795: These yelling Monsters that with ceasless cry
texts.2.796: Surround me, as thou sawst, hourly conceiv'd
texts.2.797: And hourly born, with sorrow infinite
texts.2.798: To me, for when they list into the womb
texts.2.799: That bred them they return, and howle and gnaw
texts.2.800: My Bowels, their repast; then bursting forth
texts.2.801: Afresh with conscious terrours vex me round,
texts.2.802: That rest or intermission none I find.
texts.2.803: Before mine eyes in opposition sits
texts.2.804: Grim DEATH my Son and foe, who sets them on,
texts.2.805: And me his Parent would full soon devour
texts.2.806: For want of other prey, but that he knows
texts.2.807: His end with mine involvd; and knows that I
texts.2.808: Should prove a bitter Morsel, and his bane,
texts.2.809: When ever that shall be; so Fate pronounc'd.
texts.2.810: But thou O Father, I forewarn thee, shun
texts.2.811: His deadly arrow; neither vainly hope
texts.2.812: To be invulnerable in those bright Arms,
texts.2.813: Though temper'd heav'nly, for that mortal dint,
texts.2.814: Save he who reigns above, none can resist.
texts.2.815: She finish'd, and the suttle Fiend his lore
texts.2.816: Soon learnd, now milder, and thus answerd smooth.
texts.2.817: Dear Daughter, since thou claim'st me for thy Sire,
texts.2.818: And my fair Son here showst me, the dear pledge
texts.2.819: Of dalliance had with thee in Heav'n, and joys
texts.2.820: Then sweet, now sad to mention, through dire change
texts.2.821: Befalln us unforeseen, unthought of, know
texts.2.822: I come no enemie, but to set free
texts.2.823: From out this dark and dismal house of pain,
texts.2.824: Both him and thee, and all the heav'nly Host
texts.2.825: Of Spirits that in our just pretenses arm'd
texts.2.826: Fell with us from on high: from them I go
texts.2.827: This uncouth errand sole, and one for all
texts.2.828: My self expose, with lonely steps to tread
texts.2.829: Th' unfounded deep, through the void immense
texts.2.830: To search with wandring quest a place foretold
texts.2.831: Should be, and, by concurring signs, ere now
texts.2.832: Created vast and round, a place of bliss
texts.2.833: In the Pourlieues of Heav'n, and therein plac't
texts.2.834: A race of upstart Creatures, to supply
texts.2.835: Perhaps our vacant room, though more remov'd,
texts.2.836: Least Heav'n surcharg'd with potent multitude
texts.2.837: Might hap to move new broiles: Be this or aught
texts.2.838: Then this more secret now design'd, I haste
texts.2.839: To know, and this once known, shall soon return,
texts.2.840: And bring ye to the place where Thou and Death
texts.2.841: Shall dwell at ease, and up and down unseen
texts.2.842: Wing silently the buxom Air, imbalm'd
texts.2.843: With odours; there ye shall be fed and fill'd
texts.2.844: Immeasurably, all things shall be your prey.
texts.2.845: He ceas'd, for both seemd highly pleasd, and Death
texts.2.846: Grinnd horrible a gastly smile, to hear
texts.2.847: His famine should be fill'd, and blest his mawe
texts.2.848: Destin'd to that good hour: no less rejoyc'd
texts.2.849: His mother bad, and thus bespake her Sire.
texts.2.850: The key of this infernal Pit by due,
texts.2.851: And by command of Heav'ns all-powerful King
texts.2.852: I keep, by him forbidden to unlock
texts.2.853: These Adamantine Gates; against all force
texts.2.854: Death ready stands to interpose his dart,
texts.2.855: Fearless to be o'rematcht by living might.
texts.2.856: But what ow I to his commands above
texts.2.857: Who hates me, and hath hither thrust me down
texts.2.858: Into this gloom of TARTARUS profound,
texts.2.859: To sit in hateful Office here confin'd,
texts.2.861: Here in perpetual agonie and pain,
texts.2.862: With terrors and with clamors compasst round
texts.2.863: Of mine own brood, that on my bowels feed:
texts.2.864: Thou art my Father, thou my Author, thou
texts.2.865: My being gav'st me; whom should I obey
texts.2.866: But thee, whom follow? thou wilt bring me soon
texts.2.867: To that new world of light and bliss, among
texts.2.868: The Gods who live at ease, where I shall Reign
texts.2.869: At thy right hand voluptuous, as beseems
texts.2.870: Thy daughter and thy darling, without end.
texts.2.871: Thus saying, from her side the fatal Key,
texts.2.872: Sad instrument of all our woe, she took;
texts.2.873: And towards the Gate rouling her bestial train,
texts.2.874: Forthwith the huge Porcullis high up drew,
texts.2.875: Which but her self not all the STYGIAN powers
texts.2.876: Could once have mov'd; then in the key-hole turns
texts.2.877: Th' intricate wards, and every Bolt and Bar
texts.2.878: Of massie Iron or sollid Rock with ease
texts.2.879: Unfast'ns: on a sudden op'n flie
texts.2.880: With impetuous recoile and jarring sound
texts.2.881: Th' infernal dores, and on thir hinges great
texts.2.882: Harsh Thunder, that the lowest bottom shook
texts.2.883: Of EREBUS. She op'nd, but to shut
texts.2.884: Excel'd her power; the Gates wide op'n stood,
texts.2.885: That with extended wings a Bannerd Host
texts.2.886: Under spread Ensigns marching might pass through
texts.2.887: With Horse and Chariots rankt in loose array;
texts.2.888: So wide they stood, and like a Furnace mouth
texts.2.889: Cast forth redounding smoak and ruddy flame.
texts.2.890: Before thir eyes in sudden view appear
texts.2.891: The secrets of the hoarie deep, a dark
texts.2.893: Without dimension, where length, breadth, and highth,
texts.2.894: And time and place are lost; where eldest Night
texts.2.895: And CHAOS, Ancestors of Nature, hold
texts.2.897: Of endless warrs and by confusion stand.
texts.2.898: For hot, cold, moist, and dry, four Champions fierce
texts.2.899: Strive here for Maistrie, and to Battel bring
texts.2.900: Thir embryon Atoms; they around the flag
texts.2.901: Of each his faction, in thir several Clanns,
texts.2.902: Light-arm'd or heavy, sharp, smooth, swift or slow,
texts.2.903: Swarm populous, unnumber'd as the Sands
texts.2.904: Of BARCA or CYRENE'S torrid soil,
texts.2.905: Levied to side with warring Winds, and poise
texts.2.906: Thir lighter wings. To whom these most adhere,
texts.2.907: Hee rules a moment; CHAOS Umpire sits,
texts.2.908: And by decision more imbroiles the fray
texts.2.909: By which he Reigns: next him high Arbiter
texts.2.910: CHANCE governs all. Into this wilde Abyss,
texts.2.911: The Womb of nature and perhaps her Grave,
texts.2.912: Of neither Sea, nor Shore, nor Air, nor Fire,
texts.2.913: But all these in thir pregnant causes mixt
texts.2.914: Confus'dly, and which thus must ever fight,
texts.2.915: Unless th' Almighty Maker them ordain
texts.2.916: His dark materials to create more Worlds,
texts.2.917: Into this wilde Abyss the warie fiend
texts.2.918: Stood on the brink of Hell and look'd a while,
texts.2.919: Pondering his Voyage; for no narrow frith
texts.2.920: He had to cross. Nor was his eare less peal'd
texts.2.921: With noises loud and ruinous (to compare
texts.2.922: Great things with small) then when BELLONA storms,
texts.2.923: With all her battering Engines bent to rase
texts.2.924: Som Capital City, or less then if this frame
texts.2.925: Of Heav'n were falling, and these Elements
texts.2.926: In mutinie had from her Axle torn
texts.2.927: The stedfast Earth. At last his Sail-broad Vannes
texts.2.928: He spreads for flight, and in the surging smoak
texts.2.929: Uplifted spurns the ground, thence many a League
texts.2.930: As in a cloudy Chair ascending rides
texts.2.931: Audacious, but that seat soon failing, meets
texts.2.933: Fluttring his pennons vain plumb down he drops
texts.2.934: Ten thousand fadom deep, and to this hour
texts.2.935: Down had been falling, had not by ill chance
texts.2.936: The strong rebuff of som tumultuous cloud
texts.2.937: Instinct with Fire and Nitre hurried him
texts.2.938: As many miles aloft: that furie stay'd,
texts.2.939: Quencht in a Boggie SYRTIS, neither Sea,
texts.2.940: Nor good dry Land: nigh founderd on he fares,
texts.2.941: Treading the crude consistence, half on foot,
texts.2.942: Half flying; behoves him now both Oare and Saile.
texts.2.943: As when a Gryfon through the Wilderness
texts.2.944: With winged course ore Hill or moarie Dale,
texts.2.945: Pursues the ARIMASPIAN, who by stelth
texts.2.946: Had from his wakeful custody purloind
texts.2.947: The guarded Gold: So eagerly the fiend
texts.2.948: Ore bog or steep, through strait, rough, dense, or rare,
texts.2.949: With head, hands, wings, or feet pursues his way,
texts.2.950: And swims or sinks, or wades, or creeps, or flyes:
texts.2.951: At length a universal hubbub wilde
texts.2.952: Of stunning sounds and voices all confus'd
texts.2.953: Born through the hollow dark assaults his eare
texts.2.954: With loudest vehemence: thither he plyes,
texts.2.955: Undaunted to meet there what ever power
texts.2.956: Or Spirit of the nethermost Abyss
texts.2.957: Might in that noise reside, of whom to ask
texts.2.958: Which way the neerest coast of darkness lyes
texts.2.959: Bordering on light; when strait behold the Throne
texts.2.960: Of CHAOS, and his dark Pavilion spread
texts.2.961: Wide on the wasteful Deep; with him Enthron'd
texts.2.962: Sat Sable-vested Night, eldest of things,
texts.2.963: The consort of his Reign; and by them stood
texts.2.964: ORCUS and ADES, and the dreaded name
texts.2.965: Of DEMOGORGON; Rumor next and Chance,
texts.2.966: And Tumult and Confusion all imbroild,
texts.2.967: And Discord with a thousand various mouths.
texts.2.968: T' whom SATAN turning boldly, thus. Ye Powers
texts.2.969: And Spirits of this nethermost Abyss,
texts.2.970: CHAOS and ANCIENT NIGHT, I come no Spie,
texts.2.971: With purpose to explore or to disturb
texts.2.972: The secrets of your Realm, but by constraint
texts.2.973: Wandring this darksome desart, as my way
texts.2.974: Lies through your spacious Empire up to light,
texts.2.975: Alone, and without guide, half lost, I seek
texts.2.976: What readiest path leads where your gloomie bounds
texts.2.977: Confine with Heav'n; or if som other place
texts.2.978: From your Dominion won, th' Ethereal King
texts.2.980: I travel this profound, direct my course;
texts.2.981: Directed, no mean recompence it brings
texts.2.982: To your behoof, if I that Region lost,
texts.2.984: To her original darkness and your sway
texts.2.985: (Which is my present journey) and once more
texts.2.986: Erect the Standerd there of ANCIENT NIGHT;
texts.2.987: Yours be th' advantage all, mine the revenge.
texts.2.988: Thus SATAN; and him thus the Anarch old
texts.2.989: With faultring speech and visage incompos'd
texts.2.990: Answer'd. I know thee, stranger, who thou art,
texts.2.991: That mighty leading Angel, who of late
texts.2.992: Made head against Heav'ns King, though overthrown.
texts.2.993: I saw and heard, for such a numerous host
texts.2.994: Fled not in silence through the frighted deep
texts.2.995: With ruin upon ruin, rout on rout,
texts.2.996: Confusion worse confounded; and Heav'n Gates
texts.2.997: Pourd out by millions her victorious Bands
texts.2.998: Pursuing. I upon my Frontieres here
texts.2.999: Keep residence; if all I can will serve,
texts.2.1000: That little which is left so to defend
texts.2.1001: Encroacht on still through our intestine broiles
texts.2.1002: Weakning the Scepter of old Night: first Hell
texts.2.1003: Your dungeon stretching far and wide beneath;
texts.2.1004: Now lately Heaven and Earth, another World
texts.2.1005: Hung ore my Realm, link'd in a golden Chain
texts.2.1006: To that side Heav'n from whence your Legions fell:
texts.2.1007: If that way be your walk, you have not farr;
texts.2.1008: So much the neerer danger; goe and speed;
texts.2.1009: Havock and spoil and ruin are my gain.
texts.2.1010: He ceas'd; and SATAN staid not to reply,
texts.2.1011: But glad that now his Sea should find a shore,
texts.2.1012: With fresh alacritie and force renew'd
texts.2.1013: Springs upward like a Pyramid of fire
texts.2.1014: Into the wilde expanse, and through the shock
texts.2.1015: Of fighting Elements, on all sides round
texts.2.1016: Environ'd wins his way; harder beset
texts.2.1017: And more endanger'd, then when ARGO pass'd
texts.2.1018: Through BOSPORUS betwixt the justling Rocks:
texts.2.1019: Or when ULYSSES on the Larbord shunnd
texts.2.1020: CHARYBDIS, and by th' other whirlpool steard.
texts.2.1021: So he with difficulty and labour hard
texts.2.1022: Mov'd on, with difficulty and labour hee;
texts.2.1023: But hee once past, soon after when man fell,
texts.2.1024: Strange alteration! Sin and Death amain
texts.2.1025: Following his track, such was the will of Heav'n,
texts.2.1026: Pav'd after him a broad and beat'n way
texts.2.1027: Over the dark Abyss, whose boiling Gulf
texts.2.1028: Tamely endur'd a Bridge of wondrous length
texts.2.1029: From Hell continu'd reaching th' utmost Orbe
texts.2.1030: Of this frail World; by which the Spirits perverse
texts.2.1031: With easie intercourse pass to and fro
texts.2.1032: To tempt or punish mortals, except whom
texts.2.1033: God and good Angels guard by special grace.
texts.2.1034: But now at last the sacred influence
texts.2.1035: Of light appears, and from the walls of Heav'n
texts.2.1036: Shoots farr into the bosom of dim Night
texts.2.1037: A glimmering dawn; here Nature first begins
texts.2.1038: Her fardest verge, and CHAOS to retire
texts.2.1039: As from her outmost works a brok'n foe
texts.2.1040: With tumult less and with less hostile din,
texts.2.1041: That SATAN with less toil, and now with ease
texts.2.1042: Wafts on the calmer wave by dubious light
texts.2.1043: And like a weather-beaten Vessel holds
texts.2.1044: Gladly the Port, though Shrouds and Tackle torn;
texts.2.1045: Or in the emptier waste, resembling Air,
texts.2.1046: Weighs his spread wings, at leasure to behold
texts.2.1047: Farr off th' Empyreal Heav'n, extended wide
texts.2.1048: In circuit, undetermind square or round,
texts.2.1049: With Opal Towrs and Battlements adorn'd
texts.2.1050: Of living Saphire, once his native Seat;
texts.2.1051: And fast by hanging in a golden Chain
texts.2.1052: This pendant world, in bigness as a Starr
texts.2.1053: Of smallest Magnitude close by the Moon.
texts.2.1054: Thither full fraught with mischievous revenge,
texts.2.1055: Accurst, and in a cursed hour he hies.
texts.3.1: Hail holy light, ofspring of Heav'n first-born,
texts.3.2: Or of th' Eternal Coeternal beam
texts.3.3: May I express thee unblam'd? since God is light,
texts.3.4: And never but in unapproached light
texts.3.5: Dwelt from Eternitie, dwelt then in thee,

texts.4.941: Though for possession put to try once more
texts.4.942: What thou and thy gay Legions dare against;
texts.4.943: Whose easier business were to serve thir Lord
texts.4.944: High up in Heav'n, with songs to hymne his Throne,
texts.4.945: And practis'd distances to cringe, not fight.
texts.4.946: To whom the warriour Angel soon repli'd.
texts.4.947: To say and strait unsay, pretending first
texts.4.948: Wise to flie pain, professing next the Spie,
texts.4.949: Argues no Leader, but a lyar trac't,
texts.4.950: SATAN, and couldst thou faithful add? O name,
texts.4.951: O sacred name of faithfulness profan'd!
texts.4.952: Faithful to whom? to thy rebellious crew?
texts.4.953: Armie of Fiends, fit body to fit head;
texts.4.954: Was this your discipline and faith ingag'd,
texts.4.956: Allegeance to th' acknowledg'd Power supream?
texts.4.957: And thou sly hypocrite, who now wouldst seem
texts.4.958: Patron of liberty, who more then thou
texts.4.959: Once fawn'd, and cring'd, and servilly ador'd
texts.4.960: Heav'ns awful Monarch? wherefore but in hope
texts.4.961: To dispossess him, and thy self to reigne?
texts.4.962: But mark what I arreede thee now, avant;
texts.4.963: Flie thither whence thou fledst: if from this houre
texts.4.964: Within these hallowd limits thou appeer,
texts.4.965: Back to th' infernal pit I drag thee chaind,
texts.4.966: And Seale thee so, as henceforth not to scorne
texts.4.967: The facil gates of hell too slightly barrd.
texts.4.968: So threatn'd hee, but SATAN to no threats
texts.4.969: Gave heed, but waxing more in rage repli'd.
texts.4.970: Then when I am thy captive talk of chaines,
texts.4.971: Proud limitarie Cherube, but ere then
texts.4.972: Farr heavier load thy self expect to feel
texts.4.973: From my prevailing arme, though Heavens King
texts.4.974: Ride on thy wings, and thou with thy Compeers,
texts.4.975: Us'd to the yoak, draw'st his triumphant wheels
texts.4.976: In progress through the rode of Heav'n Star-pav'd.
texts.4.977: While thus he spake, th' Angelic Squadron bright
texts.4.978: Turnd fierie red, sharpning in mooned hornes
texts.4.979: Thir Phalanx, and began to hemm him round
texts.4.980: With ported Spears, as thick as when a field
texts.4.981: Of CERES ripe for harvest waving bends
texts.4.982: Her bearded Grove of ears, which way the wind
texts.4.983: Swayes them; the careful Plowman doubting stands
texts.4.984: Least on the threshing floore his hopeful sheaves
texts.4.985: Prove chaff. On th' other side SATAN allarm'd
texts.4.986: Collecting all his might dilated stood,
texts.4.988: His stature reacht the Skie, and on his Crest
texts.4.989: Sat horror Plum'd; nor wanted in his graspe
texts.4.990: What seemd both Spear and Shield: now dreadful deeds
texts.4.991: Might have ensu'd, nor onely Paradise
texts.4.992: In this commotion, but the Starrie Cope
texts.4.993: Of Heav'n perhaps, or all the Elements
texts.4.994: At least had gon to rack, disturbd and torne
texts.4.995: With violence of this conflict, had not soon
texts.4.996: Th' Eternal to prevent such horrid fray
texts.4.997: Hung forth in Heav'n his golden Scales, yet seen
texts.4.998: Betwixt ASTREA and the SCORPION signe,
texts.4.999: Wherein all things created first he weighd,
texts.4.1000: The pendulous round Earth with ballanc't Aire
texts.4.1001: In counterpoise, now ponders all events,
texts.4.1002: Battels and Realms: in these he put two weights
texts.4.1003: The sequel each of parting and of fight;
texts.4.1004: The latter quick up flew, and kickt the beam;
texts.4.1005: Which GABRIEL spying, thus bespake the Fiend.
texts.4.1006: SATAN, I know thy strength, and thou knowst mine,
texts.4.1007: Neither our own but giv'n; what follie then
texts.4.1008: To boast what Arms can doe, since thine no more
texts.4.1009: Then Heav'n permits, nor mine, though doubld now
texts.4.1010: To trample thee as mire: for proof look up,
texts.4.1011: And read thy Lot in yon celestial Sign
texts.4.1012: Where thou art weigh'd, shown how light, how weak,
texts.4.1013: If thou resist. The Fiend lookt up and knew
texts.4.1014: His mounted scale aloft: nor more; but fled
texts.4.1015: Murmuring, and with him fled the shades of night.
texts.5.1: Now Morn her rosie steps in th' Eastern Clime
texts.5.2: Advancing, sow'd the Earth with Orient Pearle,
texts.5.3: When ADAM wak't, so customd, for his sleep
texts.5.4: Was Aerie light, from pure digestion bred,
texts.5.5: And temperat vapors bland, which th' only sound
texts.5.6: Of leaves and fuming rills, AURORA's fan,
texts.5.7: Lightly dispers'd, and the shrill Matin Song
texts.5.8: Of Birds on every bough; so much the more
texts.5.9: His wonder was to find unwak'nd EVE
texts.5.10: With Tresses discompos'd, and glowing Cheek,
texts.5.11: As through unquiet rest: he on his side
texts.5.12: Leaning half-rais'd, with looks of cordial Love
texts.5.13: Hung over her enamour'd, and beheld
texts.5.14: Beautie, which whether waking or asleep,
texts.5.15: Shot forth peculiar Graces; then with voice
texts.5.16: Milde, as when ZEPHYRUS on FLORA breathes,
texts.5.17: Her hand soft touching, whisperd thus. Awake
texts.5.18: My fairest, my espous'd, my latest found,
texts.5.19: Heav'ns last best gift, my ever new delight,
texts.5.20: Awake, the morning shines, and the fresh field
texts.5.21: Calls us, we lose the prime, to mark how spring
texts.5.22: Our tended Plants, how blows the Citron Grove,
texts.5.23: What drops the Myrrhe, what the balmie Reed,
texts.5.24: How Nature paints her colours, how the Bee
texts.5.25: Sits on the Bloom extracting liquid sweet.
texts.5.26: Such whispering wak'd her, but with startl'd eye
texts.5.27: On ADAM, whom imbracing, thus she spake.
texts.5.28: O Sole in whom my thoughts find all repose,
texts.5.29: My Glorie, my Perfection, glad I see
texts.5.30: Thy face, and Morn return'd, for I this Night,
texts.5.31: Such night till this I never pass'd, have dream'd,
texts.5.32: If dream'd, not as I oft am wont, of thee,
texts.5.33: Works of day pass't, or morrows next designe,
texts.5.34: But of offence and trouble, which my mind
texts.5.35: Knew never till this irksom night; methought
texts.5.36: Close at mine ear one call'd me forth to walk
texts.5.37: With gentle voice, I thought it thine; it said,
texts.5.38: Why sleepst thou EVE? now is the pleasant time,
texts.5.39: The cool, the silent, save where silence yields
texts.5.40: To the night-warbling Bird, that now awake
texts.5.41: Tunes sweetest his love-labor'd song; now reignes
texts.5.42: Full Orb'd the Moon, and with more pleasing light
texts.5.43: Shadowie sets off the face of things; in vain,
texts.5.44: If none regard; Heav'n wakes with all his eyes,
texts.5.45: Whom to behold but thee, Natures desire,
texts.5.46: In whose sight all things joy, with ravishment
texts.5.47: Attracted by thy beauty still to gaze.
texts.5.48: I rose as at thy call, but found thee not;
texts.5.49: To find thee I directed then my walk;
texts.5.50: And on, methought, alone I pass'd through ways
texts.5.51: That brought me on a sudden to the Tree
texts.5.52: Of interdicted Knowledge: fair it seem'd,
texts.5.53: Much fairer to my Fancie then by day:
texts.5.54: And as I wondring lookt, beside it stood
texts.5.55: One shap'd wing'd like one of those from Heav'n
texts.5.56: By us oft seen; his dewie locks distill'd
texts.5.57: Ambrosia; on that Tree he also gaz'd;
texts.5.58: And O fair Plant, said he, with fruit surcharg'd,
texts.5.59: Deigns none to ease thy load and taste thy sweet,
texts.5.60: Nor God, nor Man; is Knowledge so despis'd?
texts.5.61: Or envie, or what reserve forbids to taste?
texts.5.62: Forbid who will, none shall from me withhold
texts.5.63: Longer thy offerd good, why else set here?
texts.5.64: This said he paus'd not, but with ventrous Arme
texts.5.65: He pluckt, he tasted; mee damp horror chil'd
texts.5.66: At such bold words voucht with a deed so bold:
texts.5.67: But he thus overjoy'd, O Fruit Divine,
texts.5.68: Sweet of thy self, but much more sweet thus cropt,
texts.5.69: Forbidd'n here, it seems, as onely fit
texts.5.70: For Gods, yet able to make Gods of Men:
texts.5.71: And why not Gods of Men, since good, the more
texts.5.73: The Author not impair'd, but honourd more?
texts.5.74: Here, happie Creature, fair Angelic EVE,
texts.5.75: Partake thou also; happie though thou art,
texts.5.76: Happier thou mayst be, worthier canst not be:
texts.5.77: Taste this, and be henceforth among the Gods
texts.5.78: Thy self a Goddess, not to Earth confind,
texts.5.79: But somtimes in the Air, as wee, somtimes
texts.5.80: Ascend to Heav'n, by merit thine, and see
texts.5.81: What life the Gods live there, and such live thou.
texts.5.82: So saying, he drew nigh, and to me held,
texts.5.83: Even to my mouth of that same fruit held part
texts.5.84: Which he had pluckt; the pleasant savourie smell
texts.5.85: So quick'nd appetite, that I, methought,
texts.5.86: Could not but taste. Forthwith up to the Clouds
texts.5.87: With him I flew, and underneath beheld
texts.5.88: The Earth outstretcht immense, a prospect wide
texts.5.89: And various: wondring at my flight and change
texts.5.91: My Guide was gon, and I, me thought, sunk down,
texts.5.92: And fell asleep; but O how glad I wak'd
texts.5.93: To find this but a dream! Thus EVE her Night
texts.5.94: Related, and thus ADAM answerd sad.
texts.5.95: Best Image of my self and dearer half,
texts.5.96: The trouble of thy thoughts this night in sleep
texts.5.97: Affects me equally; nor can I like
texts.5.98: This uncouth dream, of evil sprung I fear;
texts.5.99: Yet evil whence? in thee can harbour none,
texts.5.100: Created pure. But know that in the Soule
texts.5.101: Are many lesser Faculties that serve
texts.5.102: Reason as chief; among these Fansie next
texts.5.103: Her office holds; of all external things,
texts.5.104: Which the five watchful Senses represent,
texts.5.106: Which Reason joyning or disjoyning, frames
texts.5.107: All what we affirm or what deny, and call
texts.5.108: Our knowledge or opinion; then retires
texts.5.109: Into her private Cell when Nature rests.
texts.5.110: Oft in her absence mimic Fansie wakes
texts.5.111: To imitate her; but misjoyning shapes,
texts.5.112: Wilde work produces oft, and most in dreams,
texts.5.113: Ill matching words and deeds long past or late.
texts.5.114: Som such resemblances methinks I find
texts.5.115: Of our last Eevnings talk, in this thy dream,
texts.5.116: But with addition strange; yet be not sad.
texts.5.117: Evil into the mind of God or Man
texts.5.118: May come and go, so unapprov'd, and leave
texts.5.119: No spot or blame behind: Which gives me hope
texts.5.120: That what in sleep thou didst abhorr to dream,
texts.5.121: Waking thou never wilt consent to do.
texts.5.122: Be not disheart'nd then, nor cloud those looks
texts.5.123: That wont to be more chearful and serene
texts.5.124: Then when fair Morning first smiles on the World,
texts.5.125: And let us to our fresh imployments rise
texts.5.126: Among the Groves, the Fountains, and the Flours
texts.5.127: That open now thir choicest bosom'd smells
texts.5.128: Reservd from night, and kept for thee in store.
texts.5.129: So cheard he his fair Spouse, and she was cheard,
texts.5.130: But silently a gentle tear let fall
texts.5.131: From either eye, and wip'd them with her haire;
texts.5.132: Two other precious drops that ready stood,
texts.5.133: Each in thir chrystal sluce, hee ere they fell
texts.5.134: Kiss'd as the gracious signs of sweet remorse
texts.5.135: And pious awe, that feard to have offended.
texts.5.136: So all was cleard, and to the Field they haste.
texts.5.137: But first from under shadie arborous roof,
texts.5.138: Soon as they forth were come to open sight
texts.5.139: Of day-spring, and the Sun, who scarce up risen
texts.5.140: With wheels yet hov'ring o're the Ocean brim,
texts.5.141: Shot paralel to the earth his dewie ray,
texts.5.142: Discovering in wide Lantskip all the East
texts.5.143: Of Paradise and EDENS happie Plains,
texts.5.144: Lowly they bow'd adoring, and began
texts.5.145: Thir Orisons, each Morning duly paid
texts.5.146: In various style, for neither various style
texts.5.147: Nor holy rapture wanted they to praise
texts.5.148: Thir Maker, in fit strains pronounc't or sung
texts.5.150: Flowd from thir lips, in Prose or numerous Verse,
texts.5.151: More tuneable then needed Lute or Harp
texts.5.152: To add more sweetness, and they thus began.
texts.5.153: These are thy glorious works, Parent of good,
texts.5.155: Thus wondrous fair; thy self how wondrous then!
texts.5.156: Unspeakable, who sitst above these Heavens
texts.5.157: To us invisible or dimly seen
texts.5.158: In these thy lowest works, yet these declare
texts.5.159: Thy goodness beyond thought, and Power Divine:
texts.5.160: Speak yee who best can tell, ye Sons of light,
texts.5.161: Angels, for yee behold him, and with songs
texts.5.162: And choral symphonies, Day without Night,
texts.5.163: Circle his Throne rejoycing, yee in Heav'n,
texts.5.164: On Earth joyn all yee Creatures to extoll
texts.5.165: Him first, him last, him midst, and without end.
texts.5.166: Fairest of Starrs, last in the train of Night,
texts.5.167: If better thou belong not to the dawn,
texts.5.168: Sure pledge of day, that crownst the smiling Morn
texts.5.169: With thy bright Circlet, praise him in thy Spheare
texts.5.170: While day arises, that sweet hour of Prime.
texts.5.171: Thou Sun, of this great World both Eye and Soule,
texts.5.172: Acknowledge him thy Greater, sound his praise
texts.5.173: In thy eternal course, both when thou climb'st,
texts.5.174: And when high Noon hast gaind, when thou fallst.
texts.5.175: Moon, that now meetst the orient Sun, now fli'st
texts.5.176: With the fixt Starrs, fixt in thir Orb that flies,
texts.5.177: And yee five other wandring Fires that move
texts.5.178: In mystic Dance not without Song, resound
texts.5.179: His praise, who out of Darkness call'd up Light.
texts.5.180: Aire, and ye Elements the eldest birth
texts.5.181: Of Natures Womb, that in quaternion run
texts.5.183: And nourish all things, let your ceasless change
texts.5.184: Varie to our great Maker still new praise.
texts.5.185: Ye Mists and Exhalations that now rise
texts.5.186: From Hill or steaming Lake, duskie or grey,
texts.5.187: Till the Sun paint your fleecie skirts with Gold,
texts.5.188: In honour to the Worlds great Author rise,
texts.5.189: Whether to deck with Clouds the uncolourd skie,
texts.5.190: Or wet the thirstie Earth with falling showers,
texts.5.191: Rising or falling still advance his praise.
texts.5.192: His praise ye Winds, that from four Quarters blow,
texts.5.193: Breath soft or loud; and wave your tops, ye Pines,
texts.5.194: With every Plant, in sign of Worship wave.
texts.5.195: Fountains and yee, that warble, as ye flow,
texts.5.196: Melodious murmurs, warbling tune his praise.
texts.5.197: Joyn voices all ye living Souls, ye Birds,
texts.5.198: That singing up to Heaven Gate ascend,
texts.5.199: Bear on your wings and in your notes his praise;
texts.5.200: Yee that in Waters glide, and yee that walk
texts.5.201: The Earth, and stately tread, or lowly creep;
texts.5.202: Witness if I be silent, Morn or Eeven,
texts.5.203: To Hill, or Valley, Fountain, or fresh shade
texts.5.204: Made vocal by my Song, and taught his praise.
texts.5.205: Hail universal Lord, be bounteous still
texts.5.206: To give us onely good; and if the night
texts.5.207: Have gathered aught of evil or conceald,
texts.5.208: Disperse it, as now light dispels the dark.
texts.5.209: So pray'd they innocent, and to thir thoughts
texts.5.210: Firm peace recoverd soon and wonted calm.
texts.5.211: On to thir mornings rural work they haste
texts.5.212: Among sweet dewes and flours; where any row
texts.5.213: Of Fruit-trees overwoodie reachd too farr
texts.5.214: Thir pamperd boughes, and needed hands to check
texts.5.215: Fruitless imbraces: or they led the Vine
texts.5.216: To wed her Elm; she spous'd about him twines
texts.5.217: Her mariageable arms, and with her brings
texts.5.218: Her dowr th' adopted Clusters, to adorn
texts.5.219: His barren leaves. Them thus imploid beheld
texts.5.220: With pittie Heav'ns high King, and to him call'd
texts.5.221: RAPHAEL, the sociable Spirit, that deign'd
texts.5.222: To travel with TOBIAS, and secur'd
texts.5.223: His marriage with the seaventimes-wedded Maid.
texts.5.224: RAPHAEL, said hee, thou hear'st what stir on Earth
texts.5.225: SATAN from Hell scap't through the darksom Gulf
texts.5.226: Hath raisd in Paradise, and how disturbd
texts.5.227: This night the human pair, how he designes
texts.5.228: In them at once to ruin all mankind.
texts.5.229: Go therefore, half this day as friend with friend
texts.5.230: Converse with ADAM, in what Bowre or shade
texts.5.231: Thou find'st him from the heat of Noon retir'd,
texts.5.232: To respit his day-labour with repast,
texts.5.233: Or with repose; and such discourse bring on,
texts.5.234: As may advise him of his happie state,
texts.5.235: Happiness in his power left free to will,
texts.5.236: Left to his own free Will, his Will though free,
texts.5.237: Yet mutable; whence warne him to beware
texts.5.238: He swerve not too secure: tell him withall
texts.5.239: His danger, and from whom, what enemie
texts.5.240: Late falln himself from Heav'n, is plotting now
texts.5.241: The fall of others from like state of bliss;
texts.5.242: By violence, no, for that shall be withstood,
texts.5.243: But by deceit and lies; this let him know,
texts.5.246: So spake th' Eternal Father, and fulfilld
texts.5.247: All Justice: nor delaid the winged Saint
texts.5.248: After his charge receivd, but from among
texts.5.249: Thousand Celestial Ardors, where he stood
texts.5.250: Vaild with his gorgeous wings, up springing light
texts.5.251: Flew through the midst of Heav'n; th' angelic Quires
texts.5.252: On each hand parting, to his speed gave way
texts.5.253: Through all th' Empyreal road; till at the Gate
texts.5.254: Of Heav'n arriv'd, the gate self-opend wide
texts.5.255: On golden Hinges turning, as by work
texts.5.256: Divine the sov'ran Architect had fram'd.
texts.5.257: From hence, no cloud, or, to obstruct his sight,
texts.5.258: Starr interpos'd, however small he sees,
texts.5.259: Not unconform to other shining Globes,
texts.5.260: Earth and the Gard'n of God, with Cedars crownd
texts.5.261: Above all Hills. As when by night the Glass
texts.5.263: Imagind Lands and Regions in the Moon:
texts.5.264: Or Pilot from amidst the CYCLADES
texts.5.265: DELOS or SAMOS first appeering kenns
texts.5.266: A cloudy spot. Down thither prone in flight
texts.5.267: He speeds, and through the vast Ethereal Skie
texts.5.268: Sailes between worlds worlds, with steddie wing
texts.5.269: Now on the polar windes, then with quick Fann
texts.5.270: Winnows the buxom Air; till within soare
texts.5.271: Of Towring Eagles, to all the Fowles he seems
texts.5.272: A PHOENIX, gaz'd by all, as that sole Bird
texts.5.273: When to enshrine his reliques in the Sun's
texts.5.274: Bright Temple, to AEGYPTIAN THEB'S he flies.
texts.5.275: At once on th' Eastern cliff of Paradise
texts.5.276: He lights, and to his proper shape returns
texts.5.277: A Seraph wingd; six wings he wore, to shade
texts.5.278: His lineaments Divine; the pair that clad
texts.5.279: Each shoulder broad, came mantling o're his brest
texts.5.280: With regal Ornament; the middle pair
texts.5.281: Girt like a Starrie Zone his waste, and round
texts.5.282: Skirted his loines and thighes with downie Gold
texts.5.283: And colours dipt in Heav'n; the third his feet
texts.5.284: Shaddowd from either heele with featherd maile
texts.5.285: Skie-tinctur'd grain. Like MAIA'S son he stood,
texts.5.286: And shook his Plumes, that Heav'nly fragrance filld
texts.5.287: The circuit wide. Strait knew him all the bands
texts.5.288: Of Angels under watch; and to his state,
texts.5.289: And to his message high in honour rise;
texts.5.290: For on som message high they guessd him bound.
texts.5.291: Thir glittering Tents he passd, and now is come
texts.5.292: Into the blissful field, through Groves of Myrrhe,
texts.5.293: And flouring Odours, Cassia, Nard, and Balme;
texts.5.294: A Wilderness of sweets; for Nature here
texts.5.295: Wantond as in her prime, and plaid at will
texts.5.296: Her Virgin Fancies, pouring forth more sweet,
texts.5.297: Wilde above rule or art; enormous bliss.
texts.5.298: Him through the spicie Forrest onward com
texts.5.299: ADAM discernd, as in the dore he sat
texts.5.300: Of his coole Bowre, while now the mounted Sun
texts.5.301: Shot down direct his fervid Raies, to warme
texts.5.302: Earths inmost womb, more warmth then ADAM need;
texts.5.303: And EVE within, due at her hour prepar'd
texts.5.304: For dinner savourie fruits, of taste to please
texts.5.305: True appetite, and not disrelish thirst
texts.5.306: Of nectarous draughts between, from milkie stream,
texts.5.307: Berrie or Grape: to whom thus ADAM call'd.
texts.5.308: Haste hither EVE, and worth thy sight behold
texts.5.309: Eastward among those Trees, what glorious shape
texts.5.310: Comes this way moving; seems another Morn
texts.5.311: Ris'n on mid-noon; som great behest from Heav'n
texts.5.312: To us perhaps he brings, and will voutsafe
texts.5.313: This day to be our Guest. But goe with speed,
texts.5.314: And what thy stores contain, bring forth and poure
texts.5.315: Abundance, fit to honour and receive
texts.5.316: Our Heav'nly stranger; well we may afford
texts.5.317: Our givers thir own gifts, and large bestow
texts.5.318: From large bestowd, where Nature multiplies
texts.5.319: Her fertil growth, and by disburd'ning grows
texts.5.320: More fruitful, which instructs us not to spare.
texts.5.321: To whom thus EVE. ADAM, earths hallowd mould,
texts.5.322: Of God inspir'd, small store will serve, where store,
texts.5.323: All seasons, ripe for use hangs on the stalk;
texts.5.324: Save what by frugal storing firmness gains
texts.5.325: To nourish, and superfluous moist consumes:
