texts.5.764: For thither he assembl'd all his Train,
texts.5.766: About the great reception of thir King,
texts.5.767: Thither to come, and with calumnious Art
texts.5.768: Of counterfeted truth thus held thir ears.
texts.5.770: If these magnific Titles yet remain
texts.5.771: Not meerly titular, since by Decree
texts.5.772: Another now hath to himself ingross't
texts.5.773: All Power, and us eclipst under the name
texts.5.774: Of King anointed, for whom all this haste
texts.5.775: Of midnight march, and hurried meeting here,
texts.5.776: This onely to consult how we may best
texts.5.777: With what may be devis'd of honours new
texts.5.778: Receive him coming to receive from us
texts.5.780: Too much to one, but double how endur'd,
texts.5.781: To one and to his image now proclaim'd?
texts.5.782: But what if better counsels might erect
texts.5.783: Our minds and teach us to cast off this Yoke?
texts.5.784: Will ye submit your necks, and chuse to bend
texts.5.785: The supple knee? ye will not, if I trust
texts.5.786: To know ye right, or if ye know your selves
texts.5.787: Natives and Sons of Heav'n possest before
texts.5.788: By none, and if not equal all, yet free,
texts.5.789: Equally free; for Orders and Degrees
texts.5.790: Jarr not with liberty, but well consist.
texts.5.791: Who can in reason then or right assume
texts.5.792: Monarchie over such as live by right
texts.5.793: His equals, if in power and splendor less,
texts.5.794: In freedome equal? or can introduce
texts.5.795: Law and Edict on us, who without law
texts.5.796: Erre not, much less for this to be our Lord,
texts.5.797: And look for adoration to th' abuse
texts.5.798: Of those Imperial Titles which assert
texts.5.799: Our being ordain'd to govern, not to serve?
texts.5.800: Thus farr his bold discourse without controule
texts.5.801: Had audience, when among the Seraphim
texts.5.802: ABDIEL, then whom none with more zeale ador'd
texts.5.803: The Deitie, and divine commands obei'd,
texts.5.804: Stood up, and in a flame of zeale severe
texts.5.805: The current of his fury thus oppos'd.
texts.5.806: O argument blasphemous, false and proud!
texts.5.807: Words which no eare ever to hear in Heav'n
texts.5.808: Expected, least of all from thee, ingrate
texts.5.809: In place thy self so high above thy Peeres.
texts.5.810: Canst thou with impious obloquie condemne
texts.5.811: The just Decree of God, pronounc't and sworn,
texts.5.812: That to his only Son by right endu'd
texts.5.813: With Regal Scepter, every Soule in Heav'n
texts.5.814: Shall bend the knee, and in that honour due
texts.5.815: Confess him rightful King? unjust thou saist
texts.5.816: Flatly unjust, to binde with Laws the free,
texts.5.817: And equal over equals to let Reigne,
texts.5.818: One over all with unsucceeded power.
texts.5.819: Shalt thou give Law to God, shalt thou dispute
texts.5.820: With him the points of libertie, who made
texts.5.821: Thee what thou art, formd the Pow'rs of Heav'n
texts.5.822: Such as he pleasd, and circumscrib'd thir being?
texts.5.823: Yet by experience taught we know how good,
texts.5.824: And of our good, and of our dignitie
texts.5.825: How provident he is, how farr from thought
texts.5.826: To make us less, bent rather to exalt
texts.5.827: Our happie state under one Head more neer
texts.5.828: United. But to grant it thee unjust,
texts.5.829: That equal over equals Monarch Reigne:
texts.5.830: Thy self though great glorious dost thou count,
texts.5.831: Or all Angelic Nature joind in one,
texts.5.832: Equal to him begotten Son, by whom
texts.5.833: As by his Word the mighty Father made
texts.5.834: All things, ev'n thee, and all the Spirits of Heav'n
texts.5.835: By him created in thir bright degrees,
texts.5.836: Crownd them with Glory, to thir Glory nam'd
texts.5.838: Essential Powers, nor by his Reign obscur'd,
texts.5.839: But more illustrious made, since he the Head
texts.5.840: One of our number thus reduc't becomes,
texts.5.841: His Laws our Laws, all honour to him done
texts.5.842: Returns our own. Cease then this impious rage,
texts.5.843: And tempt not these; but hast'n to appease
texts.5.844: Th' incensed Father, and th' incensed Son,
texts.5.845: While Pardon may be found in time besought.
texts.5.846: So spake the fervent Angel, but his zeale
texts.5.847: None seconded, as out of season judg'd,
texts.5.848: Or singular and rash, whereat rejoic'd
texts.5.849: Th' Apostat, and more haughty thus repli'd.
texts.5.850: That we were formd then saist thou? the work
texts.5.851: Of secondarie hands, by task transferd
texts.5.852: From Father to his Son? strange point and new!
texts.5.853: Doctrin which we would know whence learnt: who saw
texts.5.854: When this creation was? rememberst thou
texts.5.855: Thy making, while the Maker gave thee being?
texts.5.856: We know no time when we were not as now;
texts.5.857: Know none before us, self-begot, self-rais'd
texts.5.858: By our own quick'ning power, when fatal course
texts.5.859: Had circl'd his full Orbe, the birth mature
texts.5.860: Of this our native Heav'n, Ethereal Sons.
texts.5.861: Our puissance is our own, our own right hand
texts.5.862: Shall teach us highest deeds, by proof to try
texts.5.863: Who is our equal: then thou shalt behold
texts.5.865: Address, and to begirt th' Almighty Throne
texts.5.867: These tidings carrie to th' anointed King;
texts.5.868: And fly, ere evil intercept thy flight.
texts.5.869: He said, and as the sound of waters deep
texts.5.870: Hoarce murmur echo'd to his words applause
texts.5.871: Through the infinite Host, nor less for that
texts.5.872: The flaming Seraph fearless, though alone
texts.5.873: Encompass'd round with foes, thus answerd bold.
texts.5.874: O alienate from God, O spirit accurst,
texts.5.875: Forsak'n of all good; I see thy fall
texts.5.876: Determind, and thy hapless crew involv'd
texts.5.877: In this perfidious fraud, contagion spred
texts.5.878: Both of thy crime and punishment: henceforth
texts.5.879: No more be troubl'd how to quit the yoke
texts.5.880: Of Gods MESSIAH; those indulgent Laws
texts.5.881: Will not be now voutsaf't, other Decrees
texts.5.882: Against thee are gon forth without recall;
texts.5.883: That Golden Scepter which thou didst reject
texts.5.884: Is now an Iron Rod to bruise and breake
texts.5.885: Thy disobedience. Well thou didst advise,
texts.5.886: Yet not for thy advise or threats I fly
texts.5.887: These wicked Tents devoted, least the wrauth
texts.5.889: Distinguish not: for soon expect to feel
texts.5.890: His Thunder on thy head, devouring fire.
texts.5.891: Then who created thee lamenting learne,
texts.5.892: When who can uncreate thee thou shalt know.
texts.5.893: So spake the Seraph ABDIEL faithful found,
texts.5.894: Among the faithless, faithful only hee;
texts.5.897: His Loyaltie he kept, his Love, his Zeale;
texts.5.898: Nor number, nor example with him wrought
texts.5.899: To swerve from truth, or change his constant mind
texts.5.900: Though single. From amidst them forth he passd,
texts.5.901: Long way through hostile scorn, which he susteind
texts.5.902: Superior, nor of violence fear'd aught;
texts.5.903: And with retorted scorn his back he turn'd
texts.5.904: On those proud Towrs to swift destruction doom'd.
texts.6.1: All night the dreadless Angel unpursu'd
texts.6.2: Through Heav'ns wide Champain held his way, till Morn,
texts.6.3: Wak't by the circling Hours, with rosie hand
texts.6.4: Unbarr'd the gates of Light. There is a Cave
texts.6.5: Within the Mount of God, fast by his Throne,
texts.6.6: Where light and darkness in perpetual round
texts.6.7: Lodge and dislodge by turns, which makes through Heav'n
texts.6.8: Grateful vicissitude, like Day and Night;
texts.6.9: Light issues forth, and at the other dore
texts.6.10: Obsequious darkness enters, till her houre
texts.6.11: To veile the Heav'n, though darkness there might well
texts.6.12: Seem twilight here; and now went forth the Morn
texts.6.13: Such as in highest Heav'n, arrayd in Gold
texts.6.14: Empyreal, from before her vanisht Night,
texts.6.15: Shot through with orient Beams: when all the Plain
texts.6.16: Coverd with thick embatteld Squadrons bright,
texts.6.17: Chariots and flaming Armes, and fierie Steeds
texts.6.18: Reflecting blaze on blaze, first met his view:
texts.6.19: Warr he perceav'd, warr in procinct, and found
texts.6.20: Already known what he for news had thought
texts.6.21: To have reported: gladly then he mixt
texts.6.22: Among those friendly Powers who him receav'd
texts.6.23: With joy and acclamations loud, that one
texts.6.24: That of so many Myriads fall'n, yet one
texts.6.25: Returnd not lost: On to the sacred hill
texts.6.26: They led him high applauded, and present
texts.6.27: Before the seat supream; from whence a voice
texts.6.28: From midst a Golden Cloud thus milde was heard.
texts.6.29: Servant of God, well done, well hast thou fought
texts.6.30: The better fight, who single hast maintaind
texts.6.32: Of Truth, in word mightier then they in Armes;
texts.6.33: And for the testimonie of Truth hast born
texts.6.34: Universal reproach, far worse to beare
texts.6.35: Then violence: for this was all thy care
texts.6.36: To stand approv'd in sight of God, though Worlds
texts.6.37: Judg'd thee perverse: the easier conquest now
texts.6.38: Remains thee, aided by this host of friends,
texts.6.39: Back on thy foes more glorious to return
texts.6.40: Then scornd thou didst depart, and to subdue
texts.6.41: By force, who reason for thir Law refuse,
texts.6.42: Right reason for thir Law, and for thir King
texts.6.43: MESSIAH, who by right of merit Reigns.
texts.6.44: Goe MICHAEL of Celestial Armies Prince,
texts.6.45: And thou in Military prowess next
texts.6.46: GABRIEL, lead forth to Battel these my Sons
texts.6.47: Invincible, lead forth my armed Saints
texts.6.48: By Thousands and by Millions rang'd for fight;
texts.6.49: Equal in number to that Godless crew
texts.6.50: Rebellious, them with Fire and hostile Arms
texts.6.51: Fearless assault, and to the brow of Heav'n
texts.6.52: Pursuing drive them out from God and bliss,
texts.6.53: Into thir place of punishment, the Gulf
texts.6.54: Of TARTARUS, which ready opens wide
texts.6.55: His fiery CHAOS to receave thir fall.
texts.6.56: So spake the Sovran voice, and Clouds began
texts.6.57: To darken all the Hill, and smoak to rowl
texts.6.58: In duskie wreathes, reluctant flames, the signe
texts.6.59: Of wrauth awak't: nor with less dread the loud
texts.6.60: Ethereal Trumpet from on high gan blow:
texts.6.61: At which command the Powers Militant,
texts.6.62: That stood for Heav'n, in mighty Quadrate joyn'd
texts.6.64: In silence thir bright Legions, to the sound
texts.6.67: Under thir God-like Leaders, in the Cause
texts.6.68: Of God and his MESSIAH. On they move
texts.6.70: Nor streit'ning Vale, nor Wood, nor Stream divides
texts.6.71: Thir perfet ranks; for high above the ground
texts.6.72: Thir march was, and the passive Air upbore
texts.6.73: Thir nimble tread; as when the total kind
texts.6.74: Of Birds in orderly array on wing
texts.6.75: Came summond over EDEN to receive
texts.6.76: Thir names of thee; so over many a tract
texts.6.77: Of Heav'n they march'd, and many a Province wide
texts.6.78: Tenfold the length of this terrene: at last
texts.6.79: Farr in th' Horizon to the North appeer'd
texts.6.80: From skirt to skirt a fierie Region, stretcht
texts.6.81: In battailous aspect, and neerer view
texts.6.83: Of rigid Spears, and Helmets throng'd, and Shields
texts.6.85: The banded Powers of SATAN hasting on
texts.6.86: With furious expedition; for they weend
texts.6.87: That self same day by fight, or by surprize
texts.6.88: To win the Mount of God, and on his Throne
texts.6.89: To set the envier of his State, the proud
texts.6.90: Aspirer, but thir thoughts prov'd fond and vain
texts.6.91: In the mid way: though strange to us it seemd
texts.6.92: At first, that Angel should with Angel warr,
texts.6.93: And in fierce hosting meet, who wont to meet
texts.6.94: So oft in Festivals of joy and love
texts.6.95: Unanimous, as sons of one great Sire
texts.6.96: Hymning th' Eternal Father: but the shout
texts.6.97: Of Battel now began, and rushing sound
texts.6.98: Of onset ended soon each milder thought.
texts.6.99: High in the midst exalted as a God
texts.6.100: Th' Apostat in his Sun-bright Chariot sate
texts.6.102: With Flaming Cherubim, and golden Shields;
texts.6.103: Then lighted from his gorgeous Throne, for now
texts.6.104: 'Twixt Host and Host but narrow space was left,
texts.6.105: A dreadful interval, and Front to Front
texts.6.107: Of hideous length: before the cloudie Van,
texts.6.108: On the rough edge of battel ere it joyn'd,
texts.6.109: SATAN with vast and haughtie strides advanc't,
texts.6.110: Came towring, armd in Adamant and Gold;
texts.6.111: ABDIEL that sight endur'd not, where he stood
texts.6.112: Among the mightiest, bent on highest deeds,
texts.6.113: And thus his own undaunted heart explores.
texts.6.114: O Heav'n! that such resemblance of the Highest
texts.6.115: Should yet remain, where faith and realtie
texts.6.116: Remain not; wherfore should not strength might
texts.6.117: There fail where Vertue fails, or weakest prove
texts.6.118: Where boldest; though to sight unconquerable?
texts.6.119: His puissance, trusting in th' Almightie's aide,
texts.6.120: I mean to try, whose Reason I have tri'd
texts.6.121: Unsound and false; nor is it aught but just,
texts.6.122: That he who in debate of Truth hath won,
texts.6.123: Should win in Arms, in both disputes alike
texts.6.124: Victor; though brutish that contest and foule,
texts.6.125: When Reason hath to deal with force, yet so
texts.6.126: Most reason is that Reason overcome.
texts.6.127: So pondering, and from his armed Peers
texts.6.128: Forth stepping opposite, half way he met
texts.6.129: His daring foe, at this prevention more
texts.6.130: Incens't, and thus securely him defi'd.
texts.6.131: Proud, art thou met? thy hope was to have reacht
texts.6.132: The highth of thy aspiring unoppos'd,
texts.6.133: The Throne of God unguarded, and his side
texts.6.134: Abandond at the terror of thy Power
texts.6.135: Or potent tongue; fool, not to think how vain
texts.6.136: Against th' Omnipotent to rise in Arms;
texts.6.137: Who out of smallest things could without end
texts.6.138: Have rais'd incessant Armies to defeat
texts.6.139: Thy folly; or with solitarie hand
texts.6.140: Reaching beyond all limit, at one blow
texts.6.141: Unaided could have finisht thee, and whelmd
texts.6.142: Thy Legions under darkness; but thou seest
texts.6.143: All are not of thy Train; there be who Faith
texts.6.144: Prefer, and Pietie to God, though then
texts.6.145: To thee not visible, when I alone
texts.6.146: Seemd in thy World erroneous to dissent
texts.6.147: From all: my Sect thou seest, now learn too late
texts.6.148: How few somtimes may know, when thousands err.
texts.6.149: Whom the grand foe with scornful eye askance
texts.6.150: Thus answerd. Ill for thee, but in wisht houre
texts.6.151: Of my revenge, first sought for thou returnst
texts.6.152: From flight, seditious Angel, to receave
texts.6.153: Thy merited reward, the first assay
texts.6.154: Of this right hand provok't, since first that tongue
texts.6.156: A third part of the Gods, in Synod met
texts.6.157: Thir Deities to assert, who while they feel
texts.6.158: Vigour Divine within them, can allow
texts.6.159: Omnipotence to none. But well thou comst
texts.6.160: Before thy fellows, ambitious to win
texts.6.161: From me som Plume, that thy success may show
texts.6.162: Destruction to the rest: this pause between
texts.6.163: (Unanswerd least thou boast) to let thee know;
texts.6.164: At first I thought that Libertie and Heav'n
texts.6.165: To heav'nly Soules had bin all one; but now
texts.6.166: I see that most through sloth had rather serve,
texts.6.167: Ministring Spirits, traind up in Feast and Song;
texts.6.168: Such hast thou arm'd, the Minstrelsie of Heav'n,
texts.6.170: As both thir deeds compar'd this day shall prove.
texts.6.171: To whom in brief thus ABDIEL stern repli'd.
texts.6.172: Apostat, still thou errst, nor end wilt find
texts.6.173: Of erring, from the path of truth remote:
texts.6.174: Unjustly thou deprav'st it with the name
texts.6.175: Of SERVITUDE to serve whom God ordains,
texts.6.176: Or Nature; God and Nature bid the same,
texts.6.177: When he who rules is worthiest, and excells
texts.6.178: Them whom he governs. This is servitude,
texts.6.179: To serve th' unwise, or him who hath rebelld
texts.6.180: Against his worthier, as thine now serve thee,
texts.6.181: Thy self not free, but to thy self enthrall'd;
texts.6.182: Yet leudly dar'st our ministring upbraid.
texts.6.183: Reign thou in Hell thy Kingdom, let mee serve
texts.6.184: In Heav'n God ever blessed, and his Divine
texts.6.185: Behests obey, worthiest to be obey'd,
texts.6.186: Yet Chains in Hell, not Realms expect: mean while
texts.6.187: From mee returnd, as erst thou saidst, from flight,
texts.6.188: This greeting on thy impious Crest receive.
texts.6.189: So saying, a noble stroke he lifted high,
texts.6.190: Which hung not, but so swift with tempest fell
texts.6.191: On the proud Crest of SATAN, that no sight,
texts.6.192: Nor motion of swift thought, less could his Shield
texts.6.193: Such ruin intercept: ten paces huge
texts.6.194: He back recoild; the tenth on bended knee
texts.6.195: His massie Spear upstaid; as if on Earth
texts.6.196: Winds under ground or waters forcing way
texts.6.197: Sidelong, had push't a Mountain from his seat
texts.6.198: Half sunk with all his Pines. Amazement seis'd
texts.6.199: The Rebel Thrones, but greater rage to see
texts.6.200: Thus foil'd thir mightiest, ours joy filld, and shout,
texts.6.201: Presage of Victorie and fierce desire
texts.6.202: Of Battel: whereat MICHAEL bid sound
texts.6.203: Th' Arch-Angel trumpet; through the vast of Heav'n
texts.6.204: It sounded, and the faithful Armies rung
texts.6.205: HOSANNA to the Highest: nor stood at gaze
texts.6.206: The adverse Legions, nor less hideous joyn'd
texts.6.207: The horrid shock: now storming furie rose,
texts.6.208: And clamour such as heard in Heav'n till now
texts.6.209: Was never, Arms on Armour clashing bray'd
texts.6.210: Horrible discord, and the madding Wheeles

texts.6.216: Both Battels maine, with ruinous assault
texts.6.218: Resounded, and had Earth bin then, all Earth

texts.6.221: On either side, the least of whom could weild
texts.6.222: These Elements, and arm him with the force

texts.6.232: A Legion; led in fight, yet Leader seemd

texts.6.254: He hasted, and oppos'd the rockie Orb

texts.6.257: The great Arch-Angel from his warlike toile
texts.6.258: Surceas'd, and glad as hoping here to end

texts.6.261: And visage all enflam'd first thus began.
texts.6.262: Author of evil, unknown till thy revolt,

texts.6.266: And thy adherents: how hast thou disturb'd

texts.7.218: Nor staid, but on the Wings of Cherubim
texts.7.220: Farr into CHAOS, and the World unborn;
texts.7.221: For CHAOS heard his voice: him all his Traine
texts.7.222: Follow'd in bright procession to behold
texts.7.223: Creation, and the wonders of his might.
texts.7.224: Then staid the fervid Wheeles, and in his hand
texts.7.225: He took the golden Compasses, prepar'd
texts.7.226: In Gods Eternal store, to circumscribe
texts.7.227: This Universe, and all created things:
texts.7.228: One foot he center'd, and the other turn'd
texts.7.229: Round through the vast profunditie obscure,
texts.7.230: And said, thus farr extend, thus farr thy bounds,
texts.7.231: This be thy just Circumference, O World.
texts.7.232: Thus God the Heav'n created, thus the Earth,
texts.7.233: Matter unform'd and void: Darkness profound
texts.7.234: Cover'd th' Abyss: but on the watrie calme
texts.7.235: His brooding wings the Spirit of God outspred,
texts.7.236: And vital vertue infus'd, and vital warmth
texts.7.237: Throughout the fluid Mass, but downward purg'd
texts.7.238: The black tartareous cold infernal dregs
texts.7.239: Adverse to life: then founded, then conglob'd
texts.7.240: Like things to like, the rest to several place
texts.7.241: Disparted, and between spun out the Air,
texts.7.242: And Earth self-ballanc't on her Center hung.
texts.7.243: Let ther be Light, said God, and forthwith Light
texts.7.244: Ethereal, first of things, quintessence pure
texts.7.245: Sprung from the Deep, and from her Native East
texts.7.246: To journie through the airie gloom began,
texts.7.247: Sphear'd in a radiant Cloud, for yet the Sun
texts.7.248: Was not; shee in a cloudie Tabernacle
texts.7.249: Sojourn'd the while. God saw the Light was good;
texts.7.250: And light from darkness by the Hemisphere
texts.7.251: Divided: Light the Day, and Darkness Night
texts.7.252: He nam'd. Thus was the first Day Eev'n and Morn:
texts.7.254: By the Celestial Quires, when Orient Light
texts.7.255: Exhaling first from Darkness they beheld;
texts.7.256: Birth-day of Heav'n and Earth; with joy and shout
texts.7.257: The hollow Universal Orb they fill'd,
texts.7.258: And touch't thir Golden Harps, hymning prais'd
texts.7.259: God and his works, Creatour him they sung,
texts.7.260: Both when first Eevning was, and when first Morn.
texts.7.261: Again, God said, let ther be Firmament
texts.7.262: Amid the Waters, and let it divide
texts.7.263: The Waters from the Waters: and God made
texts.7.264: The Firmament, expanse of liquid, pure,
texts.7.266: In circuit to the uttermost convex
texts.7.267: Of this great Round: partition firm and sure,
texts.7.268: The Waters underneath from those above
texts.7.269: Dividing: for as Earth, so hee the World
texts.7.270: Built on circumfluous Waters calme, in wide
texts.7.271: Crystallin Ocean, and the loud misrule
texts.7.272: Of CHAOS farr remov'd, least fierce extreames
texts.7.273: Contiguous might distemper the whole frame:
texts.7.274: And Heav'n he nam'd the Firmament: So Eev'n
texts.7.275: And Morning CHORUS sung the second Day.
texts.7.276: The Earth was form'd, but in the Womb as yet
texts.7.278: Appeer'd not: over all the face of Earth
texts.7.279: Main Ocean flow'd, not idle, but with warme
texts.7.280: Prolific humour soft'ning all her Globe,
texts.7.281: Fermented the great Mother to conceave,
texts.7.282: Satiate with genial moisture, when God said
texts.7.283: Be gather'd now ye Waters under Heav'n
texts.7.284: Into one place, and let dry Land appeer.
texts.7.286: Emergent, and thir broad bare backs upheave
texts.7.287: Into the Clouds, thir tops ascend the Skie:
texts.7.288: So high as heav'd the tumid Hills, so low
texts.7.289: Down sunk a hollow bottom broad and deep,
texts.7.290: Capacious bed of Waters: thither they
texts.7.292: As drops on dust conglobing from the drie;
texts.7.293: Part rise in crystal Wall, or ridge direct,
texts.7.294: For haste; such flight the great command impress'd
texts.7.295: On the swift flouds: as Armies at the call
texts.7.296: Of Trumpet (for of Armies thou hast heard)
texts.7.297: Troop to thir Standard, so the watrie throng,
texts.7.298: Wave rowling after Wave, where way they found,
texts.7.299: If steep, with torrent rapture, if through Plaine,
texts.7.300: Soft-ebbing; nor withstood them Rock or Hill,
texts.7.301: But they, or under ground, or circuit wide
texts.7.302: With Serpent errour wandring, found thir way,
texts.7.303: And on the washie Oose deep Channels wore;
texts.7.304: Easie, e're God had bid the ground be drie,
texts.7.305: All but within those banks, where Rivers now
texts.7.306: Stream, and perpetual draw thir humid traine.
texts.7.307: The dry Land, Earth, and the great receptacle
texts.7.308: Of congregated Waters he call'd Seas:
texts.7.309: And saw that it was good, and said, Let th' Earth
texts.7.310: Put forth the verdant Grass, Herb yeilding Seed,
texts.7.311: And Fruit Tree yeilding Fruit after her kind;
texts.7.312: Whose Seed is in her self upon the Earth.
texts.7.313: He scarce had said, when the bare Earth, till then
texts.7.315: Brought forth the tender Grass, whose verdure clad
texts.7.316: Her Universal Face with pleasant green,
texts.7.317: Then Herbs of every leaf, that sudden flour'd
texts.7.318: Op'ning thir various colours, and made gay
texts.7.319: Her bosom smelling sweet: and these scarce blown,
texts.7.320: Forth flourish't thick the clustring Vine, forth crept
texts.7.321: The smelling Gourd, up stood the cornie Reed
texts.7.322: Embattell'd in her field: add the humble Shrub,
texts.7.323: And Bush with frizl'd hair implicit: last
texts.7.324: Rose as in Dance the stately Trees, and spred
texts.7.325: Thir branches hung with copious Fruit; or gemm'd
texts.7.326: Thir Blossoms: with high Woods the Hills were crownd,
texts.7.327: With tufts the vallies each fountain side,
texts.7.328: With borders long the Rivers. That Earth now
texts.7.329: Seemd like to Heav'n, a seat where Gods might dwell,
texts.7.330: Or wander with delight, and love to haunt
texts.7.331: Her sacred shades: though God had yet not rain'd
texts.7.332: Upon the Earth, and man to till the ground
texts.7.333: None was, but from the Earth a dewie Mist
texts.7.334: Went up and waterd all the ground, and each
texts.7.335: Plant of the field, which e're it was in the Earth
texts.7.336: God made, and every Herb, before it grew
texts.7.337: On the green stemm; God saw that it was good:
texts.7.338: So Eev'n and Morn recorded the Third Day.
texts.7.339: Again th' Almightie spake: Let there be Lights
texts.7.340: High in th' expanse of Heaven to divide
texts.7.341: The Day from Night; and let them be for Signes,
texts.7.342: For Seasons, and for Dayes, and circling Years,
texts.7.343: And let them be for Lights as I ordaine
texts.7.344: Thir Office in the Firmament of Heav'n
texts.7.345: To give Light on the Earth; and it was so.
texts.7.346: And God made two great Lights, great for thir use
texts.7.347: To Man, the greater to have rule by Day,
texts.7.348: The less by Night alterne: and made the Starrs,
texts.7.349: And set them in the Firmament of Heav'n
texts.7.350: To illuminate the Earth, and rule the Day
texts.7.351: In thir vicissitude, and rule the Night,
texts.7.352: And Light from Darkness to divide. God saw,
texts.7.353: Surveying his great Work, that it was good:
texts.7.354: For of Celestial Bodies first the Sun
texts.7.355: A mightie Spheare he fram'd, unlightsom first,
texts.7.356: Though of Ethereal Mould: then form'd the Moon
texts.7.357: Globose, and everie magnitude of Starrs,
texts.7.358: And sowd with Starrs the Heav'n thick as a field:
texts.7.359: Of Light by farr the greater part he took,
texts.7.360: Transplanted from her cloudie Shrine, and plac'd
texts.7.361: In the Suns Orb, made porous to receive
texts.7.362: And drink the liquid Light, firm to retaine
texts.7.363: Her gather'd beams, great Palace now of Light.
texts.7.364: Hither as to thir Fountain other Starrs
texts.7.365: Repairing, in thir gold'n Urns draw Light,
texts.7.366: And hence the Morning Planet guilds his horns;
texts.7.367: By tincture or reflection they augment
texts.7.368: Thir small peculiar, though from human sight
texts.7.369: So farr remote, with diminution seen.
texts.7.370: First in his East the glorious Lamp was seen,
texts.7.371: Regent of Day, and all th' Horizon round
texts.7.372: Invested with bright Rayes, jocond to run
texts.7.373: His Longitude through Heav'ns high rode: the gray
texts.7.374: Dawn, and the PLEIADES before him danc'd
texts.7.375: Shedding sweet influence: less bright the Moon,
texts.7.376: But opposite in leveld West was set
texts.7.377: His mirror, with full face borrowing her Light
texts.7.378: From him, for other light she needed none
texts.7.379: In that aspect, and still that distance keepes
texts.7.380: Till night, then in the East her turn she shines,
texts.7.381: Revolvd on Heav'ns great Axle, and her Reign
texts.7.382: With thousand lesser Lights dividual holds,
texts.7.383: With thousand thousand Starres, that then appeer'd
texts.7.384: Spangling the Hemisphere: then first adornd
texts.7.385: With thir bright Luminaries that Set and Rose,
texts.7.386: Glad Eevning glad Morn crownd the fourth day.
texts.7.387: And God said, let the Waters generate
texts.7.388: Reptil with Spawn abundant, living Soule:
texts.7.389: And let Fowle flie above the Earth, with wings
texts.7.390: Displayd on the op'n Firmament of Heav'n.
texts.7.391: And God created the great Whales, and each
texts.7.392: Soul living, each that crept, which plenteously
texts.7.393: The waters generated by thir kindes,
texts.7.394: And every Bird of wing after his kinde;
texts.7.395: And saw that it was good, and bless'd them, saying,
texts.7.396: Be fruitful, multiply, and in the Seas
texts.7.397: And Lakes and running Streams the waters fill;
texts.7.398: And let the Fowle be multiply'd on the Earth.
texts.7.399: Forthwith the Sounds and Seas, each Creek Bay
texts.7.400: With Frie innumerable swarme, and Shoales
texts.7.401: Of Fish that with thir Finns and shining Scales
texts.7.402: Glide under the green Wave, in Sculles that oft
texts.7.403: Bank the mid Sea: part single or with mate
texts.7.404: Graze the Sea weed thir pasture, through Groves
texts.7.405: Of Coral stray, or sporting with quick glance
texts.7.406: Show to the Sun thir wav'd coats dropt with Gold,
texts.7.407: Or in thir Pearlie shells at ease, attend
texts.7.408: Moist nutriment, or under Rocks thir food
texts.7.409: In jointed Armour watch: on smooth the Seale,
texts.7.410: And bended Dolphins play: part huge of bulk
texts.7.411: Wallowing unweildie, enormous in thir Gate
texts.7.413: Hugest of living Creatures, on the Deep
texts.7.414: Stretcht like a Promontorie sleeps or swimmes,
texts.7.415: And seems a moving Land, and at his Gilles
texts.7.416: Draws in, and at his Trunck spouts out a Sea.
texts.7.417: Mean while the tepid Caves, and Fens and shoares
texts.7.418: Thir Brood as numerous hatch, from the Egg that soon
texts.7.419: Bursting with kindly rupture forth disclos'd
texts.7.420: Thir callow young, but featherd soon and fledge
texts.7.421: They summ'd thir Penns, and soaring th' air sublime
texts.7.422: With clang despis'd the ground, under a cloud
texts.7.423: In prospect; there the Eagle and the Stork
texts.7.424: On Cliffs and Cedar tops thir Eyries build:
texts.7.425: Part loosly wing the Region, part more wise
texts.7.426: In common, rang'd in figure wedge thir way,
texts.7.427: Intelligent of seasons, and set forth
texts.7.428: Thir Aierie Caravan high over Sea's
texts.7.429: Flying, and over Lands with mutual wing
texts.7.430: Easing thir flight; so stears the prudent Crane
texts.7.431: Her annual Voiage, born on Windes; the Aire
texts.7.432: Floats, as they pass, fann'd with unnumber'd plumes:
texts.7.433: From Branch to Branch the smaller Birds with song
texts.7.434: Solac'd the Woods, and spred thir painted wings
texts.7.435: Till Ev'n, nor then the solemn Nightingal
texts.7.436: Ceas'd warbling, but all night tun'd her soft layes:
texts.7.437: Others on Silver Lakes and Rivers Bath'd
texts.7.438: Thir downie Brest; the Swan with Arched neck
texts.7.439: Between her white wings mantling proudly, Rowes
texts.7.440: Her state with Oarie feet: yet oft they quit
texts.7.441: The Dank, and rising on stiff Pennons, towre
texts.7.442: The mid Aereal Skie: Others on ground
texts.7.443: Walk'd firm; the crested Cock whose clarion sounds
texts.7.444: The silent hours, and th' other whose gay Traine
texts.7.445: Adorns him, colour'd with the Florid hue
texts.7.446: Of Rainbows and Starrie Eyes. The Waters thus
texts.7.447: With Fish replenisht, and the Aire with Fowle,
texts.7.448: Ev'ning and Morn solemniz'd the Fift day.
texts.7.449: The Sixt, and of Creation last arose
texts.7.450: With Eevning Harps and Mattin, when God said,
texts.7.451: Let th' Earth bring forth Fowle living in her kinde,
texts.7.452: Cattel and Creeping things, and Beast of the Earth,
texts.7.453: Each in their kinde. The Earth obey'd, and strait
texts.7.454: Op'ning her fertil Woomb teem'd at a Birth
texts.7.456: Limb'd and full grown: out of the ground up-rose
texts.7.457: As from his Laire the wilde Beast where he wonns
texts.7.458: In Forrest wilde, in Thicket, Brake, or Den;
texts.7.459: Among the Trees in Pairs they rose, they walk'd:
texts.7.460: The Cattel in the Fields and Meddowes green:
texts.7.461: Those rare and solitarie, these in flocks
texts.7.462: Pasturing at once, and in broad Herds upsprung:
texts.7.463: The grassie Clods now Calv'd, now half appeer'd
texts.7.464: The Tawnie Lion, pawing to get free
texts.7.465: His hinder parts, then springs as broke from Bonds,
texts.7.466: And Rampant shakes his Brinded main; the Ounce,
texts.7.467: The Libbard, and the Tyger, as the Moale
texts.7.468: Rising, the crumbl'd Earth above them threw
texts.7.469: In Hillocks; the swift Stag from under ground
texts.7.470: Bore up his branching head: scarse from his mould
texts.7.471: BEHEMOTH biggest born of Earth upheav'd
texts.7.472: His vastness: Fleec't the Flocks and bleating rose,
texts.7.473: As Plants: ambiguous between Sea and Land
texts.7.474: The River Horse and scalie Crocodile.
texts.7.475: At once came forth whatever creeps the ground,
texts.7.476: Insect or Worme; those wav'd thir limber fans
texts.7.477: For wings, and smallest Lineaments exact
texts.7.478: In all the Liveries dect of Summers pride
texts.7.479: With spots of Gold and Purple, azure and green:
texts.7.480: These as a line thir long dimension drew,
texts.7.481: Streaking the ground with sinuous trace; not all
texts.7.482: Minims of Nature; some of Serpent kinde
texts.7.483: Wondrous in length and corpulence involv'd
texts.7.484: Thir Snakie foulds, and added wings. First crept
texts.7.486: Of future, in small room large heart enclos'd,
texts.7.488: Hereafter, join'd in her popular Tribes
texts.7.490: The Femal Bee that feeds her Husband Drone
texts.7.491: Deliciously, and builds her waxen Cells
texts.7.492: With Honey stor'd: the rest are numberless,
texts.7.493: And thou thir Natures know'st, and gav'st them Names,
texts.7.494: Needlest to thee repeaed; nor unknown
texts.7.495: The Serpent suttl'st Beast of all the field,
texts.7.496: Of huge extent somtimes, with brazen Eyes
texts.7.497: And hairie Main terrific, though to thee
texts.7.498: Not noxious, but obedient at thy call.
texts.7.499: Now Heav'n in all her Glorie shon, and rowld
texts.7.500: Her motions, as the great first-Movers hand
texts.7.501: First wheeld thir course; Earth in her rich attire
texts.7.502: Consummate lovly smil'd; Aire, Water, Earth,
texts.7.503: By Fowl, Fish, Beast, was flown, was swum, was walkt
texts.7.504: Frequent; and of the Sixt day yet remain'd;
texts.7.505: There wanted yet the Master work, the end
texts.7.506: Of all yet don; a Creature who not prone
texts.7.507: And Brute as other Creatures, but endu'd
texts.7.508: With Sanctitie of Reason, might erect
texts.7.509: His Stature, and upright with Front serene
texts.7.510: Govern the rest, self-knowing, and from thence
texts.7.512: But grateful to acknowledge whence his good
texts.7.513: Descends, thither with heart and voice and eyes
texts.7.515: And worship God Supream, who made him chief
texts.7.516: Of all his works: therefore the Omnipotent
texts.7.517: Eternal Father (For where is not hee
texts.7.518: Present) thus to his Son audibly spake.
texts.7.519: Let us make now Man in our image, Man
texts.7.520: In our similitude, and let them rule
texts.7.521: Over the Fish and Fowle of Sea and Aire,
texts.7.522: Beast of the Field, and over all the Earth,
texts.7.523: And every creeping thing that creeps the ground.
texts.7.524: This said, he formd thee, ADAM, thee O Man
texts.7.525: Dust of the ground, and in thy nostrils breath'd
texts.7.526: The breath of Life; in his own Image hee
texts.7.527: Created thee, in the Image of God
texts.7.528: Express, and thou becam'st a living Soul.
texts.7.529: Male he created thee, but thy consort
texts.7.530: Femal for Race; then bless'd Mankinde, and said,
texts.7.531: Be fruitful, multiplie, and fill the Earth,
texts.7.532: Subdue it, and throughout Dominion hold
texts.7.533: Over Fish of the Sea, and Fowle of the Aire,
texts.7.534: And every living thing that moves on the Earth.
texts.7.535: Wherever thus created, for no place
texts.7.536: Is yet distinct by name, thence, as thou know'st
texts.7.537: He brought thee into this delicious Grove,
texts.7.538: This Garden, planted with the Trees of God,
texts.7.539: Delectable both to behold and taste;
texts.7.540: And freely all thir pleasant fruit for food
texts.7.541: Gave thee, all sorts are here that all th' Earth yeelds,
texts.7.542: Varietie without end; but of the Tree
texts.7.543: Which tasted works knowledge of Good and Evil,
texts.7.544: Thou mai'st not; in the day thou eat'st, thou di'st;
texts.7.545: Death is the penaltie impos'd, beware,
texts.7.546: And govern well thy appetite, least sin
texts.7.547: Surprise thee, and her black attendant Death.
texts.7.548: Here finish'd hee, and all that he had made
texts.7.549: View'd, and behold all was entirely good;
texts.7.550: So Ev'n and Morn accomplish'd the Sixt day:
texts.7.551: Yet not till the Creator from his work
texts.7.553: Up to the Heav'n of Heav'ns his high abode,
texts.7.554: Thence to behold this new created World
texts.7.555: Th' addition of his Empire, how it shew'd
texts.7.556: In prospect from his Throne, how good, how faire,
texts.7.557: Answering his great Idea. Up he rode
texts.7.558: Followd with acclamation and the sound
texts.7.559: Symphonious of ten thousand Harpes that tun'd
texts.7.560: Angelic harmonies: the Earth, the Aire
texts.7.562: The Heav'ns and all the Constellations rung,
texts.7.563: The Planets in thir stations list'ning stood,
texts.7.564: While the bright Pomp ascended jubilant.
texts.7.565: Open, ye everlasting Gates, they sung,
texts.7.566: Open, ye Heav'ns, your living dores; let in
texts.7.567: The great Creator from his work returnd
texts.7.568: Magnificent, his Six days work, a World;
texts.7.569: Open, and henceforth oft; for God will deigne
texts.7.570: To visit oft the dwellings of just Men
texts.7.572: Thither will send his winged Messengers
texts.7.573: On errands of supernal Grace. So sung
texts.7.574: The glorious Train ascending: He through Heav'n,
texts.7.575: That open'd wide her blazing Portals, led
texts.7.576: To Gods Eternal house direct the way,
texts.7.577: A broad and ample rode, whose dust is Gold
texts.7.578: And pavement Starrs, as Starrs to thee appeer,
texts.7.579: Seen in the Galaxie, that Milkie way
texts.7.580: Which nightly as a circling Zone thou seest
texts.7.581: Pouderd with Starrs. And now on Earth the Seaventh
texts.7.582: Eev'ning arose in EDEN, for the Sun
texts.7.583: Was set, and twilight from the East came on,
texts.7.584: Forerunning Night; when at the holy mount
texts.7.585: Of Heav'ns high-seated top, th' Impereal Throne
texts.7.586: Of Godhead, fixt for ever firm and sure,
texts.7.587: The Filial Power arriv'd, and sate him down
texts.7.588: With his great Father (for he also went
texts.7.590: Hath Omnipresence) and the work ordain'd,
texts.7.591: Author and end of all things, and from work
texts.7.592: Now resting, bless'd and hallowd the Seav'nth day,
texts.7.593: As resting on that day from all his work,
texts.7.594: But not in silence holy kept; the Harp
texts.7.595: Had work and rested not, the solemn Pipe,
texts.7.596: And Dulcimer, all Organs of sweet stop,
texts.7.597: All sounds on Fret by String or Golden Wire
texts.7.598: Temper'd soft Tunings, intermixt with Voice
texts.7.599: Choral or Unison: of incense Clouds
texts.7.600: Fuming from Golden Censers hid the Mount.
texts.7.601: Creation and the Six dayes acts they sung,
texts.7.602: Great are thy works, JEHOVAH, infinite
texts.7.603: Thy power; what thought can measure thee or tongue
texts.7.604: Relate thee; greater now in thy return
texts.7.605: Then from the Giant Angels; thee that day
texts.7.606: Thy Thunders magnifi'd; but to create
texts.7.607: Is greater then created to destroy.
texts.7.608: Who can impair thee, mighty King, or bound
texts.7.609: Thy Empire? easily the proud attempt
texts.7.610: Of Spirits apostat and thir Counsels vaine
texts.7.611: Thou hast repeld, while impiously they thought
texts.7.612: Thee to diminish, and from thee withdraw
texts.7.613: The number of thy worshippers. Who seekes
texts.7.614: To lessen thee, against his purpose serves
texts.7.615: To manifest the more thy might: his evil
texts.7.616: Thou usest, and from thence creat'st more good.
texts.7.617: Witness this new-made World, another Heav'n
texts.7.618: From Heaven Gate not farr, founded in view
texts.7.619: On the cleer HYALINE, the Glassie Sea;
texts.7.620: Of amplitude almost immense, with Starr's
texts.7.621: Numerous, and every Starr perhaps a World
texts.7.622: Of destind habitation; but thou know'st
texts.7.623: Thir seasons: among these the seat of men,
texts.7.624: Earth with her nether Ocean circumfus'd,
texts.7.625: Thir pleasant dwelling place. Thrice happie men,
texts.7.626: And sons of men, whom God hath thus advanc't,
texts.7.627: Created in his Image, there to dwell
texts.7.628: And worship him, and in reward to rule
texts.7.629: Over his Works, on Earth, in Sea, or Air,
texts.7.630: And multiply a Race of Worshippers
texts.7.631: Holy and just: thrice happie if they know
texts.7.633: So sung they, and the Empyrean rung,
texts.7.634: With HALLELUIAHS: Thus was Sabbath kept.
texts.7.635: And thy request think now fulfill'd, that ask'd
texts.7.636: How first this World and face of things began,

texts.8.1018: And elegant, of Sapience no small part,
texts.8.1019: Since to each meaning savour we apply,
texts.8.1020: And Palate call judicious; I the praise
texts.8.1021: Yeild thee, so well this day thou hast purvey'd.
texts.8.1022: Much pleasure we have lost, while we abstain'd
texts.8.1023: From this delightful Fruit, nor known till now
texts.8.1024: True relish, tasting; if such pleasure be
texts.8.1025: In things to us forbidden, it might be wish'd,
texts.8.1026: For this one Tree had bin forbidden ten.
texts.8.1027: But come, so well refresh't, now let us play,
texts.8.1028: As meet is, after such delicious Fare;
texts.8.1029: For never did thy Beautie since the day
texts.8.1030: I saw thee first and wedded thee, adorn'd
texts.8.1031: With all perfections, so enflame my sense
texts.8.1032: With ardor to enjoy thee, fairer now
texts.8.1033: Then ever, bountie of this vertuous Tree.
texts.8.1034: So said he, and forbore not glance or toy
texts.8.1036: Of EVE, whose Eye darted contagious Fire.
texts.8.1037: Her hand he seis'd, and to a shadie bank,
texts.8.1038: Thick overhead with verdant roof imbowr'd
texts.8.1039: He led her nothing loath; Flours were the Couch,
texts.8.1041: And Hyacinth, Earths freshest softest lap.
texts.8.1042: There they thir fill of Love and Loves disport
texts.8.1043: Took largely, of thir mutual guilt the Seale,
texts.8.1044: The solace of thir sin, till dewie sleep
texts.8.1045: Oppress'd them, wearied with thir amorous play.
texts.8.1046: Soon as the force of that fallacious Fruit,
texts.8.1048: About thir spirits had plaid, and inmost powers
texts.8.1049: Made erre, was now exhal'd, and grosser sleep
texts.8.1050: Bred of unkindly fumes, with conscious dreams
texts.8.1051: Encumberd, now had left them, up they rose
texts.8.1052: As from unrest, and each the other viewing,
texts.8.1053: Soon found thir Eyes how op'nd, and thir minds
texts.8.1054: How dark'nd; innocence, that as a veile
texts.8.1055: Had shadow'd them from knowing ill, was gon,
texts.8.1057: And honour from about them, naked left
texts.8.1058: To guiltie shame hee cover'd, but his Robe
texts.8.1059: Uncover'd more. So rose the DANITE strong
texts.8.1062: Shorn of his strength, They destitute and bare
texts.8.1063: Of all thir vertue: silent, and in face
texts.8.1064: Confounded long they sate, as struck'n mute,
texts.8.1065: Till ADAM, though not less then EVE abasht,
texts.8.1066: At length gave utterance to these words constraind.
texts.8.1067: O EVE, in evil hour thou didst give care
texts.8.1068: To that false Worm, of whomsoever taught
texts.8.1069: To counterfet Mans voice, true in our Fall,
texts.8.1070: False in our promis'd Rising; since our Eyes
texts.8.1071: Op'nd we find indeed, and find we know
texts.8.1072: Both Good and Evil, Good lost and Evil got,
texts.8.1073: Bad Fruit of Knowledge, if this be to know,
texts.8.1074: Which leaves us naked thus, of Honour void,
texts.8.1075: Of Innocence, of Faith, of Puritie,
texts.8.1076: Our wonted Ornaments now soild and staind,
texts.8.1077: And in our Faces evident the signes
texts.8.1078: Of foul concupiscence; whence evil store;
texts.8.1079: Even shame, the last of evils; of the first
texts.8.1080: Be sure then. How shall I behold the face
texts.8.1081: Henceforth of God or Angel, earst with joy
texts.8.1082: And rapture so oft beheld? those heav'nly shapes
texts.8.1083: Will dazle now this earthly, with thir blaze
texts.8.1084: Insufferably bright. O might I here
texts.8.1085: In solitude live savage, in some glad
texts.8.1087: To Starr or Sun-light, spread thir umbrage broad,
texts.8.1088: And brown as Evening: Cover me ye Pines,
texts.8.1090: Hide me, where I may never see them more.
texts.8.1091: But let us now, as in bad plight, devise
texts.8.1092: What best may for the present serve to hide
texts.8.1093: The Parts of each from other, that seem most
texts.8.1094: To shame obnoxious, and unseemliest seen,
texts.8.1095: Some Tree whose broad smooth Leaves together sowd,
texts.8.1096: And girded on our loyns, may cover round
texts.8.1097: Those middle parts, that this new commer, Shame,
texts.8.1098: There sit not, and reproach us as unclean.
texts.8.1099: So counsel'd hee, and both together went
texts.8.1100: Into the thickest Wood, there soon they chose
texts.8.1101: The Figtree, not that kind for Fruit renown'd,
texts.8.1102: But such as at this day to INDIANS known
texts.8.1103: In MALABAR or DECAN spreds her Armes
texts.8.1104: Braunching so broad and long, that in the ground
texts.8.1105: The bended Twigs take root, and Daughters grow
texts.8.1106: About the Mother Tree, a Pillard shade
texts.8.1107: High overarch't, and echoing Walks between;
texts.8.1108: There oft the INDIAN Herdsman shunning heate
texts.8.1109: Shelters in coole, and tends his pasturing Herds
texts.8.1110: At Loopholes cut through thickest shade: Those Leaves
texts.8.1111: They gatherd, broad as AMAZONIAN Targe,
texts.8.1112: And with what skill they had, together sowd,
texts.8.1113: To gird thir waste, vain Covering if to hide
texts.8.1114: Thir guilt and dreaded shame; O how unlike
texts.8.1115: To that first naked Glorie. Such of late
texts.8.1116: COLUMBUS found th' AMERICAN to girt
texts.8.1117: With featherd Cincture, naked else and wilde
texts.8.1118: Among the Trees on Iles and woodie Shores.
texts.8.1119: Thus fenc't, and as they thought, thir shame in part
texts.8.1120: Coverd, but not at rest or ease of Mind,
texts.8.1121: They sate them down to weep, nor onely Teares
texts.8.1122: Raind at thir Eyes, but high Winds worse within
texts.8.1123: Began to rise, high Passions, Anger, Hate,
texts.8.1124: Mistrust, Suspicion, Discord, and shook sore
texts.8.1125: Thir inward State of Mind, calme Region once
texts.8.1126: And full of Peace, now tost and turbulent:
texts.8.1127: For Understanding rul'd not, and the Will
texts.8.1128: Heard not her lore, both in subjection now
texts.8.1129: To sensual Appetite, who from beneathe
texts.8.1131: Superior sway: From thus distemperd brest,
texts.8.1132: ADAM, estrang'd in look and alterd stile,
texts.8.1133: Speech intermitted thus to EVE renewd.
texts.8.1134: Would thou hadst heark'nd to my words, stai'd
texts.8.1135: With me, as I besought thee, when that strange
texts.8.1136: Desire of wandring this unhappie Morn,
texts.8.1137: I know not whence possessd thee; we had then
texts.8.1138: Remaind still happie, not as now, despoild
texts.8.1139: Of all our good, sham'd, naked, miserable.
texts.8.1140: Let none henceforth seek needless cause to approve
texts.8.1141: The Faith they owe; when earnestly they seek
texts.8.1142: Such proof, conclude, they then begin to faile.
texts.8.1143: To whom soon mov'd with touch of blame thus EVE.
texts.8.1144: What words have past thy Lips, ADAM severe,
texts.8.1145: Imput'st thou that to my default, or will
texts.8.1146: Of wandering, as thou call'st it, which who knows
texts.8.1147: But might as ill have happ'nd thou being by,
texts.8.1148: Or to thy self perhaps: hadst thou bin there,
texts.8.1149: Or bere th' attempt, thou couldst not have discernd
texts.8.1150: Fraud in the Serpent, speaking as he spake;
texts.8.1151: No ground of enmitie between us known,
texts.8.1152: Why hee should mean me ill, or seek to harme.
texts.8.1153: Was I to have never parted from thy side?
texts.8.1154: As good have grown there still a liveless Rib.
texts.8.1155: Being as I am, why didst not thou the Head
texts.8.1156: Command me absolutely not to go,
texts.8.1157: Going into such danger as thou saidst?
texts.8.1158: Too facil then thou didst not much gainsay,
texts.8.1159: Nay, didst permit, approve, and fair dismiss.
texts.8.1160: Hadst thou bin firm and fixt in thy dissent,
texts.8.1161: Neither had I transgress'd, nor thou with mee.
texts.8.1162: To whom then first incenst ADAM repli'd.
texts.8.1163: Is this the Love, is the recompence
texts.8.1164: Of mine to thee, ingrateful EVE, exprest
texts.8.1165: Immutable when thou wert lost, not I,
texts.8.1166: Who might have liv'd and joyd immortal bliss,
texts.8.1167: Yet willingly chose rather Death with thee:
texts.8.1168: And am I now upbraided, as the cause
texts.8.1169: Of thy transgressing? not enough severe,
texts.8.1170: It seems, in thy restraint: what could I more?
texts.8.1171: I warn'd thee, I admonish'd thee, foretold
texts.8.1172: The danger, and the lurking Enemie
texts.8.1173: That lay in wait; beyond this had bin force,
texts.8.1174: And force upon free Will hath here no place.
texts.8.1175: But confidence then bore thee on, secure
texts.8.1176: Either to meet no danger, or to finde
texts.8.1177: Matter of glorious trial; and perhaps
texts.8.1178: I also err'd in overmuch admiring
texts.8.1179: What seemd in thee so perfet, that I thought
texts.8.1180: No evil durst attempt thee, but I rue
texts.8.1181: That errour now, which is become my crime,
texts.8.1182: And thou th' accuser. Thus it shall befall
texts.8.1183: Him who to worth in Women overtrusting
texts.8.1184: Lets her Will rule; restraint she will not brook,
texts.8.1185: And left to her self, if evil thence ensue,
texts.8.1186: Shee first his weak indulgence will accuse.
texts.8.1187: Thus they in mutual accusation spent
texts.8.1188: The fruitless hours, but neither self-condemning
texts.8.1189: And of thir vain contest appeer'd no end.
texts.9.1: Meanwhile the hainous and despightfull act
texts.9.2: Of SATAN done in Paradise, and how
texts.9.3: Hee in the Serpent had perverted EVE,
texts.9.4: Her Husband shee, to taste the fatall fruit,
texts.9.5: Was known in Heav'n; for what can scape the Eye
texts.9.6: Of God All-seeing, or deceave his Heart
texts.9.7: Omniscient, who in all things wise and just,
texts.9.8: Hinder'd not SATAN to attempt the minde
texts.9.9: Of Man, with strength entire, and free Will arm'd,
texts.9.10: Complete to have discover'd and repulst
texts.9.11: Whatever wiles of Foe or seeming Friend.
texts.9.12: For still they knew, and ought to have still remember'd
texts.9.13: The high Injunction not to taste that Fruit,
texts.9.14: Whoever tempted; which they not obeying,
texts.9.15: Incurr'd, what could they less, the penaltie,
texts.9.16: And manifold in sin, deserv'd to fall.
texts.9.17: Up into Heav'n from Paradise in hast
texts.9.18: Th' Angelic Guards ascended, mute and sad
texts.9.19: For Man, for of his state by this they knew,
texts.9.20: Much wondring how the suttle Fiend had stoln
texts.9.21: Entrance unseen. Soon as th' unwelcome news
texts.9.22: From Earth arriv'd at Heaven Gate, displeas'd
texts.9.23: All were who heard, dim sadness did not spare
texts.9.24: That time Celestial visages, yet mixt
texts.9.25: With pitie, violated not thir bliss.
texts.9.27: Th' ethereal People ran, to hear and know
texts.9.28: How all befell: they towards the Throne Supream
texts.9.29: Accountable made haste to make appear
texts.9.30: With righteous plea, thir utmost vigilance,
texts.9.31: And easily approv'd; when the most High
texts.9.32: Eternal Father from his secret Cloud,
texts.9.33: Amidst in Thunder utter'd thus his voice.
texts.9.34: Assembl'd Angels, and ye Powers return'd
texts.9.35: From unsuccessful charge, be not dismaid,
texts.9.36: Nor troubl'd at these tidings from the Earth,
texts.9.37: Which your sincerest care could not prevent,
texts.9.38: Foretold so lately what would come to pass,
texts.9.39: When first this Tempter cross'd the Gulf from Hell.
texts.9.40: I told ye then he should prevail and speed
texts.9.41: On his bad Errand, Man should be seduc't
texts.9.42: And flatter'd out of all, believing lies
texts.9.43: Against his Maker; no Decree of mine
texts.9.45: Or touch with lightest moment of impulse
texts.9.46: His free Will, to her own inclining left
texts.9.47: In eevn scale. But fall'n he is, and now
texts.9.48: What rests, but that the mortal Sentence pass
texts.9.49: On his transgression, Death denounc't that day,
texts.9.50: Which he presumes already vain and void,
texts.9.51: Because not yet inflicted, as he fear'd,
texts.9.52: By some immediate stroak; but soon shall find
texts.9.53: Forbearance no acquittance ere day end.
texts.9.54: Justice shall not return as bountie scorn'd.
texts.9.55: But whom send I to judge them? whom but thee
texts.9.56: Vicegerent Son, to thee I have transferr'd
texts.9.57: All Judgement, whether in Heav'n, or Earth; or Hell.
texts.9.58: Easie it may be seen that I intend
texts.9.59: Mercie collegue with Justice, sending thee
texts.9.60: Mans Friend, his Mediator, his design'd
texts.9.62: And destin'd Man himself to judge Man fall'n.
texts.9.63: So spake the Father, and unfoulding bright
texts.9.64: Toward the right hand his Glorie, on the Son
texts.9.65: Blaz'd forth unclouded Deitie; he full
texts.9.67: Express'd, and thus divinely answer'd milde.
texts.9.68: Father Eternal, thine is to decree,
texts.9.69: Mine both in Heav'n and Earth to do thy will
texts.9.70: Supream, that thou in mee thy Son belov'd
texts.9.71: Mayst ever rest well pleas'd. I go to judge
texts.9.72: On Earth these thy transgressors, but thou knowst,
texts.9.73: Whoever judg'd, the worst on mee must light,
texts.9.74: When time shall be, for so I undertook
texts.9.75: Before thee; and not repenting, this obtaine
texts.9.76: Of right, that I may mitigate thir doom
texts.9.77: On me deriv'd, yet I shall temper so
texts.9.78: Justice with Mercie, as may illustrate most
texts.9.79: Them fully satisfied, and thee appease.
texts.9.80: Attendance none shall need, nor Train, where none
texts.9.81: Are to behold the Judgement, but the judg'd,
texts.9.82: Those two; the third best absent is condemn'd,
texts.9.83: Convict by flight, and Rebel to all Law
texts.9.84: Conviction to the Serpent none belongs.
texts.9.85: Thus saying, from his radiant Seat he rose
texts.9.86: Of high collateral glorie: him Thrones and Powers,
texts.9.88: Accompanied to Heaven Gate, from whence
texts.9.89: EDEN and all the Coast in prospect lay.
texts.9.90: Down he descended strait; the speed of Gods
texts.9.91: Time counts not, though with swiftest minutes wing'd.
texts.9.92: Now was the Sun in Western cadence low
texts.9.93: From Noon, and gentle Aires due at thir hour
texts.9.94: To fan the Earth now wak'd, and usher in
texts.9.95: The Eevning coole when he from wrauth more coole
texts.9.96: Came the mild Judge and Intercessor both
texts.9.97: To sentence Man: the voice of God they heard
texts.9.98: Now walking in the Garden, by soft windes
texts.9.99: Brought to thir Ears, while day declin'd, they heard
texts.9.100: And from his presence hid themselves among
texts.9.101: The thickest Trees, both Man and Wife, till God
texts.9.102: Approaching, thus to ADAM call'd aloud.
texts.9.103: Where art thou ADAM, wont with joy to meet
texts.9.104: My coming seen far off? I miss thee here,
texts.9.105: Not pleas'd, thus entertaind with solitude,
texts.9.106: Where obvious dutie erewhile appear'd unsaught:
texts.9.107: Or come I less conspicuous, or what change
texts.9.108: Absents thee, or what chance detains? Come forth.
texts.9.109: He came, and with him EVE, more loth, though first
texts.9.110: To offend, discount'nanc't both, and discompos'd;
texts.9.111: Love was not in thir looks, either to God
texts.9.112: Or to each other, but apparent guilt,
texts.9.113: And shame, and perturbation, and despaire,
texts.9.114: Anger, and obstinacie, and hate, and guile.
texts.9.115: Whence ADAM faultring long, thus answer'd brief.
texts.9.116: I heard thee in the Garden, and of thy voice
texts.9.117: Affraid, being naked, hid my self. To whom
texts.9.118: The gracious Judge without revile repli'd.
texts.9.119: My voice thou oft hast heard, and hast not fear'd,
texts.9.120: But still rejoyc't, how is it now become
texts.9.121: So dreadful to thee? that thou art naked, who
texts.9.122: Hath told thee? hast thou eaten of the Tree
texts.9.123: Whereof I gave thee charge thou shouldst not eat?
texts.9.124: To whom thus ADAM sore beset repli'd.
texts.9.125: O Heav'n! in evil strait this day I stand
texts.9.126: Before my Judge, either to undergoe
texts.9.127: My self the total Crime, or to accuse
texts.9.128: My other self, the partner of my life;
texts.9.129: Whose failing, while her Faith to me remaines,
texts.9.130: I should conceal, and not expose to blame
texts.9.131: By my complaint; but strict necessitie
texts.9.133: Least on my head both sin and punishment,
texts.9.135: Devolv'd; though should I hold my peace, yet thou
texts.9.136: Wouldst easily detect what I conceale.
texts.9.137: This Woman whom thou mad'st to be my help,
texts.9.138: And gav'st me as thy perfet gift, so good,
texts.9.139: So fit, so acceptable, so Divine,
texts.9.140: That from her hand I could suspect no ill,
texts.9.141: And what she did, whatever in it self,
texts.9.142: Her doing seem'd to justifie the deed;
texts.9.143: Shee gave me of the Tree, and I did eate.
texts.9.144: To whom the sovran Presence thus repli'd.
texts.9.145: Was shee thy God, that her thou didst obey
texts.9.146: Before his voice, or was shee made thy guide,
texts.9.147: Superior, or but equal, that to her
texts.9.148: Thou did'st resigne thy Manhood, and the Place
texts.9.149: Wherein God set thee above her made of thee,
texts.9.150: And for thee, whose perfection farr excell'd
texts.9.151: Hers in all real dignitie: Adornd
texts.9.152: She was indeed, and lovely to attract
texts.9.153: Thy Love, not thy Subjection, and her Gifts
texts.9.154: Were such as under Government well seem'd,
texts.9.155: Unseemly to beare rule, which was thy part
texts.9.156: And person, had'st thou known thy self aright.
texts.9.157: So having said, he thus to EVE in few:
texts.9.158: Say Woman, what is this which thou hast done?
texts.9.159: To whom sad EVE with shame nigh overwhelm'd,
texts.9.160: Confessing soon, yet not before her Judge
texts.9.161: Bold or loquacious, thus abasht repli'd.
texts.9.162: The Serpent me beguil'd and I did eate.
texts.9.163: Which when the Lord God heard, without delay
texts.9.164: To Judgement he proceeded on th' accus'd
texts.9.165: Serpent though brute, unable to transferre
texts.9.166: The Guilt on him who made him instrument
texts.9.167: Of mischief, and polluted from the end
texts.9.168: Of his Creation; justly then accurst,
texts.9.169: As vitiated in Nature: more to know
texts.9.170: Concern'd not Man (since he no further knew)
texts.9.171: Nor alter'd his offence; yet God at last
texts.9.172: To Satan first in sin his doom apply'd,
texts.9.173: Though in mysterious terms, judg'd as then best:
texts.9.174: And on the Serpent thus his curse let fall.
texts.9.175: Because thou hast done this, thou art accurst
texts.9.176: Above all Cattel, each Beast of the Field;
texts.9.177: Upon thy Belly groveling thou shalt goe,
texts.9.178: And dust shalt eat all the days of thy Life.
texts.9.179: Between Thee and the Woman I will put
texts.9.180: Enmitie, and between thine and her Seed;
texts.9.181: Her Seed shall bruise thy head, thou bruise his heel.
texts.9.182: So spake this Oracle, then verifi'd
texts.9.183: When JESUS son of MARY second EVE,
texts.9.184: Saw Satan fall like Lightning down from Heav'n,
texts.9.185: Prince of the Aire; then rising from his Grave
texts.9.187: In open shew, and with ascention bright
texts.9.188: Captivity led captive through the Aire,
texts.9.189: The Realme it self of Satan long usurpt,
texts.9.190: Whom he shall tread at last under our feet;
texts.9.191: Eevn hee who now foretold his fatal bruise,
texts.9.192: And to the Woman thus his Sentence turn'd.
texts.9.193: Thy sorrow I will greatly multiplie
texts.9.194: By thy Conception; Children thou shalt bring
texts.9.195: In sorrow forth, and to thy Husbands will
texts.9.196: Thine shall submit, hee over thee shall rule.
texts.9.197: On ADAM last thus judgement he pronounc'd.
texts.9.198: Because thou hast heark'nd to the voice of thy Wife,
texts.9.199: And eaten of the Tree concerning which
texts.9.200: I charg'd thee, saying: Thou shalt not eate thereof,
texts.9.201: Curs'd is the ground for thy sake, thou in sorrow
texts.9.202: Shalt eate thereof all the days of thy Life;
texts.9.203: Thornes also and Thistles it shall bring thee forth
texts.9.204: Unbid, and thou shalt eate th' Herb of th' Field,
texts.9.205: In the sweat of thy Face shalt thou eate Bread,
texts.9.206: Till thou return unto the ground, for thou
texts.9.207: Out of the ground wast taken, know thy Birth,
texts.9.208: For dust thou art, and shalt to dust returne.
texts.9.209: So judg'd he Man, both Judge and Saviour sent,
texts.9.210: And th' instant stroke of Death denounc't that day
texts.9.211: Remov'd farr off; then pittying how they stood
texts.9.212: Before him naked to the aire, that now
texts.9.213: Must suffer change, disdain'd not to begin
texts.9.214: Thenceforth the forme of servant to assume,
texts.9.215: As when he wash'd his servants feet, so now
texts.9.216: As Father of his Familie he clad
texts.9.217: Thir nakedness with Skins of Beasts, or slain,
texts.9.218: Or as the Snake with youthful Coate repaid;
texts.9.219: And thought not much to cloath his Enemies:
texts.9.220: Nor hee thir outward onely with the Skins
texts.9.221: Of Beasts, but inward nakedness, much more
texts.9.222: Opprobrious, with his Robe of righteousness,
texts.9.223: Araying cover'd from his Fathers sight.
texts.9.224: To him with swift ascent he up returnd,
texts.9.226: In glory as of old, to him appeas'd
texts.9.227: All, though all-knowing, what had past with Man
texts.9.229: Meanwhile ere thus was sin'd and judg'd on Earth,
texts.9.230: Within the Gates of Hell sate Sin and Death,
texts.9.231: In counterview within the Gates, that now
texts.9.232: Stood open wide, belching outrageous flame
texts.9.233: Farr into CHAOS, since the Fiend pass'd through,
texts.9.234: Sin opening, who thus now to Death began.
texts.9.235: O Son, why sit we here each other viewing
texts.9.236: Idlely, while Satan our great Author thrives
texts.9.237: In other Worlds, and happier Seat provides
texts.9.238: For us his ofspring deare? It cannot be
texts.9.239: But that success attends him; if mishap,
texts.9.240: Ere this he had return'd, with fury driv'n

texts.9.354: O Parent, these are thy magnific deeds,

texts.9.579: Among the Heathen of thir purchase got,
