texts.10.380: Stretcht out to amplest reach of prospect lay.
texts.10.381: Not higher that Hill nor wider looking round,
texts.10.382: Whereon for different cause the Tempter set
texts.10.383: Our second ADAM in the Wilderness,
texts.10.384: To shew him all Earths Kingdomes and thir Glory.
texts.10.385: His Eye might there command wherever stood
texts.10.386: City of old or modern Fame, the Seat
texts.10.387: Of mightiest Empire, from the destind Walls
texts.10.388: Of CAMBALU, seat of CATHAIAN CAN
texts.10.389: And SAMARCHAND by OXUS, TEMIRS Throne,
texts.10.390: To PAQUIN of SINAEAN Kings, and thence
texts.10.391: To AGRA and LAHOR of great MOGUL
texts.10.392: Down to the golden CHERSONESE, or where
texts.10.393: The PERSIAN in ECBATAN sate, or since
texts.10.394: In HISPAHAN, or where the RUSSIAN KSAR
texts.10.395: In MOSCO, or the Sultan in BIZANCE,
texts.10.396: TURCHESTAN-born; nor could his eye not ken
texts.10.397: Th' Empire of NEGUS to his utmost Port
texts.10.398: ERCOCO and the less Maritine Kings
texts.10.400: And SOFALA thought OPHIR, to the Realme
texts.10.401: Of CONGO, and ANGOLA fardest South;
texts.10.402: Or thence from NIGER Flood to ATLAS Mount
texts.10.403: The Kingdoms of ALMANSOR, FEZ, and SUS,
texts.10.405: On EUROPE thence, and where ROME was to sway
texts.10.406: The VVorld: in Spirit perhaps he also saw
texts.10.407: Rich MEXICO the seat of MOTEZUME,
texts.10.408: And CUSCO in PERU, the richer seat
texts.10.410: GUIANA, whose great Citie GERYONS Sons
texts.10.411: Call EL DORADO: but to nobler sights
texts.10.412: MICHAEL from ADAMS eyes the Filme remov'd
texts.10.413: VVhich that false Fruit that promis'd clearer sight
texts.10.414: Had bred; then purg'd with Euphrasie and Rue
texts.10.415: The visual Nerve, for he had much to see;
texts.10.416: And from the VVell of Life three drops instill'd.
texts.10.417: So deep the power of these Ingredients pierc'd,
texts.10.418: Eevn to the inmost seat of mental sight,
texts.10.419: That ADAM now enforc't to close his eyes,
texts.10.420: Sunk down and all his Spirits became intranst:
texts.10.421: But him the gentle Angel by the hand
texts.10.422: Soon rais'd, and his attention thus recall'd.
texts.10.423: ADAM, now ope thine eyes, and first behold
texts.10.424: Th' effects which thy original crime hath wrought
texts.10.425: In some to spring from thee, who never touch'd
texts.10.426: Th' excepted Tree, nor with the Snake conspir'd,
texts.10.427: Nor sinn'd thy sin, yet from that sin derive
texts.10.428: Corruption to bring forth more violent deeds.
texts.10.429: His eyes he op'nd, and beheld a field,
texts.10.430: Part arable and tilth, whereon were Sheaves
texts.10.431: New reapt, the other part sheep-walks and foulds;
texts.10.432: Ith' midst an Altar as the Land-mark stood
texts.10.433: Rustic, of grassie sord; thither anon
texts.10.434: A sweatie Reaper from his Tillage brought
texts.10.435: First Fruits, the green Eare, and the yellow Sheaf,
texts.10.436: Uncull'd, as came to hand; a Shepherd next
texts.10.437: More meek came with the Firstlings of his Flock
texts.10.438: Choicest and best; then sacrificing, laid
texts.10.439: The Inwards and thir Fat, with Incense strew'd,
texts.10.440: On the cleft Wood, and all due Rites perform'd.
texts.10.441: His Offring soon propitious Fire from Heav'n
texts.10.442: Consum'd with nimble glance, and grateful steame;
texts.10.443: The others not, for his was not sincere;
texts.10.444: Whereat hee inlie rag'd, and as they talk'd,
texts.10.445: Smote him into the Midriff with a stone
texts.10.446: That beat out life; he fell, and deadly pale
texts.10.447: Groand out his Soul with gushing bloud effus'd.
texts.10.448: Much at that sight was ADAM in his heart
texts.10.449: Dismai'd, and thus in haste to th' Angel cri'd.
texts.10.450: O Teacher, some great mischief hath befall'n
texts.10.451: To that meek man, who well had sacrific'd;
texts.10.452: Is Pietie thus and pure Devotion paid?
texts.10.453: T' whom MICHAEL thus, hee also mov'd, repli'd.
texts.10.454: These two are Brethren, ADAM, and to come
texts.10.455: Out of thy loyns; th' unjust the just hath slain,
texts.10.456: For envie that his Brothers Offering found
texts.10.457: From Heav'n acceptance; but the bloodie Fact
texts.10.458: Will be aveng'd, and th' others Faith approv'd
texts.10.459: Loose no reward, though here thou see him die,
texts.10.460: Rowling in dust and gore. To which our Sire.
texts.10.461: Alas, both for the deed and for the cause!
texts.10.462: But have I now seen Death? Is this the way
texts.10.463: I must return to native dust? O sight
texts.10.464: Of terrour, foul and ugly to behold,
texts.10.465: Horrid to think, how horrible to feel!
texts.10.466: To whom thus MICHAEL. Death thou hast seen
texts.10.467: In his first shape on man; but many shapes
texts.10.468: Of Death, and many are the wayes that lead
texts.10.469: To his grim Cave, all dismal; yet to sense
texts.10.470: More terrible at th' entrance then within.
texts.10.471: Some, as thou saw'st, by violent stroke shall die,
texts.10.472: By Fire, Flood, Famin, by Intemperance more
texts.10.473: In Meats and Drinks, which on the Earth shal bring
texts.10.474: Diseases dire, of which a monstrous crew
texts.10.475: Before thee shall appear; that thou mayst know
texts.10.476: What miserie th' inabstinence of EVE
texts.10.477: Shall bring on men. Immediately a place
texts.10.478: Before his eyes appeard, sad, noysom, dark,
texts.10.479: A Lazar-house it seemd, wherein were laid
texts.10.480: Numbers of all diseas'd, all maladies
texts.10.481: Of gastly Spasm, or racking torture, qualmes
texts.10.482: Of heart-sick Agonie, all feavorous kinds,
texts.10.484: Intestin Stone and Ulcer, Colic pangs,
texts.10.485: Dropsies, and Asthma's, and Joint-racking Rheums.
texts.10.486: Dire was the tossing, deep the groans, despair
texts.10.487: Tended the sick busiest from Couch to Couch;
texts.10.488: And over them triumphant Death his Dart
texts.10.489: Shook, but delaid to strike, though oft invok't
texts.10.490: With vows, as thir chief good, and final hope.
texts.10.491: Sight so deform what heart of Rock could long
texts.10.492: Drie-ey'd behold? ADAM could not, but wept,
texts.10.493: Though not of Woman born; compassion quell'd
texts.10.494: His best of Man, and gave him up to tears
texts.10.495: A space, till firmer thoughts restraind excess,
texts.10.496: And scarce recovering words his plaint renew'd.
texts.10.497: O miserable Mankind, to what fall
texts.10.498: Degraded, to what wretched state reserv'd?
texts.10.499: Better end heer unborn. Why is life giv'n
texts.10.500: To be thus wrested from us? rather why
texts.10.501: Obtruded on us thus? who if we knew
texts.10.502: What we receive, would either not accept
texts.10.503: Life offer'd, or soon beg to lay it down,
texts.10.504: Glad to be so dismist in peace. Can thus
texts.10.505: Th' Image of God in man created once
texts.10.506: So goodly and erect, though faultie since,
texts.10.507: To such unsightly sufferings be debas't
texts.10.508: Under inhuman pains? Why should not Man,
texts.10.510: In part, from such deformities be free,
texts.10.511: And for his Makers Image sake exempt?
texts.10.512: Thir Makers Image, answerd MICHAEL, then
texts.10.513: Forsook them, when themselves they villifi'd
texts.10.514: To serve ungovern'd appetite, and took
texts.10.515: His Image whom they serv'd, a brutish vice,
texts.10.516: Inductive mainly to the sin of EVE.
texts.10.517: Therefore so abject is thir punishment,
texts.10.518: Disfiguring not Gods likeness, but thir own,
texts.10.519: Or if his likeness, by themselves defac't
texts.10.520: While they pervert pure Natures healthful rules
texts.10.521: To loathsom sickness, worthily, since they
texts.10.522: Gods Image did not reverence in themselves.
texts.10.523: I yeild it just, said ADAM, and submit.
texts.10.524: But is there yet no other way, besides
texts.10.525: These painful passages, how we may come
texts.10.526: To Death, and mix with our connatural dust?
texts.10.527: There is, said MICHAEL, if thou well observe
texts.10.528: The rule of not too much, by temperance taught
texts.10.529: In what thou eatst and drinkst, seeking from thence
texts.10.531: Till many years over thy head return:
texts.10.532: So maist thou live, till like ripe Fruit thou drop
texts.10.533: Into thy Mothers lap, or be with ease
texts.10.534: Gatherd, not harshly pluckt, for death mature:
texts.10.535: This is old age; but then thou must outlive
texts.10.536: Thy youth, thy strength, thy beauty, which will change
texts.10.537: To witherd weak gray; thy Senses then
texts.10.538: Obtuse, all taste of pleasure must forgoe,
texts.10.539: To what thou hast, and for the Aire of youth
texts.10.540: Hopeful and cheerful, in thy blood will reigne
texts.10.541: A melancholly damp of cold and dry
texts.10.542: To waigh thy spirits down, and last consume
texts.10.543: The Balme of Life. To whom our Ancestor.
texts.10.544: Henceforth I flie not Death, nor would prolong
texts.10.545: Life much, bent rather how I may be quit
texts.10.546: Fairest and easiest of this combrous charge,
texts.10.547: Which I must keep till my appointed day
texts.10.548: Of rendring up. MICHAEL to him repli'd.
texts.10.549: Nor love thy Life, nor hate; but what thou livst
texts.10.550: Live well, how long or short permit to Heav'n:
texts.10.551: And now prepare thee for another sight.
texts.10.552: He lookd and saw a spacious Plaine, whereon
texts.10.553: Were Tents of various hue; by some were herds
texts.10.554: Of Cattel grazing: others, whence the sound
texts.10.555: Of Instruments that made melodious chime
texts.10.556: Was heard, of Harp and Organ; and who moovd
texts.10.557: Thir stops and chords was seen: his volant touch
texts.10.558: Instinct through all proportions low and high
texts.10.559: Fled and pursu'd transverse the resonant fugue.
texts.10.560: In other part stood one who at the Forge
texts.10.561: Labouring, two massie clods of Iron and Brass
texts.10.562: Had melted (whether found where casual fire
texts.10.563: Had wasted woods on Mountain or in Vale,
texts.10.564: Down to the veins of Earth, thence gliding hot
texts.10.565: To som Caves mouth, or whether washt by stream
texts.10.566: From underground) the liquid Ore he dreind
texts.10.567: Into fit moulds prepar'd; from which he formd
texts.10.568: First his own Tooles; then, what might else be wrought
texts.10.569: Fulfil or grav'n in mettle. After these,
texts.10.570: But on the hether side a different sort
texts.10.571: From the high neighbouring Hills, which was thir Seat,
texts.10.572: Down to the Plain descended: by thir guise
texts.10.573: Just men they seemd, and all thir study bent
texts.10.574: To worship God aright, and know his works
texts.10.575: Not hid, nor those things lost which might preserve
texts.10.576: Freedom and Peace to men: they on the Plain
texts.10.577: Long had not walkt, when from the Tents behold
texts.10.578: A Beavie of fair Women, richly gay
texts.10.579: In Gems and wanton dress; to the Harp they sung
texts.10.580: Soft amorous Ditties, and in dance came on:
texts.10.581: The Men though grave, ey'd them, and let thir eyes
texts.10.582: Rove without rein, till in the amorous Net
texts.10.583: Fast caught, they lik'd, and each his liking chose;
texts.10.584: And now of love they treat till th' Eevning Star
texts.10.585: Loves Harbinger appeerd; then all in heat
texts.10.586: They light the Nuptial Torch, and bid invoke
texts.10.587: Hymen, then first to marriage Rites invok't;
texts.10.588: With Feast and Musick all the Tents resound.
texts.10.589: Such happy interview and fair event
texts.10.590: Of love youth not lost, Songs, Garlands, Flours,
texts.10.591: And charming Symphonies attach'd the heart
texts.10.592: Of ADAM, soon enclin'd to admit delight,
texts.10.593: The bent of Nature; which he thus express'd.
texts.10.594: True opener of mine eyes, prime Angel blest,
texts.10.595: Much better seems this Vision, and more hope
texts.10.596: Of peaceful dayes portends, then those two past;
texts.10.597: Those were of hate and death, or pain much worse,
texts.10.598: Here Nature seems fulfilld in all her ends.
texts.10.599: To whom thus MICHAEL. Judg not what is best
texts.10.600: By pleasure, though to Nature seeming meet,
texts.10.601: Created, as thou art, to nobler end
texts.10.603: Those Tents thou sawst so pleasant, were the Tents
texts.10.604: Of wickedness, wherein shall dwell his Race
texts.10.605: Who slew his Brother; studious they appere
texts.10.606: Of Arts that polish Life, Inventers rare,
texts.10.607: Unmindful of thir Maker, though his Spirit
texts.10.608: Taught them, but they his gifts acknowledg'd none.
texts.10.609: Yet they a beauteous ofspring shall beget;
texts.10.610: For that fair femal Troop thou sawst, that seemd
texts.10.611: Of Goddesses, so blithe, so smooth, so gay,
texts.10.612: Yet empty of all good wherein consists
texts.10.613: Womans domestic honour and chief praise;
texts.10.614: Bred onely and completed to the taste
texts.10.615: Of lustful apperence, to sing, to dance,
texts.10.616: To dress, and troule the Tongue, and roule the Eye.
texts.10.617: To these that sober Race of Men, whose lives
texts.10.618: Religious titl'd them the Sons of God,
texts.10.619: Shall yeild up all thir vertue, all thir fame
texts.10.620: Ignobly, to the trains and to the smiles
texts.10.621: Of these fair Atheists, and now swim in joy,
texts.10.622: (Erelong to swim at larg) and laugh; for which
texts.10.623: The world erelong a world of tears must weepe.
texts.10.624: To whom thus ADAM of short joy bereft.
texts.10.625: O pittie and shame, that they who to live well
texts.10.626: Enterd so faire, should turn aside to tread
texts.10.627: Paths indirect, or in the mid way faint!
texts.10.628: But still I see the tenor of Mans woe
texts.10.629: Holds on the same, from Woman to begin.
texts.10.630: From Mans effeminate slackness it begins,
texts.10.631: Said th' Angel, who should better hold his place
texts.10.632: By wisdome, and superiour gifts receavd.
texts.10.633: But now prepare thee for another Scene.
texts.10.634: He lookd and saw wide Territorie spred
texts.10.635: Before him, Towns, and rural works between,
texts.10.636: Cities of Men with lofty Gates and Towrs,
texts.10.637: Concours in Arms, fierce Faces threatning Warr,
texts.10.638: Giants of mightie Bone, and bould emprise;
texts.10.639: Part wield thir Arms, part courb the foaming Steed,
texts.10.640: Single or in Array of Battel rang'd
texts.10.641: Both Horse and Foot, nor idely mustring stood;
texts.10.642: One way a Band select from forage drives
texts.10.643: A herd of Beeves, faire Oxen and faire Kine
texts.10.644: From a fat Meddow ground; or fleecy Flock,
texts.10.645: Ewes and thir bleating Lambs over the Plaine,
texts.10.646: Thir Bootie; scarce with Life the Shepherds flye,
texts.10.647: But call in aide, which tacks a bloody Fray;
texts.10.648: With cruel Tournament the Squadrons joine;
texts.10.649: Where Cattel pastur'd late, now scatterd lies
texts.10.650: With Carcasses and Arms th' ensanguind Field
texts.10.651: Deserted: Others to a Citie strong
texts.10.652: Lay Siege, encampt; by Batterie, Scale, and Mine,
texts.10.653: Assaulting; others from the Wall defend
texts.10.654: With Dart and Jav'lin, Stones and sulfurous Fire;
texts.10.655: On each hand slaughter and gigantic deeds.
texts.10.656: In other part the scepter'd Haralds call
texts.10.657: To Council in the Citie Gates: anon
texts.10.658: Grey-headed men and grave, with Warriours mixt,
texts.10.659: Assemble, and Harangues are heard, but soon
texts.10.660: In factious opposition, till at last
texts.10.661: Of middle Age one rising, eminent
texts.10.662: In wise deport, spake much of Right and Wrong,
texts.10.663: Of Justice, of Religion, Truth and Peace,
texts.10.664: And Judgement from above: him old and young
texts.10.665: Exploded, and had seiz'd with violent hands,
texts.10.666: Had not a Cloud descending snatch'd him thence
texts.10.667: Unseen amid the throng: so violence
texts.10.669: Through all the Plain, and refuge none was found.
texts.10.670: ADAM was all in tears, and to his guide
texts.10.671: Lamenting turnd full sad; O what are these,
texts.10.672: Deaths Ministers, not Men, who thus deal Death
texts.10.674: Ten thousand fould the sin of him who slew
texts.10.675: His Brother; for of whom such massacher
texts.10.676: Make they but of thir Brethren, men of men?
texts.10.677: But who was that Just Man, whom had not Heav'n
texts.10.678: Rescu'd, had in his Righteousness bin lost?
texts.10.679: To whom thus MICHAEL; These are the product
texts.10.680: Of those ill-mated Marriages thou saw'st;
texts.10.681: Where good with bad were matcht, who of themselves
texts.10.682: Abhor to joyn; and by imprudence mixt,
texts.10.683: Produce prodigious Births of bodie or mind.
texts.10.684: Such were these Giants, men of high renown;
texts.10.685: For in those dayes Might onely shall be admir'd,
texts.10.686: And Valour and Heroic Vertu call'd;
texts.10.687: To overcome in Battel, and subdue
texts.10.688: Nations, and bring home spoils with infinite
texts.10.689: Man-slaughter, shall be held the highest pitch
texts.10.690: Of human Glorie, and for Glorie done
texts.10.691: Of triumph, to be styl'd great Conquerours,
texts.10.692: Patrons of Mankind, Gods, and Sons of Gods,
texts.10.693: Destroyers rightlier call'd and Plagues of men.
texts.10.694: Thus Fame shall be achiev'd, renown on Earth,
texts.10.695: And what most merits fame in silence hid.
texts.10.696: But hee the seventh from thee, whom thou beheldst
texts.10.697: The onely righteous in a World perverse,
texts.10.698: And therefore hated, therefore so beset
texts.10.699: With Foes for daring single to be just,
texts.10.700: And utter odious Truth, that God would come
texts.10.701: To judge them with his Saints: Him the most High
texts.10.702: Rapt in a balmie Cloud with winged Steeds
texts.10.703: Did, as thou sawst, receave, to walk with God
texts.10.704: High in Salvation and the Climes of bliss,
texts.10.705: Exempt from Death; to shew thee what reward
texts.10.706: Awaits the good, the rest what punishment;
texts.10.707: Which now direct thine eyes and soon behold.
texts.10.708: He look'd, saw the face of things quite chang'd;
texts.10.709: The brazen Throat of Warr had ceast to roar,
texts.10.710: All now was turn'd to jollitie and game,
texts.10.711: To luxurie and riot, feast and dance,
texts.10.713: Rape or Adulterie, where passing faire
texts.10.714: Allurd them; thence from Cups to civil Broiles.
texts.10.715: At length a Reverend Sire among them came,
texts.10.716: And of thir doings great dislike declar'd,
texts.10.717: And testifi'd against thir wayes; hee oft
texts.10.719: Triumphs or Festivals, and to them preachd
texts.10.720: Conversion and Repentance, as to Souls
texts.10.722: But all in vain: which when he saw, he ceas'd
texts.10.723: Contending, and remov'd his Tents farr off;
texts.10.724: Then from the Mountain hewing Timber tall,
texts.10.725: Began to build a Vessel of huge bulk,
texts.10.726: Measur'd by Cubit, length, breadth, and highth,
texts.10.727: Smeard round with Pitch, and in the side a dore
texts.10.728: Contriv'd, and of provisions laid in large
texts.10.729: For Man and Beast: when loe a wonder strange!
texts.10.730: Of everie Beast, and Bird, and Insect small
texts.10.731: Came seavens, and pairs, and enterd in, as taught
texts.10.732: Thir order; last the Sire, and his three Sons
texts.10.733: With thir four Wives, and God made fast the dore.
texts.10.734: Meanwhile the Southwind rose, with black wings
texts.10.735: Wide hovering, all the Clouds together drove
texts.10.736: From under Heav'n; the Hills to their supplie
texts.10.737: Vapour, and Exhalation dusk and moist,
texts.10.738: Sent up amain; and now the thick'nd Skie
texts.10.739: Like a dark Ceeling stood; down rush'd the Rain
texts.10.740: Impetuous, and continu'd till the Earth
texts.10.741: No more was seen; the floating Vessel swum
texts.10.742: Uplifted; and secure with beaked prow
texts.10.743: Rode tilting o're the Waves, all dwellings else
texts.10.744: Flood overwhelmd, and them with all thir pomp
texts.10.745: Deep under water rould; Sea cover'd Sea,
texts.10.746: Sea without shoar; and in thir Palaces
texts.10.747: Where luxurie late reign'd, Sea-monsters whelp'd
texts.10.748: And stabl'd; of Mankind, so numerous late,
texts.10.749: All left, in one small bottom swum imbark't.
texts.10.750: How didst thou grieve then, ADAM, to behold
texts.10.751: The end of all thy Ofspring, end so sad,
texts.10.753: Of tears and sorrow a Floud thee also drown'd,
texts.10.754: And sunk thee as thy Sons; till gently reard
texts.10.755: By th' Angel, on thy feet thou stoodst at last,
texts.10.756: Though comfortless, as when a Father mourns
texts.10.757: His Childern, all in view destroyd at once;
texts.10.758: And scarce to th' Angel utterdst thus thy plaint.
texts.10.759: O Visions ill foreseen! better had I
texts.10.760: Liv'd ignorant of future, so had borne
texts.10.761: My part of evil onely, each dayes lot
texts.10.762: Anough to bear; those now, that were dispenst
texts.10.763: The burd'n of many Ages, on me light
texts.10.764: At once, by my foreknowledge gaining Birth
texts.10.765: Abortive, to torment me ere thir being,
texts.10.766: With thought that they must be. Let no man seek
texts.10.767: Henceforth to be foretold what shall befall
texts.10.768: Him or his Childern, evil he may be sure,
texts.10.769: Which neither his foreknowing can prevent,
texts.10.770: And hee the future evil shall no less
texts.10.771: In apprehension then in substance feel
texts.10.772: Grievous to bear: but that care now is past,
texts.10.773: Man is not whom to warne: those few escap't
texts.10.774: Famin and anguish will at last consume
texts.10.775: Wandring that watrie Desert: I had hope
texts.10.776: When violence was ceas't, and Warr on Earth,
texts.10.777: All would have then gon well, peace would have crownd
texts.10.778: With length of happy days the race of man;
texts.10.779: But I was farr deceav'd; for now I see
texts.10.780: Peace to corrupt no less then Warr to waste.
texts.10.781: How comes it thus? unfould, Celestial Guide,
texts.10.782: And whether here the Race of man will end.
texts.10.783: To whom thus MICHAEL. Those whom last thou sawst
texts.10.784: In triumph and luxurious wealth, are they
